label: HB 10874
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FREE ANNUAL MEDICAL CHECK-UP FOR ALL FILIPINOS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Annual health examinations are important for the early detection and management of silent medical conditions. However, data shows 40% of Filipinos undergo annual medical checkups.1 Among the primary reasons behind this low rate are the high cost attributed to consultation and diagnostic tests, and prioritization of basic needs over healthcare concerns. We must shift our perspective from a reactive mindset, that is “If it is not broken, don’t fix it”, to a preventive and proactive health care. By prioritizing early intervention, we optimize the window of opportunity to treat and manage diseases before symptoms manifest, which will result to saving more lives at a much lower healthcare costs. Under Article XIII of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the State is mandated to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development. While we took a big step towards this mandate with the enactment of Republic Act No. 11223 or the Universal Health Care Act in 2018, there should be a continuous efforts to expand and enhance the range of healthcare services being offered to the Filipino people. 1 "New Study Reveals Only 40% of Filipinos Get Yearly Checkups, an issue that can be addressed by UHC law – Atty. Conti," Capstone-Intel, September 4, 2023, https://www.capstone-intel.com/new-study-reveals-only-40- of-filipinos-get-yearly-checkups-an-issue-that-can-be-addressed-by-uhc-law-atty-conti/. As such, this measures seeks to provide all Filipinos access to free annual health examinations, aside from the benefits granted under the Universal Health Care Act. The annual health examination shall includes consultation, physical examination, routine laboratory or diagnostic examinations, complete blood count (CBC), lipid profile, fasting blood sugar (FBS), chest x-ray, among others. The saying “health is wealth” applies not only to individual but to the nation as a whole. Maintaining a healthy population is a good foundation of a robust economy, efficient and effective workforce, and high national productivity. The expansion and strengthening of our healthcare services is an essential investment in our human capital. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 10875
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE INSTALLATION OF BEHIND-THE-METER ELECTRICITY GENERATION AND ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ELECTRIC POWER INDUSTRY REFORM ACT OF 2001”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE With the instability and uncertainties surrounding the electricity generation in the country, Filipinos are increasingly turning to renewable energy sources such as solar power. The Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities (ICSC) reported a surge on rooftop solar adoption in the Philippines, with roughly 600 megawatts (MW) added in the last 12 months leading to April 2026, amid rising power costs and the high cost of living. Behind-the-meter (BTM) energy storage, such as rooftop solar panels and storage systems, offers significant benefits to consumers and the power grid alike. By generating clean, fuel-free energy directly at the point of use, these systems immediately protect households from volatile retail power rates, provide critical back-up electricity during recurring grid blackouts, and reduce overall peak demand on distribution grid. However, everyday Filipino consumers face severe hurdles in adopting these solutions. Case in point: the installation of BTM systems continues being hindered by technology costs, administrative red tape, excessive local government unit (LGU) permit and clearance requirements, among other obstacles. As such, this measure seeks to simplify the regulatory requirements for the installation of behind-the-meter electricity generation and battery storage systems, intended solely for personal use. Through the removal of the existing administrative restrictions, this bill aims to promote public access to these technologies for electricity generation, and to making clean power simple, easy and affordable for Filipinos Households. Through this, the mainstreaming of renewable energy across the country will be accelerated. This measure will expand Filipinos access to alternative renewable energy and directly alleviate the concerns over the rising electricity expenses. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. CHEENO MIGUEL D. title: AN ACT GRANTING LIFETIME VALIDITY OF IDENTIFICATION CARDS FOR PERSONS WITH PERMANENT DISABILITY AND RATIONALIZING THE VALIDITY PERIOD FOR TEMPORARY DISABILITY IDENTIFICATION CARDS, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MAGNA CARTA FOR DISABLED PERSONS”, AS AMENDED 26 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 22 The dignity of persons with disabilities should include the right to be recognized without having to repeatedly prove their condition. In other words, a permanent disability does not become temporary simply because an identification card has an expiration date. 26 This proposed measure therefore seeks to grant lifetime validity to PWD identification cards issued to persons with permanent disabilities. This proposal recognizes that once the permanence of a disability has been properly established, repeated renewal only adds a burden to our brothers and sisters with disabilities. 31 Likewise, this proposed measure also distinguishes between permanent and temporary disabilities to ensure that PWD benefits remain available to those who qualify, while preventing abuse of PWD privileges. 35 Ultimately, this bill seeks to make the recognition of disability simpler, more accessible, and more humane. Behind every PWD identification card is a person who may already face challenges that require physical, mental, and emotional strength every day. It is now the responsibility of the State to ensure that its laws and systems do not add to these burdens but instead provide an effective support to our brothers and sisters with disabilities. 42 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 44 45 46 REP. label: HB 10882
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE JUSTICE, PROTECTION, AND SUPPORT SYSTEM FOR VICTIMS AND SURVIVORS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN, PROVIDING FOR EXPEDITED PROTECTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE MECHANISMS, INTEGRATED SURVIVOR SERVICES, CHILD-SENSITIVE AND TECHNOLOGY-RESPONSIVE PROCEDURES, INTER-AGENCY COORDINATION, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Violence against women and their children remains a serious concern that requires not only strong laws, but also an effective, accessible, and coordinated justice and protection system. The Philippines has enacted significant legislation addressing violence against women and children which provide important legal remedies and protections. However, the existence of legal remedies does not by itself guarantee meaningful access to justice. Victims and survivors may still encounter delays in obtaining protection, difficulty navigating multiple government agencies, inadequate access to legal and psychosocial services, geographic barriers, lack of specialized personnel, repeated interviews and disclosures, insufficient coordination among service providers, and limited access to assistance outside regular government operating 1 hours. These difficulties can be particularly severe for women and children in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, persons with disabilities, persons with limited financial resources, and victims who lack access to reliable transportation, technology, or legal assistance. The urgency of strengthening the justice and protection system is heightened by the changing nature of violence. Abuse may now extend beyond physical spaces into digital environments through online harassment, cyberstalking, threats, unauthorized dissemination of intimate material, technology-assisted coercion, and other forms of technology-facilitated violence. Children are likewise increasingly exposed to online sexual abuse and exploitation, requiring close coordination between traditional child-protection mechanisms and digital investigation and response systems. The proposed measure therefore seeks to strengthen the implementation of existing laws without diminishing or duplicating their substantive protections. Rather than creating an entirely separate judicial system, the bill strengthens the existing Family Court and VAWC framework by allowing the Supreme Court, consistent with its constitutional authority, to establish specialized dockets, calendars, or other appropriate mechanisms for the expeditious handling of VAWC- related proceedings. The bill further establishes mechanisms for expedited protection-order processing and emergency response. In situations involving imminent or continuing danger, victims and survivors should not be required to navigate multiple agencies independently before receiving appropriate assistance. The proposed emergency response mechanism seeks to facilitate coordinated law-enforcement intervention, protection-order assistance, emergency medical and psychosocial services, shelter, transportation, and legal assistance. The measure also establishes integrated Survivor Support Desks and Survivor Support Coordinators to help victims and survivors navigate available legal, medical, psychological, social welfare, shelter, and other government services. This approach seeks to reduce unnecessary duplication, prevent victims from repeatedly recounting traumatic experiences, and improve continuity of assistance from the initial report through the resolution of the case. Every victim and survivor should be able to seek protection without having to overcome unnecessary institutional barriers. Through this measure, the State affirms that protection from violence is not merely a statutory promise but a responsibility 2 that must be supported by functioning institutions, trained personnel, accessible services, accountable agencies, and sustained public investment. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10883
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM, PROVIDING ACCESS TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN, INTEGRATING MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH INTO PUBLIC HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Pregnancy and the postpartum period are significant stages in a woman’s life that involve profound physical, emotional, psychological, and social changes. While motherhood is often associated with joy and fulfillment, many women experience mental health challenges during this period, including depression, anxiety disorders, trauma-related conditions, and other mental health concerns. If left undetected and untreated, these conditions may adversely affect the health, safety, and quality of life of mothers, their children, and their families. Maternal mental health conditions remain an underrecognized public health concern due to various barriers, including stigma, lack of awareness, limited access to mental health professionals, inadequate screening and referral systems, and financial constraints. Many women experiencing symptoms do not seek care because they fear judgment, discrimination, or misunderstanding of their condition. As a result, opportunities for early detection, intervention, and recovery are often missed. 1 Thus, this bill seeks to establish a National Maternal Mental Health Program that integrates maternal mental health services into existing maternal, newborn, child, and primary healthcare systems. It provides for routine and evidence-based screening during pregnancy and the postpartum period, standardized referral pathways, community-based support services, emergency intervention mechanisms, and continuity of care for women requiring further assessment and treatment. Further, the measure strengthens the capacity of healthcare providers and frontline workers through competency-based training and continuing education on maternal mental health detection, intervention, referral, and stigma-sensitive care. It promotes workplace and educational support systems, community awareness programs, and the responsible use of tele-mental health services to expand access, particularly in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas. By recognizing maternal mental health as an essential component of women’s health, family well-being, and public health, this bill seeks to build a healthcare system that supports mothers not only in surviving pregnancy and childbirth but also in achieving mental, emotional, and social well-being throughout the postpartum period. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10884
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING MOBILE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CLINICS FOR UNDERSERVED AND GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED COMMUNITIES, PROVIDING ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL WOMEN’S HEALTH SERVICES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the right to health of every Filipino and directs the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development that shall make essential goods, health services, and other social services available to all. Despite existing efforts to improve healthcare delivery, many women, particularly those living in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs), rural communities, island barangays, Indigenous Peoples' communities, and disaster- or conflict-affected areas, continue to experience barriers in accessing timely, affordable, and quality reproductive, maternal, and preventive healthcare services. Limited healthcare facilities, geographic distance, inadequate transportation, socioeconomic challenges, and shortages in health personnel often delay access to essential services and contribute to preventable maternal and reproductive health complications. These challenges highlight the need for innovative and community- 1 based healthcare delivery mechanisms that can bring critical services closer to women and families who need them most. Thus, this bill seeks to establish the Mobile Reproductive Health Clinic Program under the Department of Health (DOH) to provide accessible, equitable, and quality reproductive, maternal, preventive, and women's healthcare services through mobile healthcare units deployed to underserved and hard-to-reach communities. By bringing healthcare services directly to communities, the measure aims to reduce disparities in health access, promote early detection and prevention of reproductive and maternal health conditions, and strengthen continuity of care through coordinated referrals with Rural Health Units, hospitals, and other appropriate healthcare facilities. The proposed Mobile Reproductive Health Clinics shall provide essential services such as prenatal and postnatal care, maternal health monitoring, reproductive health counseling and education, family planning information consistent with existing laws, breast and cervical health screening, nutrition counseling, preventive health services, mental health support, and referral assistance. Through this measure, the State shall strengthen primary healthcare delivery and improve access to essential women's health services. This represents a proactive investment in equitable healthcare delivery and advances the State’s commitment to ensuring that no woman is deprived of necessary health services because of geographic, economic, or social barriers. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10885
title: AN ACT MANDATING A SMOKE-FREE AND VAPE-FREE ENVIRONMENT IN ALL PUBLIC AND WORKPLACES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9211 AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11900, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State has a constitutional duty to protect and promote the people’s right to health and to instill health consciousness among them. Consistent with this mandate, as well as with the country’s obligations under the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, there is a need to strengthen the legal framework for creating genuinely smoke-free and vape-free public spaces and workplaces. The proposed “Smoke-Free and Vape-Free Environment Act” seeks to establish a clear and comprehensive national policy prohibiting smoking and vaping in public places, public conveyances, and workplaces, while strengthening the protection afforded to children, workers, commuters, students, patients, and the general public from exposure to tobacco smoke and vape emissions. It expands and clarifies the definitions of public places, public conveyances, smoking, vaping, workplaces, and other relevant terms to reflect the realities of modern transportation, 1 employment, commerce, education, and public life. The measure likewise recognizes that protection from exposure must extend beyond enclosed establishments to appropriate outdoor areas where people commonly gather, particularly schools, playgrounds, health facilities, transportation terminals, markets, parks, walkways, and other places frequented by the public. At the same time, the measure provides a carefully regulated framework for designated smoking and vaping areas in places where such areas may legally be established. Protection of public health remains the governing principle while providing clear and enforceable standards for establishments that choose to maintain designated areas. Further, this bill requires provinces, cities, and municipalities to establish Smoke-Free and Vape-Free Task Forces that will coordinate enforcement, monitoring, education, and community-level implementation. Ultimately, this bill seeks to move beyond a limited regulation of smoking and vaping toward the establishment of a comprehensive smoke-free and vape-free environment in which the right to breathe clean and healthy air is protected in places where people live, work, study, travel, and gather. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10886
title: AN ACT GRANTING A ONE-TIME GENERAL TAX AMNESTY ON INTEREST, SURCHARGES, COMPROMISE PENALTIES, AND OTHER ADDITIONS TO THE TAX WITH RESPECT TO UNPAID OR UNDERPAID NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES FOR TAXABLE YEAR 2025 AND PRIOR YEARS, UPON PAYMENT OF THE BASIC TAX DUE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Tax compliance is essential to the delivery of public services. Unpaid tax liabilities, however, may become increasingly difficult to settle as interest, surcharges, and penalties accumulate over time. What may once have been a manageable obligation can eventually become difficult to settle. When that happens, the Government is left with a liability on paper, while the taxpayer remains outside full compliance. This legislative proposal provides a practical way forward by granting a one-time amnesty on interest, surcharges, compromise penalties, and other additions to unpaid or underpaid national internal revenue taxes for taxable year 2025 and prior years. In return, the taxpayer must pay one hundred percent (100%) of the basic tax lawfully due. This measure provides citizens and businesses a clear opportunity to settle past obligations without the accumulated burden of penalties and interest. It covers unassessed liabilities, pending assessments, and final and executory liabilities. It also provides reasonable installment arrangements for individuals and smaller taxpayers, while preserving validation and safeguards against fraudulent availment. For the Government, the measure can convert outstanding liabilities into actual collections while bringing taxpayers back into the formal tax system. This is particularly significant given the central role of tax revenues in funding public services. In 2024, the Bureau of Internal Revenue collected ₱2.852 trillion, underscoring the central role of tax revenues in financing government operations and public services.1 A tax amnesty should not diminish the value of voluntary compliance. Neither should accumulated penalties become a permanent barrier to payment. By requiring full and final settlement of the basic tax while providing a reasonable path back to compliance, this measure is able to strike a balance between granting meaningful relief to taxpayers and preserving the fiscal interests of the Government to fund essential public services. 1 Recto to BIR: Do not waver in pursuit of funding the growing nations’ needs, Department of Finance, 1 August 2025, available at https://www.dof.gov.ph/recto-to-bir-do-not-waver-in-pursuit-of-funding-the-growing-nations-needs/ This way, taxpayers are given a fresh opportunity to settle, and the Government collects revenue that might otherwise remain unpaid. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 10887
title: AN ACT PROTECTING BORROWERS FROM UNFAIR, DECEPTIVE, ABUSIVE, AND PREDATORY ONLINE LENDING PRACTICES, ESTABLISHING MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR ONLINE LENDING AND DIGITAL DEBT COLLECTION, STRENGTHENING ENFORCEMENT AGAINST UNAUTHORIZED ONLINE LENDING PLATFORMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE A loan application can now be completed in minutes. Unfortunately, so can the harassment that follows it. Online lending has made credit faster and more accessible to Filipinos who may otherwise have difficulty obtaining funds through traditional channels. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ 2025 Consumer Finance and Inclusion Survey found that one in four Filipino adults had outstanding loans and noted the growing reach of online lending platforms. The same survey found that speed of loan processing and approval is among the foremost considerations of borrowers. Speed and convenience clearly matter to borrowers, but convenience should not come at the cost of fairness, privacy, or dignity. In March 2026, the Department of Information and Communications Technology, National Privacy Commission, and Securities and Exchange Commission jointly warned of reports involving online lending platforms engaged in harassment, intimidation, public shaming, and unlawful use of personal data.1 The advisory reiterated prohibitions against unnecessary access to borrowers’ contact lists, contacting persons other than lawful guarantors for debt collection, and using personal data for threatening or unfair collection practices. Technology has changed not only how quickly people may borrow, but also how much information a lender may attempt to obtain and how easily pressure may be exerted on a borrower. A delinquent loan should not turn a borrower’s contact list into a collection directory, a family group chat into a public notice board, or a mobile phone into an instrument of humiliation. A debt is an obligation to pay; it is not a surrender of dignity, privacy, or basic rights. This bill establishes durable minimum protections for online borrowers without attempting to legislate every technical detail of a rapidly evolving industry. It requires clear disclosure and affirmative acceptance of loan terms; promotes responsible lending; Joint Public Advisory on Online Lending Platforms (OLPs) issued on 18 March 2026 prohibits undisclosed, excessive, fictitious, and circumvention-based charges; protects borrowers against unnecessary and disproportionate access to personal data; and prohibits harassment, public shaming, false threats, deceptive collection, and demands for payment from persons who never assumed the debt. This measure likewise ensures that lenders cannot avoid accountability by outsourcing collection or other functions, and extends the core prohibitions to unauthorized online lenders. Online lending has made borrowing possible with a few taps on a screen. Our laws must ensure that those few taps do not open the door to hidden charges, harassment, or misuse of a person’s private life. Credit may be digital, but the rights on the other side of the screen remain decidedly human. In view of the foregoing, the immediate enactment of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 10888
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A UNIFIED CRIMINAL RECORDS CLEARANCE SYSTEM, HARMONIZING THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION CLEARANCE AND THE NATIONAL POLICE CLEARANCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Government should not require citizens to prove twice what it can securely verify once. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Clearance and the National Police Clearance remain separate processes despite their overlapping purpose of checking an applicant against government-held criminal records. For citizens who would otherwise be required to secure both clearances, this means separate applications, fees, travel, waiting time, and administrative requirements. These burdens weigh particularly heavily on jobseekers, workers, and applicants who must travel to clearance centers or take time away from work. A single clearance can reduce these costs and transactions while preserving the integrity of criminal records verification. This bill therefore establishes a Unified Criminal Records Clearance System under which a single clearance may satisfy requirements for both an NBI Clearance and a National Police Clearance. Rather than creating another central repository, the measure relies on secure interoperability: the NBI and the Philippine National Police (PNP) retain custody and responsibility for their respective records while the System verifies the information necessary to issue one clearance. The reform also benefits government. Interoperability can reduce duplicative processing, make better use of existing systems and personnel, improve coordination between the NBI and the PNP, and allow government resources to be directed toward verification, records accuracy, and service delivery rather than repetitive transactions. This approach is consistent with the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018, which promotes interconnectivity among government agencies, and the E-Governance Act, which advances interoperable government systems and integrated frontline services. This measure does not diminish legitimate law-enforcement functions, background investigations, or specialized clearances required by law. It simply replaces unnecessary duplication with a more efficient and coordinated government process. For citizens, this means fewer transactions, lower costs, less travel and waiting time, and less red tape. For government, it means greater efficiency, better coordination, and more effective use of public resources. Where government can securely verify the necessary records once, citizens should need only one clearance. In view of the foregoing, the passage of the Unified Criminal Records Clearance Act is earnestly sought. label: HB 10889
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AN INTEGRATED SERVICE NETWORK FOR GOVERNMENT TRANSACTIONS RELATED TO EMPLOYMENT, STREAMLINING ACCESS THERETO FOR JOBSEEKERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Finding a job requires persistence, preparation, and patience. It should not, however, require a tour of government offices. Before employment begins, a jobseeker may need to secure clearances, registrations, certifications, and other government documents from different agencies. When these transactions require separate systems, repeated submissions, multiple appointments, and unnecessary travel, routine compliance can become another barrier to work. This matters especially for young workers entering the labor market. In June 2026, the Philippine Statistics Authority reported a youth employment rate of 86.5 percent, while around 743,000 employed youth were underemployed.1 Congress already reduced one barrier through Republic Act No. 11261 (First Time Jobseekers Assistance Act), which waives covered government fees for qualified first-time jobseekers and directs Public Employment Service Offices to assist them in securing pre- employment documents. But cost is only one part of the problem, and first-time jobseekers are only one part of the workforce. The need for simpler government transactions also arises when workers change jobs, reenter the workforce, seek employment after displacement, or otherwise pursue new employment opportunities. The proposed Streamlined Transactions for Employment Processing (STEP) Act addresses this broader administrative challenge. It establishes the STEP Service Network, an integrated service framework using existing digital government platforms, Public Employment Service Offices, participating agencies, and assisted-access points, to make employment-related government transactions easier to access and complete. The measure builds on Republic Act No. 12254 (E-Governance Act), which 1Number of Employed Persons Increased to 50.66 Million as Labor Force Participation Rose in June 2026, PHILIPPINE STATISTICS AUTHORITY, 6 August 2026, available at https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/labor-force-survey mandates interoperable, citizen-centered government services and integration of frontline transactions involving agencies such as the Philippine Statistics Authority, National Bureau of Investigation, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Social Security System, Pag-IBIG Fund, and Philippine Health Insurance Corporation. It seeks to provide jobseekers with a common point of access to participating services; facilitate electronic applications, appointments, payments, and transaction tracking where legally and technically feasible; provide assisted access through PESOs; and reduce unnecessary repetitive submissions through secure government-to- government verification. A citizen who is ready to work has already taken an important step toward contributing to the economy. Government should help make the next step simpler, faster, and more economical. The passage of the STEP Act is therefore respectfully urged for the jobseeker who is taking their initial step into employment, pursuing a better opportunity, rebuilding after displacement, or simply trying to earn a living without first having to navigate a maze of government transactions. label: HB 10890
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL URBAN AND PERI-URBAN AGRICULTURE PROGRAM, PROMOTING VERTICAL FARMING AND OTHER SPACE-EFFICIENT AND CLIMATE-RESILIENT FOOD PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Food does not become less necessary when concrete replaces soil. But as communities urbanize, the places where people live and the places where much of their food is produced grow farther apart. That distance makes cities increasingly dependent on transport, logistics, functioning markets, and uninterrupted supply chains for something no household can postpone buying. In 2024, 62.22 million Filipinos, or 55.2% of the population, lived in urban barangays, up from 58.93 million in 2020.1 At the same time, food remains beyond the comfortable reach of many households with 4.84 million Filipinos lived below the food threshold in 2023,2 meaning their incomes were insufficient to meet even their basic food needs. Urbanization changes the geography of food security. It does not diminish the importance of rural agriculture, but it makes the resilience of urban food systems increasingly important. Urban and peri-urban agriculture can be a part of that resilience. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) recognizes its potential to improve access to fresh food, support livelihoods, and strengthen food security and nutrition, particularly when integrated into broader urban and territorial planning.3 Fortunately, we are not starting from an empty garden bed. The Department of Agriculture (DA), through Administrative Order No. 03, Series of 2022, established the National Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture Program (NUPAP) to promote food production in urban and peri-urban areas, improve access to nutritious food, reduce food miles and logistics costs, and create livelihood opportunities. 1 Highlights on the Urban Population Based on the 2024 Census of Population (2024 POPCEN), PHILIPPINE STATISTICS AUTHORITY, 6 July 2026, available at https://psa.gov.ph/content/highlights-urban-population-based-2024-census-population-2024-popcen 2 Percentage of Filipino Families Classified as Poor Declined to 10.9 Percent in 2023, PHILIPPINE STATISTICS AUTHORITY, 22 July 2024, available at https://psa.gov.ph/content/percentage-filipino-families-classified-poor-declined-109-percent-2023 3 Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture, FOOD AND AGRICULTURE ORGANIZATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS, available at https://www.fao.org/urban-peri- urban-agriculture/en This bill institutionalizes and strengthens that existing program instead of planting another bureaucracy beside it. It supports household and community gardens, rooftop and container gardening, hydroponics, aquaponics, vertical farming, controlled- environment agriculture, and other appropriate production systems. It likewise integrates food safety, site suitability, environmental protection, structural safety, and responsible resource use into the national framework. As our towns and cities continue to build upward and outward, their capacity to nourish the people who live in them should not be left behind. Progress may change the landscape, but it should never put the most basic necessities farther out of reach. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is respectfully urged to ensure that, where food can be grown safely, sensibly, and sustainably, government can help make room for it. label: HB 10891
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROFESSIONAL REGULATION COMMISSION OFFSITE SERVICE CENTER IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF GUIGUINTO, PROVINCE OF BULACAN, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to government services is an important part of effective professional regulation. For professionals and examinees, timely and convenient access to licensing, registration, certification, and related services can help reduce unnecessary travel, costs, and inconvenience. Bulacan has a population of 3,876,806, making it the most populous province in Central Luzon based on the 2024 Census of Population. At present, the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) does not have an offsite service center in Bulacan, requiring many Bulakenyos who need in-person services to travel outside the province. This bill seeks to establish a PRC Offsite Service Center in the Municipality of Guiguinto, Bulacan to serve professionals, examinees, and other clients throughout the province and nearby areas. By bringing PRC services closer to the public, the measure will help reduce travel costs and transaction time for citizens, ease demand on existing PRC facilities, and promote more accessible and efficient government service delivery. For a province of Bulacan’s population and continuing growth, a PRC service presence within the province is practical and timely. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. By bringing PRC services closer to the public, the measure will help reduce travel costs and transaction time for citizens, ease demand on existing PRC facilities, and promote more accessible and efficient government service delivery. For a province of Bulacan’s population and continuing growth, a PRC service presence within the province is practical and timely. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. AGATHA “AG

label: HB 10897
title: AN ACT ORDAINING THE PROMOTION OF SOCIAL ENTERPRISES TO ALLEVIATE POVERTY, ESTABLISHING FOR THE PURPOSE THE POVERTY REDUCTION THROUGH SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP (PRESENT) PROGRAM AND PROVIDING SUPPORT, BENEFITS, AND APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine economy remains one of Southeast Asia's strongest growth drivers, supported by a large domestic market, a young workforce, and a vibrant entrepreneurial sector. However, recent data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) show that while the economy grew by 2.8% in the first quarter of 2026, investments declined by 3.3%, underscoring the need for a measured approach that promotes sustainable, productive, and inclusive growth. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), which comprise 99.5% of all business establishments and employ about 63% of the country's workforce, remain the backbone of the Philippine economy. Yet many continue to face barriers to finance, innovation, technology, and market access, limiting their capacity to generate greater economic value and lift more Filipinos out of poverty. This bill recognizes that social enterprises offer a practical solution by combining commercial viability with social impact. Through the establishment of the Poverty Reduction through Social Entrepreneurship (PRESENT) Program, the measure strengthens the ecosystem for social enterprises by providing capability-building, financing, market access, research and development, procurement preferences, and institutional support to enterprises that empower marginalized communities as workers, suppliers, partners, and owners. We implore the support of Congress to advance this piece of legislation in pursuit of the best interest of Philippine small businesses, the backbone of our national economy and the main driver of our economic growth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 10898
title: AN ACT FURTHER PROMOTING ENTREPRENEURSHIP BY STRENGTHENING, EMPOWERING, AND ENHANCING THE FINANCING AND OTHER SUPPORT PROGRAMS FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6977, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MAGNA CARTA FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (MSMEs)”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of the Philippine economy. As of 2023, MSMEs account for 99.59% of all business establishments in the country and generate the majority of private sector employment. In CALABARZON, one of the nation's principal economic engines, there are 189,662 MSMEs, representing 99.57% of all establishments in the region and providing employment to nearly 956,000 workers. Batangas, as one of the region's leading industrial and commercial provinces, owes much of its economic dynamism to thousands of entrepreneurs engaged in manufacturing, agribusiness, logistics, tourism, retail, and services. Yet the very enterprises that drive economic growth remain among the most vulnerable to economic disruptions. Unlike large corporations with greater capital reserves and market power, MSMEs are disproportionately affected by inflation, volatile fuel prices, supply chain disruptions, rising logistics costs, fluctuating interest rates, and other price shocks. A sudden increase in the cost of electricity, transportation, imported inputs, or financing can rapidly erode already thin profit margins, constrain expansion, or even force business closures. Compounding this challenge is the fact that the statutory thresholds defining micro, small, and medium enterprises under Republic Act No. 6977, as amended, have remained largely disconnected from changing economic realities. Inflation and sustained increases in the cost of doing business have significantly reduced the real value of these asset thresholds. Consequently, many enterprises are prematurely reclassified despite having no corresponding increase in their actual productive capacity or financial strength, thereby losing access to programs specifically intended to help them grow. This measure recognizes that a rapidly growing economy requires equally responsive institutions. It strengthens the Magna Carta for MSMEs by ensuring that enterprise classifications are periodically reviewed to reflect prevailing economic conditions; expanding access to financing through strengthened credit support and innovative lending mechanisms; simplifying regulatory compliance; reducing the cost of doing business; improving market access through government procurement and commercial opportunities; promoting digitalization and financial inclusion; strengthening local MSME development councils; and enhancing the institutional capacity of the MSMED Council and the Small Business Corporation to respond more effectively to the evolving needs of Filipino entrepreneurs. This bill seeks to build enterprises that are not only competitive during periods of economic expansion but also resilient in the face of inflation, market volatility, natural disasters, and other external shocks. We implore Congress to consider this measure to create an enabling environment where local entrepreneurship can flourish, innovation can thrive, and economic opportunities can spread and reach all communities across the country. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 10899
title: AN ACT PROMOTING ENTREPRENEURSHIP BY ESTABLISHING A SUSTAINABLE FINANCING PROGRAM FOR MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES THROUGH THE PONDO SA PAGBABAGO AT PAG-ASENSO PROGRAM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the foundation of the Philippine economy. As of 2023, they comprise 99.59% of all business establishments nationwide and account for a majority of private sector employment. In CALABARZON, one of the country's foremost economic regions, there are 189,662 MSMEs, representing 99.57% of all establishments and employing nearly 956,000 Filipinos. Batangas, as a leading industrial, logistics, manufacturing, tourism, and agricultural hub, exemplifies how entrepreneurship fuels local development, generates jobs, and sustains household incomes. Despite their indispensable role, micro and small enterprises (MSEs) continue to face persistent barriers to growth, foremost of which is limited access to affordable credit. Many entrepreneurs remain unable to obtain financing from formal financial institutions due to inadequate collateral, limited credit histories, or burdensome documentary requirements. As a result, countless small businesses are forced to rely on informal lenders charging exorbitant interest rates, commonly known as the "5-6" lending system, trapping entrepreneurs in cycles of debt and preventing them from expanding their enterprises. This financing gap has become even more pronounced amid a rapidly changing economic environment. While the Philippine economy continues to post steady growth, MSEs remain highly vulnerable to inflation, rising fuel and electricity costs, supply chain disruptions, higher transportation expenses, and elevated borrowing costs. These price shocks disproportionately affect small businesses, whose limited capital leaves little room to absorb increases in operating expenses. Access to timely, affordable working capital often determines whether an enterprise survives periods of economic uncertainty or is forced to close its doors. Recognizing these realities, the proposed Pondo sa Pagbabago at Pag-asenso (P3) Act institutionalizes a sustainable financing mechanism dedicated to micro and small enterprises. The measure transforms the existing P3 Program into a permanent statutory financing facility, ensuring its continuity beyond administrative issuances and annual budget priorities. It establishes a revolving P3 Fund to provide collateral-free loans at affordable interest rates through the Small Business Corporation and accredited partner financial institutions, thereby expanding access to formal credit while reducing dependence on predatory lending practices. Affordable financing is not merely a source of capital, it is an investment in enterprise resilience, employment generation, and inclusive economic growth. Strengthening access to credit empowers entrepreneurs to purchase inventory, modernize equipment, adopt new technologies, expand production, and withstand temporary economic shocks. Every successful microenterprise strengthens local supply chains, creates jobs, stimulates domestic demand, and contributes to poverty reduction. This measure reinforces the State's commitment to empowering Filipino entrepreneurs, promoting financial inclusion, and building a more resilient and inclusive economy where the smallest enterprises are given the opportunity not only to survive, but to grow and prosper. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 10901
title: AN ACT ENSURING THE EFFECTIVE EXERCISE OF THE RIGHT TO VOTE AND TO BE ELECTED TO PUBLIC OFFICE OF MEMBERS OF VULNERABLE SECTORS, INSTITUTIONALIZING THE VULNERABLE SECTORS OFFICE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Commission on Elections (COMELEC) implements measures for vulnerable sectors, including persons with disabilities, senior citizens, indigenous peoples, persons deprived of liberty, women, and youth, during voter registration and election-day voting processes. These measures include satellite voter registration sites, early voting hours, special voting centers and polling places. The effective exercise of the right to vote and to be elected to public office; requires a holistic and systematic approach. This approach demands supplementary evaluation of identified vulnerable sectors and consequent barriers in all electoral processes and procedures. A more comprehensive set of affirmative measures and reasonable accommodations is likewise envisioned following this approach. The institutionalization of a permanent Vulnerable Sectors Office is intended to complement the shift in approach, and support the sustained and proactive engagement of the Commission with the vulnerable sectors and their members. Therefore, this proposed measure aims to reinforce the inclusion of vulnerable sectors in the Philippine electoral process; enhance the accessibility of the process; and increase its integrity. The establishment of a Vulnerable Sectors Office within the Commission will enable it to systematically consider the concerns of vulnerable sectors when designing and implementing processes related to voter registration, voting, voter education, and participation in public office. Furthermore, it provides a continuous channel for the Commission to examine current practices and suggest additional legislative or regulatory measures where there is evidence that present legislation and/or regulations fail to sufficiently mitigate identified barriers. The proposed office does not aim to substitute existing measures, but instead to support and build upon them. As long as the Commission maintains up-to-date knowledge of the barriers experienced by vulnerable sectors; conducts accessibility assessments; coordinates with government agencies and NGOs; and develops reasonable accommodations, the Commission will shift from addressing measures for each individual election to adopting a more comprehensive and systematic approach toward making electoral processes accessible. An institutionally based approach is consistent with the idea that both the right to vote and the right to be elected must be implemented in practice, and not simply recognized in law. The Commission on Elections has also taken steps to meet the accessibility requirements of vulnerable-sector voters. On June 25, 2026, COMELEC issued Resolution No. 11238 regarding vulnerable-sector voters in relation to the 2026 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections1. The fact that COMELEC issued a specific resolution in 2026 demonstrates that there continues to be an operational need to identify and address the unique circumstances of vulnerable voters. Therefore, a permanent Vulnerable Sectors Office would establish a structural mechanism through which such measures could be continuously developed, coordinated, monitored, and enhanced. Additionally, the 2025 election results demonstrate the large-scale participation of voters across different age groups. Voter registration and voting statistics by age bracket provided by COMELEC indicate that vulnerable and potentially underserved populations comprise a considerable portion of the electorate. Thus, ensuring that these voters are able to fully participate in the electoral process is not simply a matter of providing individual accommodations, but is also important in protecting equitable and meaningful participation in the electoral process. The continuing need for such measures is evident in recent electoral data. In the 2025 National and Local Elections, the COMELEC reported 69,673,653 registered voters, 57,350,968 of whom cast ballots, representing a total voter turnout of 82.20%2.This high level of participation underscores the importance of ensuring that electoral processes are accessible to all voters, particularly those who experience physical, informational, transportation, or procedural barriers. label: HB 10908
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6982, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "SOCIAL AMELIORATION PROGRAM IN THE SUGAR INDUSTRY ACT," TO EXPAND THE IMPOSITION OF THE SOCIAL AMELIORATION LIEN TO IMPORTED SUGAR, UPDATE THE LIEN RATE, PROVIDE FOR PERIODIC ADJUSTMENTS, MODERNIZE COLLECTION AND REMITTANCE MECHANISMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 6982 was enacted in 1991 to establish the Social Amelioration Program (SAP) for workers in the sugar industry. The law provides that a lien is imposed on domestically produced sugar, the proceeds of which are used to provide cash bonuses and fund socioeconomic programs for sugar workers. More than thirty-five (35) years since its enactment, however, certain provisions of the law no longer reflect the present conditions of the sugar industry. The Five Peso (Php 5.00) per picul lien, or its equivalent in LKG, has remained largely unchanged despite the significant increase in the cost of living since the passage of Republic Act No. 6982. As a result, the value of the assistance generated from the lien has significantly diminished over time. The sugar industry itself has also changed. In recent years, the country has increasingly resorted to the importation of raw and refined sugar to address domestic supply requirements. While imported sugar is released and sold in the same domestic market as locally produced sugar, it does not contribute to the Social Amelioration Program. The burden of funding the Program therefore continues to fall on local sugar producers. At the same time, imported sugar enters and competes in the domestic market without being subject to the same lien intended for the benefit of workers whose livelihoods depend on the sugar industry. This bill seeks to address these concerns by extending the Social Amelioration Program lien to imported sugar and updating the applicable lien rate. It likewise provides for periodic adjustments based on inflation, in place of the existing automatic increases, and updates the collection and remittance process to provide for electronic reporting and closer coordination among the Bureau of Customs, the Sugar Regulatory Administration, and the Department of Labor and Employment. These amendments are intended to strengthen the Social Amelioration Program and ensure a more equitable sharing of responsibility for the welfare of sugar workers. The measure seeks to provide a more sustainable source of support for the workers who remain an essential part of the Philippine sugar industry by requiring both locally produced and imported sugar to contribute to the Program. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. EMILIO BERNARDINO L. label: HB 10924
title: AN ACT FIXING THE TERM OF OFFICE OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN TO FIVE (5) YEARS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 12232 OR “AN ACT SETTING THE TERM OF OFFICE OF THE BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution does not prescribe a fixed term of office for barangay officials. Congress therefore possesses the authority—and the corresponding responsibility—to establish a term that promotes democratic accountability while allowing barangay officials sufficient time to govern effectively. Republic Act No. 12232 presently fixes the term of elected barangay and _________NOVFFFFFFF Sangguniang Kabataan officials at four (4) years. This measure proposes to increase the term to five (5) years in order to provide greater stability, continuity, and effectiveness in barangay governance. The barangay is the government institution closest to the people. It is the primary point of contact for residents seeking basic services, public assistance, dispute resolution, disaster response, peace-and-order intervention, and access to government programs. Under the Local Government Code, the barangay serves as the basic political unit and the principal planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, programs, projects, and activities within the community. Despite the breadth of these responsibilities, barangay officials are often required to perform their duties within a governing period significantly shortened by administrative transition and electoral preparation. The initial year of a term is commonly devoted to organizing the new administration, constituting committees, preparing or updating development and investment plans, familiarizing officials with budgeting, accounting, procurement, and audit requirements, and coordinating proposed programs with municipal, city, provincial, and national government agencies. Projects involving infrastructure, livelihood, health, sanitation, disaster preparedness, peace and order, and social welfare may require several stages of planning, funding, procurement, implementation, and evaluation. Before these programs can fully mature, officials may already be compelled to prepare for the next election. Political organizations must be maintained, consultations intensified, campaign resources assembled, and electoral challenges addressed. Consequently, the actual period during which barangay officials can devote their full attention to governance may be considerably shorter than their nominal term. This frequent return to electoral activity can encourage short-term and highly visible projects at the expense of programs whose benefits require sustained implementation. Essential but less immediately visible initiatives—such as drainage maintenance, disaster- risk mapping, nutrition programs, community-based peace-and-order systems, digitization of records, financial controls, and long-term development planning—may be neglected because their results do not always coincide with the electoral calendar. A five-year term would provide barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials with a more practical governing cycle. It would allow sufficient time for institutional organization and comprehensive planning, followed by sustained implementation, project completion, evaluation, accountability, and an orderly transition. label: HB 10928
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FIRE STATION IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF ANAHAWAN, PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every Filipino community deserves timely and reliable protection during ires, disasters, accidents, and other emergencies. The Constitution recognizes the State’s duty to provide adequate public services and improve the quality of life of its people, while Republic Act No. 6975 requires at least one ire station in every municipality. Yet the Municipality of Anahawan, Southern Leyte, still does not have a dedicated ire station and is currently served by the ire station in neighboring San Juan. Anahawan is home to thousands of residents across its fourteen barangays, including families, schools, businesses, government of ices, and other establishments that require dependable emergency services. When every second can mean the difference between saving a life and losing one, distance matters. The absence of a local ire station may result in longer response times, especially during ires, natural disasters, vehicular accidents, and other emergencies requiring immediate rescue and assistance. This bill seeks to establish a dedicated Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) ire station in Anahawan. Bringing ire ighters, rescue personnel, equipment, and emergency services closer to the people will allow faster response, strengthen ire prevention and preparedness, and provide greater security to families and businesses. The Municipality of Anahawan shall provide the necessary land or site, while the BFP shall operate the station in accordance with applicable standards and regulations. 1|Page The establishment of a ire station in Anahawan is more than the construction of a government facility, it is an investment in lives, property, and community safety. It will give families greater peace of mind and ensure that help is closer when they need it most. By bringing essential emergency services closer to the people of Anahawan, this measure advances the State’s duty to protect every community and provide genuine, responsive public service In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. label: HB 10929
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING GREATER RESPONSIBILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY FROM PRIVATE EMPLOYMENT AGENCIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT 10361, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “BATAS KASAMBAHAY”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 10361, otherwise known as the Domestic Workers Act or Batas Kasambahay, is a landmark law that upholds the rights and welfare of domestic workers while recognizing their valuable contribution to Filipino families. The law also allows employers to hire kasambahays through licensed Private Employment Agencies (PEAs), which are expected to carefully screen applicants and ensure that the required clearances and supporting documents are submitted before deployment. While these safeguards are important, they may not always be enough to protect employers and their families from individuals who may use fraudulent identities or falsi ied documents to gain access to private homes and commit crimes. For many Filipino families, the home is a place of safety and trust. Entrusting a domestic worker with the care of children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and valuable property requires con idence that the recruitment process has been conducted with the highest level of diligence and accountability. This bill seeks to strengthen the responsibility and accountability of Private Employment Agencies by requiring them to exercise greater care in screening, verifying, and endorsing applicants for domestic work. By reinforcing existing safeguards, the measure aims to protect both employers and legitimate domestic workers, preserve public trust in the recruitment system, and promote a safer and 1|Page more reliable environment for household employment. In doing so, the bill strikes a fair balance between protecting the rights of kasambahays and ensuring the security and peace of mind of the families they serve. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10930
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE FREE USE OF GOVERNMENT-DONATED FARM MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 18 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7607, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MAGNA CARTA OF SMALL FARMERS”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino farmers play a vital role in ensuring the country's food security, yet many continue to struggle with rising production costs and limited access to affordable farm equipment. Although the government has invested billions of pesos in tractors and other agricultural machinery to help increase farm productivity, many small farmers are still required to pay service charges for using equipment that was purchased with public funds. As a result, the very assistance intended to ease their burden often remains beyond their inancial reach, leaving many farmers with little choice but to rely on expensive private services or continue using labor-intensive methods. This bill seeks to ensure that government assistance truly bene its the farmers it is meant to serve. It requires that government-donated farm machinery and equipment be made available to eligible small farmers without service charges, subject only to the cost of fuel and the availability of the equipment. The measure covers the irst three hectares cultivated by each eligible farmer and may be availed of twice each year, allowing farmers to reduce production costs, cultivate more land, improve productivity, and invest more in their crops instead of spending scarce resources on machinery fees. This measure reaf irms the State's commitment to supporting Filipino farmers and strengthening the agricultural sector. By making government-provided farm 1|Page machinery more accessible and affordable, the bill will help increase farm incomes, improve food production, and uplift the lives of farming families across the country. More importantly, it ensures that public funds allocated for agricultural assistance produce meaningful and lasting bene its for those who feed the nation. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10931
title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE SAINT BERNARD – HINUNANGAN DIVERSION ROAD IN THE PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE INTO A NATIONAL ROAD AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Saint Bernard–Hinunangan Diversion Road is a vital lifeline for the Paci ic Towns of Southern Leyte. By providing a shorter and more direct route between the municipalities of Saint Bernard and Hinunangan, it reduces travel time, lowers transportation costs, and makes it easier for people to reach schools, hospitals, markets, government of ices, and places of work. It also allows farmers, isherfolk, and local entrepreneurs to transport their products more quickly and ef iciently, creating greater opportunities for economic growth and improving the quality of life of communities along its route. Beyond its economic value, the diversion road plays a critical role during emergencies and natural disasters. Whenever the Agas-Agas route becomes impassable due to landslides or other hazards, this road serves as an important alternative route for residents, emergency responders, relief operations, and the delivery of essential goods and services. Its importance was clearly demonstrated during Typhoon Odette, when access to several areas became dif icult. This bill seeks to convert the Saint Bernard–Hinunangan Diversion Road into a national road, placing it under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) for its continued improvement, maintenance, and development. The measure also ensures that the project will be implemented in accordance with engineering, environmental, disaster-resilience, and right-of-way requirements to guarantee a safe, durable, and reliable road network. 1|Page Converting this road into a national road is an investment in the future of Southern Leyte. It will strengthen connectivity among the Paci ic Towns, promote tourism and investment, improve access to essential public services, enhance disaster preparedness and response, and support inclusive and sustainable development throughout the province. By providing the national government's sustained support for this vital infrastructure, the bill will help create better opportunities and a brighter future for the people of Southern Leyte. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FAIR TREATMENT OF CERTAIN SENIOR CITIZEN PENSIONERS BY GRANTING ANNUAL CHRISTMAS CASH GIFT AND PENSION INCREASE TO PENSIONERS OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM AND GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM WHO ARE BENEFICIARIES OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7699, “AN ACT INSTITUTING LIMITED PORTABILITY SCHEME IN THE SOCIAL SECURITY INSURANCE SYSTEMS BY TOTALIZING THE WORKERS’ CREDITABLE SERVICES OF CONTRIBUTIONS IN EACH OF THE SYSTEMS”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks for a fair treatment to our senior citizen pensioners who are bene iciaries of Republic Act No. 7699, “An Act Instituting Limited Portability Scheme in the Social Security Insurance Systems by Totalizing the Workers’ Creditable Services or Contributions in each of the Systems” but are not deemed quali ied, based on existing implementing rules and regulations and other issuances of the SSS and GSIS Boards, to receive some of the bene its given to regular pensioners, speci ically the annual Christmas cash gift and right to pension increase. While RA 7699 appears to be a special law, an accommodation to individual workers who have not “saved enough” in either system, it is necessary to remind the managers of our social security agencies that the law they are implementing and the funds that they are zealously guarding were created to ful il the State’s obligation to protect its people in times of inancial want, especially when they are no longer considered employable. R.A. No. 7699 provides the formula to enable workers to bene it from the fruits of their savings or contributions in both systems. 1|Page Depriving Portability Law pensioners of the bene its given to regular old-age pensioners of both systems is discriminatory and anathema to current trends in social legislation that value and honor the contributions of our senior citizens to society during their productive years. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10933
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MANDATORY INTEGRATION OF VOTER EDUCATION IN THE JUNIOR AND SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL CURRICULA
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill mandates the Department of Education (DepEd) to integrate voter education in the Junior and Senior High School curricula in order to provide a fair and impartial venue for discussion of the Philippine electoral process to young citizens as they prepare to exercise their constitutional right to vote. The electoral process being a catalyst for peaceful and democratic change in the political, social, historical, and economic structures of the country, it is essential that students in Junior and Senior High Schools are educated properly about the importance of elections, plebiscites, or referendums outside the partisan advocacies of competing political parties and candidates during election periods. By providing the youth with suf icient knowledge about the nuances and importance of elections to their future, it is hoped that the proposed High School Voter Education Act will empower the youth to exercise their right to vote responsibly. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10934
title: AN ACT MODERNIZING THE REGULATION OF HEALTH FACILITIES AND SERVICES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HOSPITAL LICENSURE ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every Filipino deserves access to safe, quality, and reliable health care. However, the law governing the licensing and regulation of hospitals was enacted more than ive decades ago, long before the emergence of modern health facilities, mobile medical services, stand-alone diagnostic centers, specialized treatment facilities, and other innovative forms of health care. As the country's health system continues to evolve, our laws must also keep pace to ensure that every health facility and health service meets the standards needed to protect the lives, health, and safety of the Filipino people. This bill seeks to modernize the country's system for regulating health facilities and services by replacing the outdated Hospital Licensure Act with a more comprehensive and responsive legal framework. It expands government oversight to cover not only hospitals but also other health facilities and emerging health services, strengthens the authority of the Department of Health to license, inspect, monitor, and enforce compliance with health standards, and promotes closer coordination among government agencies involved in health regulation. At the same time, the measure upholds fairness and due process while ensuring that unsafe, substandard, or unlicensed facilities cannot continue to operate at the expense of public health. 1|Page This measure reaf irms the State's constitutional duty to protect and promote the right to health. By strengthening the regulation of health facilities and services, it helps ensure that every Filipino receives safe, accessible, and quality health care wherever they may be. More than simply updating an outdated law, this bill is an investment in a stronger health system, greater public trust, and better health outcomes for present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino workers are the backbone of our nation's progress. Every day, they work tirelessly to provide for their families and contribute to the country's economic growth, often sacri icing time for rest, health, and loved ones. Yet despite the increasing demands of the modern workplace, the law continues to grant only ive (5) days of Service Incentive Leave (SIL), a bene it that has remained unchanged for decades. At a time when work-related stress and burnout have become increasingly common, it is only itting that our labor standards evolve to better protect the well- being of Filipino workers. Service Incentive Leave allows employees to recover from illness, attend to family responsibilities, manage personal matters, and take the rest they need to remain healthy and productive. This bill seeks to increase the annual Service Incentive Leave from ive (5) days to ten (10) days. To encourage employees to actually use their leave for rest and recovery, only up to ive (5) unused leave days may be converted into cash, while the remaining ive (5) days are intended to be enjoyed as paid leave. The measure likewise protects workers by ensuring that existing leave bene its that are more favorable than those provided by law will not be diminished. By giving workers more time to rest, recharge, and care for themselves and their families, this measure promotes a healthier, more productive, and more motivated 1|Page workforce. It recognizes that protecting the welfare of workers is not only an act of compassion but also a sound investment in the nation's productivity and economic growth. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10936
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A PERMANENT STAFFING COMPLEMENT FOR THE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE FOR INDIGENT AND FINANCIALLY INCAPACITATED PATIENTS (MAIFIP) PROGRAM OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, CREATING PLANTILLA POSITIONS THEREFOR, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE For decades, the Department of Health (DOH) has provided medical assistance to indigent and financially incapacitated Filipinos who are unable to fully shoulder the cost of hospitalization, medicines, diagnostic procedures, and other necessary medical services. Through the years, this assistance has evolved under different program names and mechanisms, from the Medical Assistance Program (MAP), to the Medical Assistance for Indigent Patients (MAIP), and presently, the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) Program. Despite changes in its name and implementing guidelines, the purpose of the program has remained constant: to ensure that financial hardship does not prevent Filipinos from obtaining necessary medical care. MAIFIP has since become an important component of the government's health and social protection system. Its implementation requires personnel who receive and evaluate requests for assistance, coordinate with hospitals and health facilities, process and monitor financial assistance, maintain records, prepare reports, and perform other administrative and patient-facing functions necessary for the timely delivery of medical assistance. However, while MAIFIP has developed into a continuing government program with substantial responsibilities at the national, regional, and local levels, the personnel structure supporting its implementation has not necessarily developed at the same pace. In many areas, program implementation continues to depend on personnel engaged under temporary arrangements or on existing personnel who perform MAIFIP-related functions alongside their regular responsibilities. A continuing public service should be supported by an appropriately stable and accountable workforce. Dependence on temporary staffing arrangements for continuing functions may result in personnel turnover, loss of institutional knowledge, repeated training requirements, uneven implementation, and disruptions in the delivery of assistance. These challenges are particularly significant in a program whose beneficiaries are patients and families seeking government assistance at a time of medical and financial distress. This measure therefore seeks to institutionalize a permanent staffing complement for the MAIFIP Program by directing the DOH, in coordination with the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and the Civil Service Commission (CSC), to establish appropriate permanent plantilla positions for its implementation at the DOH Central Office, Centers for Health Development, and Provincial DOH Offices or other appropriate field offices. Rather than prescribing a uniform number of personnel for every locality, the proposed measure allows staffing requirements to be determined according to actual program workload and operational needs, including the number of beneficiaries and applications processed, the number of participating health facilities, geographic coverage, program allocation and utilization, and other relevant indicators. The measure likewise recognizes the experience acquired by existing personnel who have been performing MAIFIP functions under Job Order, Contract of Service, and similar arrangements by ensuring that qualified personnel are given the opportunity to apply for the permanent positions created pursuant to this Act, subject to the Constitution, civil service laws, qualification standards, and the principles of merit and fitness. The MAIFIP Program has endured and expanded because the need it addresses remains. It is therefore appropriate that the government strengthen not only the resources available for medical assistance, but also the institutional capacity and workforce responsible for ensuring that such assistance reaches those who need it. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10937
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SEEDLING BANK OF THE BUREAU OF PLANT INDUSTRY IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF HINUNANGAN, PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture remains the backbone of many communities in the Philippines, providing food on every Filipino table and livelihood to millions of families. Yet despite the hard work and dedication of our farmers, many continue to struggle with low productivity, limited access to quality seeds and planting materials, and the increasing challenges brought about by pests, diseases, and climate change. Without the proper support, farmers find it difficult to increase their harvests, improve their incomes, and meet the growing demand for food. One of the biggest challenges faced by farmers, especially in rural areas, is the lack of affordable access to certified seeds, improved planting materials, and modern farming technologies. Many small farmers cannot afford expensive farm inputs or must travel long distances just to obtain quality seedlings and technical assistance. As a result, they often rely on low-quality planting materials that produce poor yields, limiting both their productivity and their opportunities to earn a better living. This bill seeks to establish a Seedling Bank of the Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) in the Municipality of Hinunangan, Province of Southern Leyte. Strategically located to serve the municipalities of the province, particularly those along the Pacific area, the proposed facility will provide quality seeds and planting materials, technical assistance, farmer training, and modern crop production technologies. It will also 1 | Page serve as a center for research, demonstration, and the promotion of climate-resilient and high-value crops, enabling farmers to produce more, earn more, and become more resilient to the effects of climate change. The establishment of a BPI Seedling Bank in Southern Leyte is more than an investment in agriculture, it is an investment in food security, rural development, and the future of Filipino farming families. By bringing government services closer to farmers, this measure will reduce production costs, improve crop quality, increase farm productivity, and create more livelihood opportunities in the countryside. It will also strengthen the province's capacity to supply quality planting materials that will benefit not only Southern Leyte but neighboring areas as well. Through this measure, the State reaffirms its commitment to empowering Filipino farmers with the tools, knowledge, and support they need to succeed. A stronger agriculture sector means stronger rural communities, greater food security, and a more resilient economy. By helping our farmers grow more today, we secure a better future for generations to come. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M.
