label: HB 10938
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ANTI-RABIES PROGRAM THROUGH MANDATORY MICROCHIPPING OF PET DOGS AND CATS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9482, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-RABIES ACT OF 2007”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the country’s anti-rabies program under Republic Act No. 9482 or the “Anti-Rabies Act of 2007”, by requiring the mandatory microchipping, in addition to mandatory registration, of pet cats and dogs, in order to ensure that stray dogs and cats are easily identi ied and returned to their owners as soon as they are caught to avoid possible infection from infected stray animals in the community. While stray dogs are usually the main source of rabies infestation in a community, cats are proposed to be included for mandatory registration and microchipping for the simple reason that house cats that are left to roam around the community are vulnerable to being attacked by another animals that are possibly infected with rabies. Unlike other progressive countries, the Philippines has remained to have one of the highest numbers of rabies cases in the world. The Department of Health (DOH) has reported that around 200 or 300 Filipinos die of rabies every year. One of the major reasons for this high rabies incidence in the country is the low compliance with the mandatory registration of dogs provided in RA 9482, hence, the dif iculty on the part of government employees to return stray dogs to their rightful owners. 1|Page In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill is in support of the legislative agenda of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), our partner in securing our public and private infrastructures from all destructive ires. label: HB 10940
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS HOTLINE, MANDATING ITS OPERATION, INTEROPERABILITY, AND ADEQUATE FUNDING, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11036, or the “Mental Health Act,” was a landmark step in recognizing mental health as a matter of national policy. Section 21 of the law directs the Department of Health (DOH) to establish twenty-four hour, toll-free, and accessible hotlines for suicide prevention. Since its passage, this mandate remains only partly realized. Several agencies and private organizations operate separate helplines using different numbers, protocols, and hours of operation, resulting in a fragmented system where a person in crisis may not know which number to call, or may reach a line that cannot respond in time. This proposed Act does not attempt to overhaul the country’s entire mental health crisis infrastructure, but focuses on a single, achievable, and urgently needed reform, one that establishes a three-digit national hotline that is easy to remember, free of charge on all networks, and capable of receiving calls, text messages, and the like. Consistent with how mental health crises actually are, the hotline is intended to serve any person experiencing a mental health crisis, whether they are under overwhelming stress, anxiety, panic, grief, trauma, or other acute emotional distress, regardless of whether this leads to thoughts of self-harm or suicide. In light of the prevailing climate of uncertainty, escalating violence, and disruptions brought about by an always-connected, online, and overstimulating world, more and more are having to navigate complex mental health landscapes. This necessitates convenient platforms for listening and helping address such concerns. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this Bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 10941
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FIXED VALUE-ADDED TAX PRICE BENCHMARK FOR COVERED ELECTRICITY TRANSACTION AND EXPANDING THE VALUE- ADDED TAX EXEMPTION FOR FUELS USED IN POWER GENERATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 108 AND 109 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Electricity is a basic service and an essential input to household welfare, public services, and economic activity. However, electricity charges may rise sharply when international fuel prices increase, particularly where generation depends on coal, natural gas, diesel, fuel oil, or other fuel sources exposed to global markets, foreign-exchange movements, transport costs, and supply disruptions. When value-added tax is computed on the entire increased charge, the tax correspondingly magnifies the burden on households, micro, small and medium enterprises, and other electricity consumers. In Small Power Utilities Group and other missionary, off-grid, and isolated- grid areas, electricity is frequently supplied by diesel and oil-fired generators. The cost and logistical difficulty of transporting fuel to remote areas may result in materially higher generation costs and may increase the need for subsidies and other support mechanisms. Fuel-related increases may therefore affect both the electricity bills of consumers and the fiscal burden associated with maintaining reliable electricity service. Under Section 108 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 9337, the sale of electricity by generation, transmission, and distribution companies is treated as a sale or exchange of services subject to value-added tax on gross receipts. The Bureau of Internal Revenue has likewise clarified that generation, transmission, distribution companies, and electric cooperatives are subject to value-added tax on their sale of electricity. This bill retains the statutory value-added tax rate and instead limits the taxable base for specified electricity sales. It establishes a Fixed VAT Price Benchmark, expressed in Philippine pesos per kilowatt-hour, as the maximum VAT taxable base for covered electricity transactions. Value-added tax shall be computed on the lower of the actual gross receipts or selling price per kilowatt-hour and the applicable benchmark. The portion of the actual electricity charge exceeding the benchmark shall be excluded from the VAT taxable base, without being treated as a VAT-exempt or zero-rated transaction and without creating an additional entitlement to input-tax refund or credit. This measure recognizes that generation technologies have different cost structures and exposure to fuel-price shocks. The Energy Regulatory Commission shall therefore determine, validate, review, and publish the benchmarks using objective and verifiable standards. International energy-crisis measures demonstrate the policy validity of using targeted tax relief and price-stabilization tools to protect electricity consumers. The Fixed VAT Price Benchmark is a Philippine legislative adaptation of such recognized policy tools, designed to provide relief from extraordinary electricity-price increases while preserving a predictable and administratively workable VAT base for the National Government. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. SERGIO C. DAGOOC REP. PRESLEY C. label: HB 10942
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR DIGITAL PLATFORMS, PROMOTING RESPONSIBLE DIGITAL ENGAGEMENT AND ONLINE SAFETY FOR THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM ONLINE HARMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid advancement of information and communications technology has fundamentally reshaped the manner by which Filipinos communicate, access information, pursue education, conduct business, and participate in civic life. Digital platforms, including social networking services, messaging applications, online gaming platforms, content-sharing services, livestreaming platforms, and other interactive digital technologies have become indispensable tools in modern society. While these technologies have significantly contributed to economic growth, innovation, and digital inclusion, they have likewise created unprecedented challenges, particularly with respect to the protection of children in the online environment. The increasing accessibility of digital platforms has correspondingly heightened the exposure of children and adolescents to online harms such as cyberbullying, online grooming, identity theft, privacy violations, harmful and age-inappropriate content, deceptive digital practices, excessive screen time, and other forms of digital exploitation. These risks have become more complex as digital platforms continue to evolve, underscoring the need for a comprehensive regulatory framework that balances technological innovation with the State's constitutional duty to protect the welfare of its citizens. Empirical evidence demonstrates the urgency of legislative intervention. In Sexual Exploitation and Abuse of Children Online in the Philippines: A Review of Online News and Articles, Hernandez, Lacsina, Ylade, Aldaba, Lam, Estacio, and Lopez documented the alarming prevalence of Online Sexual Exploitation and Abuse of Children (OSEAC) in the Philippines. The study identified recurring incidents involving livestreamed child sexual abuse, child sexual abuse materials, and sextortion, with victims ranging from infancy to adolescence. It further observed that the widespread availability of digital technologies, coupled with socioeconomic vulnerabilities and inadequate online safeguards, has facilitated the proliferation of these offenses, thereby highlighting the necessity for stronger preventive measures and institutional responses. Complementing these findings, a study published in the Philippine Social Science Journal emphasizes that children's increasing engagement with digital platforms extends their exposure beyond criminal exploitation to a broader spectrum of psychosocial and developmental risks. The study identifies cyberbullying, problematic digital use, diminished parental supervision, privacy and data security concerns, and harmful online interactions as emerging issues that require coordinated interventions involving government, families, educational institutions, and digital platform operators. It likewise underscores that digital literacy, platform accountability, and child-centered online safety mechanisms are essential components of an effective child protection framework in the digital age. Although the Philippines has enacted significant legislation such as Republic Act No. 10173, otherwise known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012; Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; and Republic Act No. 11930, or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act, these laws principally address specific unlawful acts or regulate particular aspects of digital governance. At present, there remains no comprehensive statutory framework that establishes uniform safety standards, preventive obligations, and accountability mechanisms applicable to digital platform operators for the protection of children. This proposed measure seeks to address this legislative gap by establishing a comprehensive regulatory framework governing digital platforms operating within the Philippines. It mandates the adoption of age- appropriate safeguards, privacy-preserving age verification systems, digital well-being features, parental supervision mechanisms, transparent platform policies, and effective reporting and redress systems. It likewise institutionalizes inter-agency coordination among the Department of Information and Communications Technology, the National Telecommunications Commission, the National Privacy Commission, the Department of Health, the Department of Education, the Department of Social Welfare and Development, the Presidential Communications Office, the Council for the Welfare of Children, and other concerned agencies to ensure a coherent and whole-of-government approach to digital safety and child protection. Ultimately, this measure affirms the State's commitment to uphold the constitutional rights and welfare of children while fostering a safe, secure, and trustworthy digital ecosystem that promotes responsible innovation, protection, and ensures that technological advancement remains consistent with the public interest. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTOLIN “LENLEN” A. label: HB 10943
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING COCONUT FARMERS’ PARTICIPATION IN THE UTILIZATION OF THE COCONUT FARMERS AND INDUSTRY TRUST FUND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11524, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “COCONUT FARMERS AND INDUSTRY TRUST FUND ACT”, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The coconut industry remains an important pillar of Philippine agriculture, providing livelihoods to millions of Filipino farmers and contributing significantly to the country’s agricultural economy. Despite its importance, coconut farmers continue to face challenges such as low productivity, aging coconut trees, limited access to technology, pests and diseases, and increasingly severe weather disturbances. Republic Act No. 11524, or the “Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund Act,” provides for the utilization of the Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund for the benefit of coconut farmers and the development of the industry. However, meaningful participation of farmers in decisions involving the trust fund remains essential to ensure that its programs and resources respond to their actual needs. Therefore, this bill seeks to establish the Coconut Farmers Advisory Board (COCOFAB), composed of representatives from registered coconut farmers’ federations, cooperatives, and/or people’s organizations. The COCOFAB shall participate in reviewing development priorities and proposed budget allocations, monitoring trust fund programs, and providing policy recommendations to the Philippine Coconut Authority and relevant agencies. By giving coconut farmers a meaningful voice in the management of resources intended for their benefit, this measure seeks to promote a more transparent, accountable, responsive, and sustainable coconut industry. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10944
title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE CLASSIFICATION OF IROSIN DISTRICT OFFICE OF THE LAND TRANSPORTATION OFFICE (LTO) IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF IROSIN, PROVINCE OF SORSOGON FROM CLASS “D” TO CLASS “B” DISTRICT OFFICE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Land Transportation Office (LTO) Irosin District Office plays an important role in providing licensing, motor vehicle registration, enforcement, and other frontline services to the people of the Second District of Sorsogon. As the volume of transactions continues to increase, the office faces growing demands on its existing personnel and operational capacity. The LTO Irosin District Office has recorded significant and sustained activity in recent years. Motor vehicle registrations increased annually, from 7,524 in 2023 to 19,534 in 2025, while 15,763 registrations were already recorded from January to July 2026. The office likewise handled 13,233 motor vehicle registration and case transactions in 2023, whereas it recorded 24,326 in just the first seven months of 2026. The office also issued 12,518 licenses and permits in 2023 and handled 19,474 license and permit transaction cases, compared to 8,790 and 15,735, respectively, from January to July 2026 as well. Therefore, this bill seeks to upgrade the classification of the LTO Irosin District Office from Class “D” to Class “B” and increase its permanent plantilla positions from eight (8) to twenty (20). The additional personnel will strengthen the office’s capacity to address its growing workload, reduce processing time, and provide faster and more efficient frontline services to the public. By aligning the office’s classification and personnel complement with its actual workload, this measure seeks to improve public service delivery, strengthen traffic and transportation regulation, and enhance the efficiency of government operations in the Second District of Sorsogon. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10949
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A GRADUATED, AGE-CALIBRATED FRAMEWORK OF LIABILITY FOR CHILDREN IN CONFLICT WITH THE LAW AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 6 AND 7 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9344, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10630
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE When Republic Act No. 9344, or the "Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006," was enacted, it represented a deliberate and well-intentioned shift toward a child-centered, restorative approach to juvenile justice, raising the minimum age of criminal responsibility (MACR) from nine (9) to fifteen (15) years old and placing children in conflict with the law (CICL) at the center of intervention, diversion, and rehabilitation rather than punishment. That policy shift was, and remains, consistent with the State's obligations under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and with the constitutional mandate to protect and promote the rights of children to assistance, proper care, and special protection from all forms of neglect, abuse, cruelty, exploitation, and other conditions prejudicial to their development. Nearly two decades later, the law as currently calibrated did not anticipate and has struggled to respond to a disturbing pattern of petty and more recently heinous crimes committed by children who, because of the blanket exemption enjoyed by those fifteen (15) years old and below, are shielded from criminal liability regardless of the gravity of the act or the clarity of intent behind it. This gap has become impossible to ignore in light of a string of recent, well-documented incidents involving children in conflict with the law: Page 1 On June 16, 2026, a 14-year-old Grade 8 student armed with a kitchen knife entered a Grade 5 classroom at a private school in General Trias City, Cavite, and stabbed seven (7) young pupils, two of whom required surgery. On June 22, 2026, two students aged 14 and 15 opened fire inside San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, killing three (3) fellow students and wounding twenty (20) others in what has been described as one of the deadliest school-related attacks in the country's recent history. On June 23, 2026, a 17-year-old student stabbed a fellow 17-year-old student outside Julio Ledesma National High School in San Carlos City, Negros Occidental, arising from a personal grudge, leaving the victim seriously wounded. On July 31, 2026, a 14-year-old student fatally stabbed his 13-year-old classmate inside Las Piñas National High School over a trivial dispute involving ten pesos (Php10.00) in change, prompting the school to suspend face-to-face classes and review how a bladed weapon evaded metal detectors and security personnel. Most recently, on August 18, 2026, a 14-year-old Grade 9 student brought firearms onto the campus of the Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City, shot and killed a fellow student, wounded several others, and then turned the gun on himself — an attack that was livestreamed on social media and that has been described as the country's second fatal school shooting in less than two months. These incidents, taken together with the increasing frequency of law enforcement interceptions of children carrying firearms, knives, and other bladed weapons on their way to school, reveal that a rigid, single-threshold exemption no longer reflects the reality on the ground. A significant number of children between the ages of nine (9) and seventeen (17) are demonstrably capable of forming intent, understanding the wrongfulness of grave acts, and, in the most extreme cases, planning and executing them; circumstances that the pre-2006 regime under the Revised Penal Code was designed to address through the concept of "discernment" and the privileged mitigating circumstance of minority, without abandoning the child's constitutional and statutory protections. This bill does not seek to undo the restorative and rehabilitative philosophy that undergirds Republic Act No. 9344. Diversion, restorative justice, confidentiality of records, the prohibition against detention of children in regular jails alongside adults, the automatic suspension of sentence, access to Bahay Pag-Asa and comprehensive intervention programs, and the child's right to counsel and to be heard remain fully intact under this measure. What this bill proposes is a more calibrated, three-tiered framework restoring the pre-Republic Act No. 9344 age brackets under Article 12 of the Revised Penal Code under which: (i) children below nine (9) years of age remain absolutely exempt from criminal liability and are referred to intervention programs; (ii) children nine (9) years old up to below fifteen Page 2 (15) years old are conditionally liable, subject to a threshold inquiry into whether they acted with discernment; and (iii) children fifteen (15) years old up to below eighteen (18) years old are subject to the full weight of criminal responsibility, tempered by the privileged mitigating circumstance of minority and continued access to suspended sentence and rehabilitative disposition. This measure seeks to strike the balance the public is demanding: one that neither treats a nine-year-old as a hardened offender nor allows a heinous, premeditated act by a sixteen-year-old to go entirely unanswered by the criminal justice system, while preserving every child-sensitive and restorative safeguard that Republic Act No. 9344 has built over the past two decades. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. The passage of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. ALEXANDER T. label: HB 10950
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FREE MEDICAL AND DENTAL SERVICES TO INDIGENT CHILDREN, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide medical and dental services to indigent children from families who lack the means to pay for their treatment. As the saying goes, the children are our future. The 1987 Constitution affords them every form of protection, directing the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development, endeavoring to make essential goods, health, and other social services available to all the people at affordable cost, with priority given to the underprivileged sick, elderly, disabled, and children. Children remain more susceptible to illness given their developing immune systems, yet many families — particularly those hit hardest by rising costs since the pandemic — cannot afford to bring them to a doctor or dentist. In the first semester of 2021, the Philippine Statistics Authority reported that the poverty rate in the country had increased by 2.6 percentage points, from 21.1% to 23.7%. This bill seeks to address and provide a real difference in how free and timely care would make a difference in a child's life and in a family's peace of mind. I now file this measure, first introduced in the 19th Congress, to extend that same commitment nationwide. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. MARCELINO R. label: HB 10951
title: AN ACT GRANTING FUNERAL AND MEMORIAL DISCOUNT PRIVILEGES TO QUALIFIED PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant our public school teachers funeral and memorial discount privileges on account of work-related sickness and injuries. Teaching remains one of the noblest professions, entrusted with shaping the character and capability of our people. The 1987 Constitution itself directs the State to give priority to education in order to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development. Yet our educators continue to receive compensation that leaves little room to absorb life's heaviest expenses — among them, the cost of a decent burial for a loved one lost in the course of their work. It is estimated that funeral services in the Philippines cost at least P100,000 to cover registration of death, mortuary care, coffin or urns, cremation, and columbarium or memorial lots. Having served the people of Marikina both as a legislator and, later, as Mayor, I have seen the sacrifices our teachers make and the burdens their families carry when tragedy strikes in the course of their duties. This measure, first filed in the 19th Congress, seeks to ease that burden, if only in part. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. MARCELINO R. label: HB 10952
title: AN ACT PROVIDING HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATION (HMO) COVERAGE FOR ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide a Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) to all qualified public school teachers employed in accredited public educational institutions nationwide. Our educators carry out a role of national importance, simplifying complex problems and imparting the knowledge that eventually becomes our own — yet they continue to receive compensation insufficient to cover even their basic medical needs, let alone comprehensive health coverage. As our schools continue to hold face-to-face classes, it is only right that our teachers be assured of protection not just against infectious disease, but for their health needs as a whole. Having worked closely with our local schools during my time as Mayor of Marikina, I know how much our teachers give of themselves — often at the expense of their own well-being — for the sake of their students. This measure, originally filed in the 19th Congress, seeks to ensure that our teachers' health is finally given the protection it deserves. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. MARCELINO R. label: HB 10953
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL FILIPINO WOMEN'S MUSEUM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish the National Filipino Women's Museum to honor the significant contributions of Filipino women in their fight for equality and justice, as well as those who have made a lasting impact on the lives of the Filipino people. Throughout our history, women have played an indispensable role in nation-building, even as they were long denied the same rights, opportunities, and recognition afforded to men. It was through their courage and resolve that many of the freedoms we now enjoy — the right to vote, to education, to health services, and to full participation in public life — were secured. Our national museums rightly honor heroes such as Jose Rizal, Andres Bonifacio, Emilio Aguinaldo, and Apolinario Mabini, yet give far less space to the women who stood alongside them and, in many cases, led the way: Gabriela Silang, who led an uprising against a foreign power; Melchora Aquino, popularly known as Tandang Sora, the Mother of the Revolution; Josefa Llanes Escoda, who pioneered the Girl Scouts of the Philippines; and Teresa Magbanua, who commanded the northern zone of Iloilo against the Spaniards. Their contributions shaped our social, political, and working conditions, our marital rights, and the very foundations of our laws. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. MARCELINO R. label: HB 10954
title: AN ACT GRANTING SCHOLARSHIP GRANTS TO ALL QUALIFIED PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND THEIR CHILDREN, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant scholarship grants to all qualified public school teachers for the advancement of their profession, and to their children for their growth and development. Our public school teachers remain among the most undervalued yet indispensable pillars of nation-building. It is through their patience and dedication that generations of Filipinos, including many of my own constituents in Marikina, have been equipped to think critically, adapt to change, and contribute meaningfully to our society. During my years as Mayor of Marikina, I saw firsthand how our teachers labored to advance their own credentials — often pursuing further studies at their own expense and against real financial constraints — while still prioritizing the education of their own children ahead of their own advancement. It is time that the State shoulder more of this burden, so that our educators need not choose between their own growth and that of their families. This measure was first filed in the 19th Congress. I am seeking to revive it because our educators deserve nothing less than our full and sustained support. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. During my years as Mayor of Marikina, I saw firsthand how our teachers labored to advance their own credentials — often pursuing further studies at their own expense and against real financial constraints — while still prioritizing the education of their own children ahead of their own advancement. It is time that the State shoulder more of this burden, so that our educators need not choose between their own growth and that of their families. This measure was first filed in the 19th Congress. I am seeking to revive it because our educators deserve nothing less than our full and sustained support. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE MARIKINA-SAN MATEO-RODRIGUEZ GROWTH AREA, CREATING THE MARIKINA-SAN MATEO-RODRIGUEZ GROWTH AREA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The contiguous corridor comprising the City of Marikina and the Municipalities of San Mateo and Rodriguez (Montalban) in the Province of Rizal serves as a critical strategic gateway bridging Metro Manila and the Sierra Madre mountain range. This interconnected geographic area shares vital natural resources, such as the Upper Marikina River Basin, while facing common socio-economic, environmental, and infrastructure challenges. Despite rapid urban expansion, this contiguous territory possesses great potential for sustainable economic growth through ecotourism, low-impact industrial development, modern infrastructure integration, and unified watershed protection. To attract catalytic investments, encourage green industry adoption, and ensure sustainable development, this bill establishes the Marikina-San Mateo-Rodriguez (MARISARO) Growth Area, creates the MARISARO Growth Area Development Authority (MGADA), and provides a targeted framework of fiscal, non-fiscal, and administrative incentives for eligible projects and enterprises. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly requested. REP. label: HB 10956
title: AN ACT PROMOTING HOUSEHOLD SOLAR ENERGY ADOPTION, PROVIDING INCENTIVES AND FINANCING MECHANISMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill, the "Household Solar Energy Adoption Act” addresses the Philippines' vulnerability to global fossil fuel volatility and climate shocks by shifting the national energy architecture toward household-level, distributed renewable energy systems. Recent geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East have highlighted the fragility of an energy grid heavily reliant on imported fossil fuels, driving inflation and high electricity costs for Filipino households. Beyond these short-term crises, this measure serves as a long-term investment in generational security, economic resilience, and climate survival. By deploying rooftop solar, energy storage, and smart grids, the state can transition homes from passive consumers into active energy producers—democratizing access, lowering utility bills, and building localized disaster resilience. While Republic Act No. 9513 (the Renewable Energy Act of 2008) laid the foundation for large-scale renewable energy development, nearly two decades of implementation reveal a critical gap: the limited penetration of clean energy technologies at the household level. This measure bridges that gap by directly translating national climate commitments into localized, household-centered energy transformation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. label: HB 10958
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING CRIMINAL LIABILITY FOR THE NEGLIGENT FAILURE TO SAFEGUARD FIREARMS, PROVIDING ENHANCED PENALTIES WHEN SUCH FIREARMS ARE SUBSEQUENTLY USED IN THE COMMISSION OF A CRIME OR WHEN THE FIREARM INVOLVED IS GOVERNMENT-ISSUED, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10591, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “COMPREHENSIVE FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION REGULATION ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The privilege of owning or possessing a firearm carries a corresponding duty to keep it secure and beyond the reach or control of unauthorized persons. A firearm that is carelessly stored, left unattended, or otherwise inadequately safeguarded may be lost, taken, accessed, or used by another person, creating a grave and preventable risk to public safety. Republic Act No. 10591, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act,” regulates the licensing, possession, transfer, and reporting of firearms. The law, however, does not establish a clear and direct criminal offense that focuses specifically on negligent failure to safeguard a firearm before any unlawful transfer or failure to report occurs. This measure therefore creates two separate criminal acts. First, a licensed firearm holder who, through negligence, fails to safely secure or safeguard a firearm shall be punished by imprisonment of two (2) years. Second, when the firearm negligently left unsecured or inadequately safeguarded is subsequently used in the commission of a crime, the firearm holder shall be punished by imprisonment of five (5) years. The bill further recognizes the heightened duty borne by public officers and employees who are entrusted with government-issued firearms by reason of their office, position, or employment. Because such firearms are public property placed in their custody for an official purpose, the penalties are increased when the negligent firearm holder is a public officer or employee and the firearm involved is government-issued. Under this measure, the corresponding penalties are four (4) years for negligent failure to safeguard a government-issued firearm and ten (10) years when that firearm is subsequently used in the commission of a crime. The proposed offenses are directed at negligent custody and safekeeping. They do not diminish the criminal liability of the person who unlawfully takes, possesses, or uses the firearm, and they do not prevent prosecution under other applicable laws where the facts independently establish another offense. The measure likewise protects lawful defensive access to and use of a firearm during an emergency. The mere fact that a spouse, relative, household member, guest, or other person gains access to a firearm in order to defend the firearm holder, another person, or the dwelling against an actual or imminent unlawful attack shall not, by itself, establish negligent safekeeping. Nor shall a firearm used under a justifying circumstance recognized in Article 11 of the Revised Penal Code be deemed to have been used in the commission of a crime for purposes of the enhanced offense under this Act. This protection is intended to preserve the right of individuals to act lawfully in defense of life and safety while maintaining accountability for genuinely negligent firearm custody. By establishing clear duties and proportionate penalties, this measure seeks to promote responsible firearm ownership, strengthen accountability among public officers entrusted with government firearms, and reduce the risk that negligently secured firearms will be used to endanger life, property, and public order. Approval of this bill is earnestly sought. JANICE V. label: HB 10961
title: AN ACT MANDATING A SMOKE–FREE AND VAPE–FREE ENVIRONMENT IN ALL PUBLIC PLACES AND WORKPLACES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9211, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “TOBACCO REGULATION ACT OF 2003” AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11900, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “VAPORIZED NICOTINE AND NON-NICOTINE PRODUCTS AND REGULATION ACT”, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to mandate a truly smoke-free and vape-free environment in all public places and workplaces. It amends Republic Act (RA) No. 9211, otherwise known as the “Tobacco Regulation Act of 2003” and RA No. 11900, otherwise known as the “Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act” to expand and modernize key definitions to ensure comprehensive coverage regardless of ownership or physical enclosure. It strengthens enforcement by requiring strict standards for designated smoking and vaping areas, creating local Smoke-Free and Vape-Free Task Forces with dedicated budget allocations, and instituting a Tobacco and Vape Sales License system, all while imposing graduated penalties for violations. The abovementioned laws were enacted to regulate the sale, use, and promotion of tobacco and vape products. However, gaps in the current definitions of public places, public conveyances, and smoking and vaping activities have allowed inconsistent enforcement of smoke-free policies, particularly with the rise of vaping and heated tobacco products, which were not adequately contemplated when RA No. 9211 was first passed. This bill closes definitional loopholes and strengthens local enforcement mechanisms. It upholds the State’s policy to protect public health consistent with the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, safeguarding non-smokers, workers, and minors from the harmful effects of tobacco smoke and vape emissions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10962
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10152, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MANDATORY INFANTS AND CHILDREN HEALTH IMMUNIZATION ACT OF 2011”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive and mandatory National Immunization Program that expands vaccine coverage across all life stages, strengthens the country’s immunization framework, institutionalizes evidence-based vaccine policy through the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG), and integrates immunization services into the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) benefit package. Despite existing immunization programs, vaccine-preventable diseases continue to pose significant public health risks due to gaps in coverage, declining vaccination rates, fragmented implementation, and limited public awareness. The current legal framework primarily focuses on infants and children and does not provide a comprehensive, life-course approach to immunization. This bill expands mandatory immunization coverage, provides free vaccine administration through government health facilities and school- and community-based programs, institutionalizes an independent technical advisory body to guide immunization policy, strengthens public education and health personnel training, and ensures sustained funding and oversight for the National Immunization Program. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10963
title: AN ACT EXPANDING MENTAL HEALTH COVERAGE UNDER THE PHILIPPINE HEALTH INSURANCE CORPORATION BY ESTABLISHING A MENTAL HEALTH VOUCHER SYSTEM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to expand mental health coverage under the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) by establishing a Mental Health Voucher System (MHVS). It institutes tiered benefit packages calibrated to the severity of a beneficiary's condition and establishes a dedicated Mental Health Fund Pool to ensure sustainable financing. Mental health remains one of the most underfunded and inaccessible areas of healthcare in the Philippines. Despite the enactment of Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as the “Mental Health Act”, which legally recognized mental health care as a fundamental right, substantial barriers to treatment persist. High costs for psychiatric consultations, therapy, and essential medications remain a major obstacle, leaving many Filipinos unable to maintain the continuity of care necessary for recovery. This current gap in financing prevents timely interventions and undermines the effectiveness of the national mental health strategy. This bill creates a dedicated, needs-based financing mechanism for mental health care. In fulfillment of this goal, it promotes early diagnosis, continuity of treatment, and improved health outcomes for Filipinos living with mental health conditions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10964
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MODERN HOSPITAL NETWORK LICENSING SYSTEM, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HOSPITAL LICENSURE ACT”, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a Modern Hospital Network Licensing System that regulates hospitals and healthcare facilities as part of integrated networks. It institutes a comprehensive licensing framework covering governance, quality and patient safety standards, interoperability and cybersecurity requirements, emergency preparedness, and continuity of care, while promoting integration between public and private healthcare systems and providing appropriate incentives, administrative sanctions, and criminal penalties to ensure compliance. Republic Act No. 4226, otherwise known as the “Hospital Licensure Act”, has governed hospital licensing in the Philippines for over five decades, but it no longer reflects the realities of modern healthcare delivery. Today, many hospitals operate as part of integrated networks spanning multiple facilities, employ digital health systems and telemedicine, and rely on interoperable health information systems. These are developments that the current facility-based licensing model was never designed to address. This bill ensures that our healthcare regulatory framework keeps pace with scientific advances and digital transformation, while safeguarding patient safety, data privacy, and quality of care for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10965
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF AND PROVIDING FOR EXTENDED PATERNITY LEAVE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8187, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PATERNITY LEAVE ACT OF 1996”, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to expand the coverage and duration of paternity leave from seven (7) to thirty (30) working days. It amends Republic Act (RA) No. 8187, otherwise known as the “Paternity Leave Act of 1996”, extends the eligibility to all male employees regardless of marital status, and recognizes partners in cohabiting arrangements. Despite the enactment of RA No. 8187, the existing seven-day leave period is often insufficient for fathers and their partners to provide meaningful support during childbirth and postpartum recovery. Many fathers are compelled to immediately return to work despite the physical, emotional, and financial demands faced by mothers and newborn children during the crucial early stages of recovery and caregiving. According to the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), fathers who actively participate in early caregiving help reduce maternal stress and improve child well-being1. Likewise, the International Labour Organization (ILO) emphasized that paternity leave policies promote gender equality in caregiving responsibilities and create more family-supportive workplaces2. This proposed measure provides a more responsive, inclusive, and progressive paternity leave policy that promotes shared parenting responsibilities and supports the welfare of Filipino families. It recognizes the important role of fathers and partners in ensuring a safe, healthy, and supportive environment for both mother and child. 1 United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) (2019). Are the World’s Richest Countries Family Friendly? Policy in the OECD and EU. UNICEF. Accessed on 18 May 2026. 2 International Labour Organization (2022). Care at Work: Investing in Care Leave and Services for a More Gender Equal World of Work. International Labour Organization. Accessed on 18 May 2026. Strengthening paternity leave is not merely a labor measure but a social investment in healthier families and more equitable parenting. It is the imperative duty of the State to adopt policies that uphold gender equality, shared responsibility, and family well-being. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10966
title: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE REGIONAL OFFICES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) has long been at the forefront of fostering technological innovation and scientific advancement in the Philippines. A crucial part of DOST’s strategy in fulfilling its mandate is through the implementation of various programs aimed at empowering local industries, improving the lives of Filipino communities, and contributing to national progress. These programs, such as the Small Enterprise Technology Upgrading Program (SET-UP), Community Empowerment through Science and Technology (CEST), OneLab, and Grants-in-Aid for Research and Innovation on Development (GRIND), play a pivotal role in addressing the needs of local businesses, communities, and scientific institutions. To ensure the effective and seamless implementation of these programs and meet the increasing demands for science and technology interventions, it is crucial to strengthen the capacities of the DOST Regional Offices that would enhance collaboration with local government units (LGUs), stakeholders, and regional industries, contributing to the overall advancement of science and technology initiatives across the country. This will allow DOST to expand its reach, improve program delivery, and provide more responsive, localized services to various sectors across the country. Strengthening the DOST Regional Offices to better implement and manage these key programs is essential in addressing the evolving needs of the local communities, industries, and research sectors. With enhanced capabilities at the regional level, DOST will be able to ensure more efficient program delivery, facilitate the adoption of science and technology innovations, and contribute to the overall progress of the country. Finally, the proposed strengthening of the regional offices will empower DOST to more effectively carry out its mandate of fostering inclusive and sustainable growth through science, technology, and innovation across the Philippines. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMO B. label: HB 10968
title: AN ACT GRANTING THE MISAMIS ORIENTAL II ELECTRIC SERVICE COOPERATIVE, INC. (MORESCO II), A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO THE END-USERS IN THE CITY OF GINGOOG AND THE MUNICIPALITIES OF MAGSAYSAY, MEDINA, TALISAYAN, BALINGOAN, KINOGUITAN, SUGBONGCOGON, BINUANGAN, SALAY, LAGONGLONG, BALINGASAG, AND CLAVERIA, ALL IN THE PROVINCE OF MISAMIS ORIENTAL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Misamis Oriental II Electric Service Cooperative, Inc. (MORESCO II) has been serving the eastern portion of the Province of Misamis Oriental for several decades. Incorporated and registered on October 1, 1976, MORESCO II has grown from its early rural electrification operations into a major distribution utility serving a geographically extensive and economically diverse area. This bill seeks to grant MORESCO II a franchise to construct, install, establish, operate, own, manage, and maintain a distribution system for the conveyance of electric power to end-users within the City of Gingoog and the Municipalities of Magsaysay, Medina, Talisayan, Balingoan, Kinoguitan, Sugbongcogon, Binuangan, Salay, Lagonglong, Balingasag, and Claveria, all in the Province of Misamis Oriental. MORESCO II presently serves a franchise area extending over approximately 1,800 square kilometers. Its service territory encompasses both urbanizing population centers and remote communities where access to electricity remains an important component of local development. The cooperative has approximately 123,699 registered member-consumers, with around 110,892 service connections, representing approximately 93% of potential household connections within its coverage area. The cooperative has also consistently attained a “Triple A” rating from the National Electrification Administration (NEA) and is classified as a Mega Large Electric Cooperative, reflecting its operational performance and institutional capability. Its continued efforts toward total electrification, modernization of its distribution system, improvement of consumer services, and strengthening of its financial and operational performance further demonstrate its continuing role in the development of the communities under its care. Granting MORESCO II a congressional franchise will provide the necessary statutory authority and institutional certainty for the cooperative to continue serving these communities, invest in the expansion and modernization of its distribution network, respond to increasing electricity demand, improve system reliability and resiliency, and pursue the electrification of remaining underserved and unserved areas. More importantly, the grant of this franchise recognizes that the provision of electricity is not merely a commercial undertaking but a public service imbued with public interest. MORESCO II is called upon to ensure that the benefits of electrification reach communities throughout its franchise area while remaining accountable to its member-consumer- owners and compliant with applicable laws, regulations, technical standards, and the requirements of government regulatory agencies. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SERGIO C. DAGOOC PRESLEY C. label: HB 10969
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INTEGRATION OF WEST PHILIPPINE SEA STUDIES INTO THE CURRICULA OF ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AT ALL LEVELS AND A NATIONWIDE INFORMATION AND AWARENESS CAMPAIGN
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize the teaching of the historical, legal, ecological, and socio-economic dimensions of the West Philippine Sea across all levels of the Philippine educational system, in keeping with Article II, Section 7 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution which provides that the State shall pursue an independent foreign policy, where the paramount considerations are national sovereignty, territorial integrity, national interest, and the right to self-determination. Furthermore, Article II, Section 13 mandates the State to promote the holistic well-being of the youth while inculcating in them patriotism and nationalism. The West Philippine Sea dispute is one of the most pressing foreign policy and national security issues facing the Philippines. At its core is the conflict between the Philippines' maritime entitlements and the People's Republic of China's sweeping claim over almost the entire West Philippine Sea (WPS), represented by the so-called "nine-dash line." While the Republic of the Philippines has fiercely asserted its sovereign rights over the West Philippine Sea on the global stage, the defense of the national territory must also take root in the minds of the Filipino people, most importantly the youth. Recent geopolitical developments have laid bare the urgent need for a unified, educated, and resolute citizenry. Our sovereignty continues to be challenged by aggressive and illegal foreign incursions in our Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). According to recent reports, the ongoing harassment of our uniformed personnel and fisherfolk remains a pressing national security issue. On July 20, 2026, a confrontation escalated at Ayungin Shoal when China Coast Guard personnel deployed a rigid-hull inflatable boat and struck a Philippine Navy sailor on the head with a wooden baton near the BRP Sierra Madre, leaving two Filipinos injured. Beyond physical confrontations, incidents such as the December 2025 targeting of Filipino civilian fishing boats with water cannons near Sabina Shoal highlight the escalating threat to the livelihoods of coastal communities. These relentless maritime incursions have caused a significant shift in public sentiment. A national survey released in July 2026 revealed that 64 percent of Filipinos now distrust China, a sharp increase driven by the continued harassment of Filipino personnel and the sweeping claims over the disputed waters. In response to these escalating threats, the Philippine government achieved a landmark legislative victory on November 7, 2024, when President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. signed the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, or Republic Act No. 12064. This law officially codified our maritime boundaries into domestic legislation, strictly aligning our territorial claims with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and the historic July 12, 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration Award. The passage of this law firmly established the legal framework for the Philippines to assert its sovereign rights to explore, exploit, and manage marine resources within its Exclusive Economic Zone. However, legislation and diplomatic protests alone cannot secure the waters. While public sentiment strongly favors the defense of the West Philippine Sea, there is a necessity to elevate this from reactionary emotion to a deep, factual, and legal understanding. True patriotism is rooted in knowledge. By mandating the Department of Education and the Commission on Higher Education to integrate West Philippine Sea Studies into basic and higher education, students will understand the significance of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the 2016 Arbitral Award, and the ecological and economic importance of the Exclusive Economic Zone. Furthermore, the measure provides continuous capacity-building for educators and drives nationwide public information campaigns through the Philippine Information Agency. To protect the West Philippine Sea is to protect the nation's future. By educating the youth, the State ensures that the legacy of our maritime heritage, the clarity of our legal rights, and the courage of those who defend our waters today will never be forgotten or surrendered by the generations of tomorrow. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTOLIN “LENLEN” A. label: HB 10972
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL-BASED PROGRAM FOR THE PREVENTION OF GUN VIOLENCE AND OTHER FORMS OF SERIOUS VIOLENCE AMONG LEARNERS AND STUDENTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Schools and other educational institutions must remain safe spaces where learners and students can learn and grow without fear of violence. However, recent incidents of gun violence in schools have emphasized the urgent need for stronger and coordinated measures to protect learners, students, teachers, faculty members, school administrators, and school personnel. On June 22, 2026, a shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City left three students dead and several others injured. Two minors were taken into custody in connection with the incident. 1 Police investigation later revealed that one of the firearms used was a police-issued handgun belonging to a relative of one of the minors, which raised serious concerns over access of minors to firearms. 2 Barely two months later, on August 18, 2026, another fatal shooting occurred at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University Junior High School, where two students died. Authorities recovered two firearms and it was found out that the student brought the firearms inside the school premises by taking them from his father's car and bypassing the main security entrance.3 The occurrence of two fatal school shootings within such a short period is a call to strengthen measures for the prevention of and preparedness for gun violence in schools across the country. An effective response must begin with prevention and early intervention by addressing factors that may place learners and students at risk of violence, providing appropriate mental health and psychosocial support, strengthening positive relationships, and establishing accessible mechanisms for reporting credible threats and unauthorized access to firearms. 1 Bonzo, L. T. (2026, June 22). Two minors allegedly linked to Tacloban school shooting now in police custody. GMA News Online. 2 Bonzo, L. T. (2026, June 22). 40 bullet shells, 1 police-issued handgun recovered at Tacloban school shooting. GMA News Online. 3 Casimiro, Q., De Guzman, K., Punzalan, J., & Villaruel, J. E. (2026, August 18). Two dead in Ateneo de Zamboanga shooting. ABS-CBN News; Consulta, J. (2026, August 23). The bag, the bullets, and the wake-up call: The moments before Ateneo de Zamboanga school shooting. GMA News Online. Likewise, schools and educational institutions must have appropriate measures to prevent and detect the unauthorized entry of firearms and other deadly weapons. Schools and their personnel must be equipped to recognize and report warning signs, coordinate with law enforcement and emergency responders, and implement appropriate protective measures during an armed threat. This bill seeks to establish a Comprehensive School Gun Violence Prevention Program applicable to public and private basic education institutions and public and private higher education institutions throughout the country. The Department of Education (DepEd) and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), within their respective jurisdictions, shall oversee the implementation of the Program. The Program shall strengthen school-based prevention and early intervention strategies, firearm-related threat reporting, school and community partnerships, appropriate school safety infrastructure, personnel training and capacity building, emergency preparedness and response, and crisis and post-incident recovery. Every learner and student has the right to pursue education in a safe and secure environment. The recent tragedies serve as a reminder that the State must act proactively to strengthen the capacity of schools and educational institutions to prevent gun violence and protect the lives and well-being of learners and school personnel. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. EMILIO BERNARDINO L. label: HB 10973
title: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 6 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1271, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED “AN ACT NULLIFYING DECREES OF REGISTRATION AND CERTIFICATES OF TITLE COVERING LANDS WITHIN THE BAGUIO TOWNSITE RESERVATION ISSUED IN CIVIL RESERVATION CASE NO. 1, GLRO RECORD NO. 211 PURSUANT TO REPUBLIC ACT NO. 913, AS AMENDED, BUT CONSIDERING AS VALID CERTAIN TITLES OF SUCH LANDS THAT ARE ALIENABLE AND DISPOSABLE UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”, TO LOCALIZE THE COMPOSITION OF THE VALIDATION COMMITTEE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Presidential Decree No. 1271, as amended, was enacted to provide a mechanism for the validation of certain land titles issued covering lands within the Baguio Townsite Reservation. It recognized that, despite the nullification of decrees of registration and certificates of titles issued pursuant to Republic Act. No. 931, as amended, equity and fairness demanded that titles over lands which are alienable and disposable and which satisfied the requirements of the said law be afforded an opportunity for validation. The reglementary period of availing validation started in March 1978. It was extended by Presidential Decree No. 1651 and Presidential Decree No. 2034 and eventually expired in February 1987. Numerous petitions for validation were filed within the reglementary period, of which not less than two thousand six hundred thirteen (2,613) have not been acted upon and remain unresolved to this day. As a result, many petitioners and their successors-in -interest continue to suffer from uncertainty regarding the status of their properties, adversely affecting the exercise of property rights, the transfer and development of land, and the orderly administration of land ownership within the Baguio Townsite Reservation. One of the factors contributing to the delay is the present composition of the Validation Committee, which composed of the Secretary of Justice, the Solicitor General, and the Director of the Land Management Bureau, coupled with the absence of a specific budgetary allocation for the Committee to support the discharge of its functions. There is no question as to the competence, expertise, and dedication of these officials in the discharge of their respective duties, however, the Department of Justice, the Office of the Solicitor General, and the Land Management Bureau under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, are each entrusted with broad and demanding national mandates and are continuously confronted with numerous and important governmental responsibilities requiring their immediate attention. Consequently, the members of the present Validation Committee are necessarily called upon to attend to numerous other official functions in addition to their responsibilities under PD 1271. The situation makes it difficult for them to devote sufficient time and attention to the substantial number of petitions for validation pending before the Committee. While the existing composition may have been appropriate at the time the Decree was issued, the experience of its implementation demonstrates the need for a more accessible and responsive mechanism that can devote focused attention to the resolution of these long-pending petitions. The proposed localization of the Validation Committee is therefore not intended to diminish or question the competence of its present members. Rather, it seeks to complement their expertise by entrusting the validation function to local officials who are physically and institutionally closer to the properties, records, petitioners, and other stakeholders directly affected by the proceedings. Considering that the subject properties, records, and government offices directly involved in the validation process are principally located in Baguio City, it is both practical and efficient to constitute a localized Validation Committee composed, among others, of the Regional Director of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources- Cordillera Administrative Region, The City Mayor of Baguio City, the Community Environment and Natural Resources Officer (CENRO), the Baguio City Legal Officer, together with other appropriate members whose functions and expertise are relevant to the validation of the subject land titles. A localized Committee will be in a better position to undertake the necessary evaluation of petitions, coordinate with concerned government agencies, examine records and technical documents, and conduct such proceedings as may be necessary for the proper disposition of the petitions. More importantly, it will provide a mechanism through which long-pending petitions may be addressed with greater focus, accessibility, and administrative efficiency. This proposed measure therefore seeks to amend Section 6 of Presidential Decree No. 1271, as amended, by reconstituting and localizing the Validation Committee. The passage of this measure will help bring long-overdue resolution to the numerous petitions for validation that have remained pending for many years, promote the orderly and efficient administration of lands within the Baguio Townsite Reservation, and strengthen the government’s commitment to ensuring a fair, accessible, and expeditious validation process. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MAURICIO G. label: HB 10979
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CAMPUS OF THE SURIGAO DEL NORTE STATE UNIVERSITY IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF ALEGRIA, PROVINCE OF SURIGAO DEL NORTE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Under Section 1, Article XIV of the 1987 Constitution, the State is mandated to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all. Furthermore, Section 2 (1) of the same Article provides that the State shall establish, maintain, and support a complete, adequate, and integrated system of education relevant to the needs of the people and society. Access to quality, affordable, and relevant higher education remains a fundamental driver of local development and inclusive growth. In the Province of Surigao del Norte, many deserving students, particularly those from geographically isolated and economically disadvantaged areas continue to face financial and logistical challenges in pursuing tertiary education. The establishment of a campus of the Surigao del Norte State University (SNSU) in the Municipality of Alegria seeks to address these barriers by bringing quality instruction, research, and extension services closer to the people. As a state university mandated to provide advanced education, technological and professional instruction, and to promote research and community engagement, SNSU plays a vital role in the socio-economic development of the province and the Caraga Region. The proposed SNSU Alegria Campus will expand access to degree and non-degree programs aligned with local development priorities, including agriculture, fisheries, environmental sustainability, tourism, entrepreneurship, and emerging technologies. It will likewise serve as a hub for skills training, innovation, and community-based research responsive to the needs of local industries and stakeholders. By establishing this campus, the State affirms its constitutional commitment to make quality education accessible to all and to promote equitable opportunities for lifelong learning. The measure is envisioned to empower the youth, strengthen the local workforce, stimulate economic activity, and contribute to long-term regional progress. Moreover, the institutional recognition of SNSU Alegria Campus through legislation would provide a legal basis for regular national funding and infrastructure development, support the expansion of academic offerings aligned with local industry and regional development goals, and ensure operational stability, staffing, and long-term sustainability of the campus. The establishment will promote inclusive growth and development which will encourage the expansion of its services and facilities to provide quality education to more students and will give wider latitude to learning. This legislative measure is consistent with the provisions of Republic Act No. 8292, otherwise known as the “Higher Education Modernization Act of 1997” and aims to promote the State’s policy to provide access to quality tertiary education for all. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE S. label: HB 10980
title: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11982, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “NEW PHILIPPINE PASSPORT ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine passport is a primary document that confirms an individual’s citizenship and identity. As such, it is critical to ensure that only genuine Filipino citizens are granted the privilege of holding a Philippine passport. However, the increasing cases of foreigners fraudulently acquiring Philippine passports through fake birth certificates or improperly documented Delayed Registration of Live Birth highlight a loophole in the current system. The Philippine Passport Law, as it stands, provides insufficient safeguards against the fraudulent acquisition of passports by individuals who exploit the less stringent requirements for applicants using Delayed Registration of Live Birth. This issue compromises the integrity of our passport system and tarnishes the reputation of the Philippine government in the international community. To address this concern, the proposed legislation seeks to amend the existing Philippine Passport Law by mandating additional documentary requirements for applicants using Delayed Registration of Live Birth. These additional safeguards aim to uphold the integrity of the Philippine passport and ensure that it is issued only to bona fide Filipino citizens. By requiring independent attestations and clearances from various agencies, this measure provides a robust mechanism to prevent the misuse of delayed birth registrations for fraudulent purposes. Furthermore, this legislation is a proactive response to the growing global security concerns and the need for stronger border control mechanisms. It aligns with the government’s commitment to protecting the sanctity of Philippine citizenship and safeguarding the trust placed in our passport by international authorities. In light of these considerations, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. BERNADETTE S. label: HB 10981
title: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7898, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10349, BY REVITALIZING THE REVISED AFP MODERNIZATION PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 6 of Republic Act No. 7898, as amended by Section 2 of Republic Act No. 10349, fixed the period of implementation of the Revised AFP Modernization Program at 15 years from the approval of the amendatory Act on December 11, 2012. The Program will therefore lapse on December 11, 2027. In January 2024, the President approved Re-Horizon 3, the revised acquisition plan for the third and final phase of the Program, carrying a 10-year implementation period and an estimated cost of ₱2 trillion. Acquisitions scheduled under that plan extend to 2034, seven years beyond the date on which the authority to undertake them expires. Article II, Section 3 of the 1987 Constitution constitutes the Armed Forces of the Philippines as the protector of the people and the State, and charges it with securing the sovereignty of the State and the integrity of the national territory. That mandate is stated without limitation as to period. The 15-year term in Section 6 was a drafting choice made in 2012, when the horizon it set exceeded the horizon of the acquisitions then contemplated. This measure repeals Section 6 and allows the Program to continue as a standing undertaking, subject as it already is to annual appropriation and to congressional review. The scheduled lapse is also inconsistent with Republic Act No. 12024, the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Revitalization Act, signed on October 8, 2024, which directs the Department of National Defense to develop a domestic defense industry through fiscal incentives and government-backed financing for local manufacturers. Investment of that kind is recovered over production runs measured in years. A supplier deciding whether to establish a line in the Philippines must assess the demand of its principal customer, and the statutory authority of that customer presently ends in 2027. Sustaining the industrial policy adopted in RA 12024 requires sustaining the procurement authority against which it was designed. 1 The financing mechanism requires attention as well. Under the General Appropriations Act for Fiscal Year 2025, the Program was allotted ₱75 billion, of which ₱35 billion was programmed and ₱40 billion was carried as unprogrammed appropriations, releasable only upon collection of revenue in excess of the fiscal program. Unprogrammed appropriations carry no assured source of funds, and a contract for a multi-year acquisition cannot prudently be executed against them. Major platforms such as frigates, aircraft, and missile systems are procured as single indivisible items whose payment schedules span several fiscal years, and where the appropriation cannot cover the schedule the acquisition is deferred rather than reduced. Section 3 of this measure addresses that constraint. It authorizes the President and Commander-in-Chief to contract loans, credits, and indebtedness, including supplier’s credit and deferred payment arrangements, and to conclude bilateral agreements for other forms of financial assistance, for projects under the Program. The authority is subject to conditions drawn from existing practice in other capital programs: the project plans must first be prepared by the Department of National Defense and approved by the President, and the Secretary of Budget and Management must certify both that funds for the fiscal year in question are appropriated and programmed to service the external debt of the public sector, including the obligation proposed to be contracted, and that the counterpart peso funding requirement has been programmed and will be available as and when needed for the completion of the project. Section 2 exempts the importation by the AFP of defense equipment under the Program from value-added tax and customs duties. Such duties and taxes are paid out of the Program’s own appropriation and returned to the National Treasury, producing no net revenue for the government while reducing the quantity of materiel the appropriation is able to procure. The exemption keeps that amount within the Program, where it can be applied to additional platforms, to the sustainment of assets already in service, and to the readiness of the personnel who operate them. This measure does not increase the appropriation for the Program, prescribe its acquisition list, or alter the role of Congress in reviewing either. It removes a terminal date, provides a financing instrument suited to the length of the acquisition cycle, and relieves the Program of a tax paid from one government account to another. Decisions on the scale and content of modernization remain with Congress, to be made through the annual budget process rather than settled by the expiry of a provision enacted in 2012. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. BELLA VANESSA B.
