label: HB 11051
title: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH FAIR AND INCLUSIVE CREDIT REPORTING MECHANISMS TO ENSURE EQUITABLE CREDIT ACCESS TO THE MOST VULNERABLE SECTORS OF SOCIETY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to affordable and formal credit remains out of reach for millions of Filipinos, particularly those without an established credit history, such as informal sector workers, farmers, fisherfolk, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Financial institutions play a central role in closing this gap, and the growing availability of alternative and digital transaction data presents new opportunities to responsibly assess the creditworthiness of previously underserved borrowers. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has itself recognized the value of alternative data, such as mobile, utility, and online transaction data, in painting a more complete picture of a borrower’s creditworthiness, allowing more individuals and businesses, especially those with thin or no credit files, to be assessed for credit. Realizing this potential, however, requires that credit scoring models built on such data remain accurate, fair, and free from undue bias against the very sectors they are meant to serve. Given BSP’s immediate action in ensuring liquidity in the economy through decreased lending rates and reserve requirement during the COVID-19 Pandemic, the pressure is on for banks to operationalize such measures post- pandemic and continue to normalize such practice. While the intention of the government is to provide support, banks would need to immediately scale their operations to manage worsening credit positions of existing borrowers and accommodate possible increase in new credit due to lowered interest rates.1 The lack of alternatives and exclusionary mechanisms of financial credit scoring systems have led many FIlipinos to resort to more expensive, poorly- supervised, and potentially illegal lending operations that impose abusive 1 https://www.pwc.com/ph/en/business-unusual/banks-approach-to-covid-19.html interest rates and practice predatory lending activities, to the detriment of many disadvantaged and underprivileged sectors of the society. The lack of alternatives and exclusionary mechanisms of financial credit scoring systems have led many FIlipinos to resort to more expensive, poorly- supervised, and potentially illegal lending operations that impose abusive interest rates and practice predatory lending activities, to the detriment of many disadvantaged and underprivileged sectors of the society. This bill seeks to encourage the development of non-traditional approaches to credit scoring, with the aim of including more sectors of the society that have been excluded under more conventional and traditional approaches. With a fairer and more inclusive approach to credit scoring, more members of the agriculture sector, MSMEs, informal sector, and other vulnerable groups will be able to access more affordable credit that proactively enables them to engage in more productive economic activities. This Act specifically mandates a credit inclusiveness study to determine whether conventional credit scoring techniques exclude specific segments and sectors of the society; grants the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) clear regulatory oversight of credit scoring methods; requires a regular review of credit scoring models to assess their inclusivity; and allows the BSP to prohibit credit scoring models that are deemed to be unduly exclusionary. Finally, this bill responds to the continuing need to translate financial system liquidity into credit in the real economy, particularly for sectors that remain underserved by conventional credit scoring systems. Through this, more Filipinos will be able to engage in productive economic activity that will help sustain and broaden the country’s economic growth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11052
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES AT THE LEVEL OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Constitution makes it the State’s responsibility to “protect and promote the right to health of the people” and to “instill health consciousness among them. Acting upon this, in 2018, Republic Act No 11036 (“Mental Health Act”) was passed, which, in Section 3 thereof, bound the State to the following objectives: SECTION 3. Objectives. — The objectives of this Act are as follows: (a) Strengthen effective leadership and governance for mental health by, among others, formulating, developing, and implementing national policies, strategies, programs, and regulations relating to mental health; (b) Develop and establish a comprehensive, integrated, effective, and efficient national mental health care system responsive to the psychiatric, neurologic, and psychosocial needs of the Filipino people; (c) Protect the rights and freedoms of persons with psychiatric, neurologic, and psychosocial health needs; (d) Strengthen information systems, evidence and research for mental health; (e) Integrate mental health care in the basic health services; and (f) Integrate strategies promoting mental health in educational institutions, the workplace, and in communities. It is in furtherance of these policies and commitments that this Bill is proposed. This Bill aims to put into place barangay mental health workers and city/municipal mental health professionals. The barangay mental health workers, in particular, shall (1) maintain close contact with those most in need of mental health services and (2) take charge of building community awareness of, thereby boosting the accessibility of, the government’s mental health services. It is for the foregoing premises that the approval of this Bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11053
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE VALUE-ADDED TAX EXEMPTION FOR PRESCRIBED DRUGS AND MEDICINES FOR MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 109 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution provides as a policy that the State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.1 This policy covers all aspects of health vital to every Filipino’s well-being. The importance of mental health has received increasing recognition in recent years, and in line with the state policy abovementioned, Congress passed Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as “Mental Health Act” in 2018. To fully realize the essence of the Mental Health Act, and in recognition of the fact that Republic Act No. 11534, otherwise known as the “CREATE Act,” has already exempted the sale or importation of prescription drugs and medicines for mental illness from value-added tax (VAT) effective January 1, 2021 under Secion 109 (1)(AA)(ii) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC), this bill seeks to strengthen and clarify the scope of the said exemption by alighing coverage with the broader definition of “mental health condition” under the Mental Health Act. Absent a sufficiently broad and unamibigious definition, prescribed medicies for anxiety, depression, and other conditions recognized under the Mental Health Act risk being excluded from the existing VAT exemption if the term “mental illness” is narrowly construed. VAT is a tax on consumption levied on the sale, barter, exchange or lease of goods and services.2 It is an indirect tax which is often shifted or passed on to the buyer of the goods or services. In cases 1 1987 CONST., art. II, sec. 15. 2 Bureau of Internal Revenue. Value-Added Tax. of mental health conditions, it is the patient who will bear the burden of the value-added tax. This bill aims to remove this burden and makes prescribed mental health medicines more accessible to those who need it. After all, mental health conditions affect both the rich and the poor, and the poor are less capable of addressing this concern due to financial constraints. In light of these circumstances, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11054
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A BASIC EDUCATION SCHOOLS SAFETY FRAMEWORK TO ENSURE THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF STUDENTS AND SCHOOL WORKERS ALIKE, PROVIDING FOR FUNDING, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The strings of violent incidents that occurred in schools at various times and points in the country have rocked consciousness and have instilled unnecessary anxiety amongst students, parents, guardians, and school personnel alike. Violent school incidents that we used to hear from foreign news updates and which seemed to be light years away from us suddenly became real and chilling. With the advent and proliferation of various cyber-technological applications that promote or foster unhealthy fanaticism and individualism, violence, self-harm, hate and other extreme expressions of emotions, some unknowing and misguided young Filipino students have fallen victims of their own unguarded psyche, leaving in their path a trail of snuffed out lives, physiological damages, moral injuries, and destruction to properties in institutions that are supposed to be zones of peace and development and havens of learnings and education. There is a need for the government to immediately intervene in order to prevent the violent scenarios of recent from turning into common scenes. Gun violence, extreme physical harm, destruction of properties, and campus threats cannot be accepted as an ordinary part of Philippine school life. Moreover, while the Department of Education has launched a nationwide school safety campaign, the nationalization of basic education has thrust support to education services such as security personnel, equipment, and infrastructure into the already overly burdened coffers of the local government unit. The MOOE of schools may be used for this purpose, but schools prioritize allocating their meager MOOE allotment for school and office supplies, and similar expenditures. Thus, given the mandate of the Department of Education “to protect and promote the right of every Filipino to quality, equitable, culture-based, and complete basic education, which includes creating an enabling and supportive learning environment where learners are protected and secured from any form of harm, abuse, and violence within and under its jurisdiction,” there is a need for Congress to pass a law that institutionalize basic education schools safety framework to ensure the safety and well-being of students and school workers alike and to providing for funding. Schools need permanent funding to upgrade physical defenses and to hire security personnel. If the government wishes not to witness another violent incident in schools such as those that happened in Zamboanga City and Tacloban, then it must provide for mechanisms to prevent the same from happening. In view of the foregoing premises, approval of this measure is earnestly sought. ESMAEL G. label: HB 11058
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY FRAMEWORK, ENSURING THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF LEARNERS AND SCHOOL PERSONNEL, AND PROMOTING A SAFE AND SUPPORTIVE SCHOOL COMMUNITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The school is supposed to be one of the safest places in a child's life—a place where learners acquire knowledge, develop character, build friendships, and prepare for their future. Yet recent events demonstrate that Filipino schools are facing increasingly complex threats to the safety and well-being of learners, teachers, and other school personnel. The need for a comprehensive and institutionalized school safety framework has become especially urgent following a series of violent incidents in and around Philippine schools. On June 22, 2026, a shooting occurred inside San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, resulting in the deaths of three students and injuries to several others. The Commission on Human Rights confirmed the deaths of the three students and noted that the incident involved minors aged 14 and 15. Subsequent police reports indicated that the attack had allegedly been planned for more than a month. The incident prompted heightened security measures in Tacloban schools, including stricter entry protocols and bag inspections. The gravity of the incident was underscored by the fact that the alleged perpetrators were themselves minors. This demonstrates that school violence cannot be addressed solely through guards, gates, and post-incident police investigations. There is a need for early identification of risks, effective reporting mechanisms, mental health and psychosocial support, learner formation, violence prevention, proper referral systems, and coordinated intervention among schools, families, communities, and government agencies. Barely two months later, on August 18, 2026, another deadly school shooting occurred at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University Junior High School in Zamboanga City. According to the Department of the Interior and Local Government, a Grade 9 student entered the school carrying a pistol and a rifle, fired at another student, and subsequently took his own life. A Grade 10 student was killed, while other students were reportedly injured. The incident was reportedly livestreamed, raising additional concerns regarding the intersection of school violence, firearms, social media, and the digital environment in which young people increasingly live. These incidents are not isolated. Reports have also documented other forms of violence occurring within or in connection with schools. In 2025, a student in Nueva Ecija was reportedly shot by her former boyfriend inside a school, while in Lanao del Sur, a teacher was shot and killed inside a school after a student reportedly received a failing grade. In 2023, a medical technology student in Tuguegarao City was reportedly beaten and shot by a classmate at a university parking area. Even prior to the Tacloban tragedy, the Department of the Interior and Local Government noted two separate stabbing incidents involving students in schools in Cavite, emphasizing the need to strengthen school safety, early intervention, and community-based violence prevention. Taken together, these incidents reveal that threats to school safety are not limited to one particular type of violence. They may involve firearms, knives and other weapons, bullying, interpersonal conflicts, abuse, harassment, mental health concerns, online influence, cyberbullying, and other emerging threats. The increasing use of digital platforms further complicates the situation, as harmful content and incidents of violence can spread rapidly among young people. Recent national efforts to strengthen online child-safety measures likewise reflect growing concerns about the digital environment surrounding Filipino children and adolescents. The response to school violence must therefore go beyond reacting after an incident has already occurred. At present, various laws, policies, and programs already address particular aspects of learner protection, anti-bullying, mental health, disaster preparedness, child protection, and school security. However, these mechanisms must operate as part of a coordinated and comprehensive system. Schools need clear standards on prevention, risk assessment, reporting, emergency response, case management, referral, recovery, digital safety, infrastructure, security, and the protection and well- being of school personnel. This proposed measure seeks to establish such a system through a National Comprehensive School Safety Framework and require every school to develop and regularly update a School Safety Plan and School Safety Handbook appropriate to its circumstances and risk profile. The proposed measure also recognizes that school safety is not merely a security issue. A truly safe school must address the physical, mental, emotional, psychosocial, and digital well-being of learners and school personnel. It must provide mechanisms for early intervention before conflicts escalate into violence. It must ensure that learners have safe avenues to report bullying, threats, abuse, harassment, and other concerns. It must provide appropriate mental health and psychosocial support to those affected by violence and trauma. It must likewise establish clear coordination among school officials, parents, local government units, law enforcement, health and social welfare agencies, and other stakeholders. The bill further provides for appropriate school safety personnel, security and protective measures, emergency and life-safety equipment, visitor management, risk assessment, emergency drills, digital safety policies, learner well-being programs, incident reporting, case management, referral systems, recovery and reintegration programs, and protection and support for school personnel. Importantly, the measure adopts a prevention-oriented approach. The objective is not simply to make schools more difficult to enter or to increase security after a tragedy. label: HB 11059
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10742, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN REFORM ACT OF 2015,” AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11768, PROVIDING FOR THE APPOINTMENT OF SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN MEMBERS TO FILL PERMANENT VACANCIES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) is an important institution for ensuring the participation of the youth in local governance. Through the SK, young Filipinos are given the opportunity to represent their fellow youth and participate in the formulation and implementation of programs and policies in their communities. However, vacancies in the Sangguniang Kabataan continue to occur for various reasons. These include positions that remain unfilled after elections, as well as vacancies arising from resignation, death, removal from office, permanent incapacity, failure to qualify, and other circumstances recognized by law. Under Republic Act No. 10742, as amended by Republic Act No. 11768, vacancies in the SK membership are generally filled through a special Katipunan ng Kabataan assembly and election. The number of unfilled positions after the 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections demonstrates that the issue is not merely theoretical. Following the 2023 elections, 692 SK positions nationwide remained vacant because there were no candidates for those positions—139 SK Chairperson positions and 553 SK Member positions. The Commission on Elections subsequently had to provide rules for the conduct of special elections to address these vacancies. More importantly, vacancies do not occur only immediately after an election. During the term of office, an SK position may become vacant because of resignation, death, permanent incapacity, removal from office, failure to qualify, or other circumstances. These vacancies can leave an SK with fewer members than required and may affect its ability to meet quorum, deliberate on matters, and effectively implement programs for the youth. The existing requirement of a special election or special Katipunan ng Kabataan assembly may also result in delays in filling a vacant position. Conducting a separate electoral process for a single vacant seat requires coordination, administrative preparation, and resources, while the vacant position may remain unfilled during the process. This measure therefore proposes a simpler and more efficient mechanism for filling permanent vacancies in the membership of the Sangguniang Kabataan. Instead of conducting a special election for every vacancy, the remaining members of the Sangguniang Kabataan shall recommend a qualified member of the Katipunan ng Kabataan to fill the vacant position. The recommendation shall be submitted through a duly approved SK Resolution to the concerned City or Municipal Mayor, who shall make the appointment. This proposed mechanism is similar to the general approach under the Local Government Code in filling permanent vacancies in local sanggunian, while still preserving the participation of the youth sector in identifying the person who will represent them. The proposed appointment shall be limited to the unexpired portion of the term, and the appointee must possess all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications prescribed by law. The measure also provides a definite period for the SK to submit its recommendation to ensure that vacancies will not remain unfilled for an extended period. The objective of this measure is simple: to ensure that every Sangguniang Kabataan remains complete, functional, and capable of serving the youth of the barangay. By replacing the requirement of a special election with a timely appointment upon the recommendation of the SK Council and approval of the concerned Mayor, this measure will reduce administrative delays, avoid unnecessary electoral expenses, and ensure continuity in youth representation and governance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 11061
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FREE FREIGHT SERVICES IN THE TRANSPORTATION OF RELIEF GOODS TO CALAMITY-STRICKEN AREAS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is one of the countries most vulnerable to natural hazards. According to the World Risk Index, the Philippines has consistently ranked among the countries with the highest disaster risk in the world. The 2024 World Risk Index ranked the Philippines first among 193 countries, underscoring the country's continuing exposure to typhoons, floods, earthquakes, landslides, and other hazards. The frequency and scale of disasters place a significant burden on government and humanitarian organizations. The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) regularly report millions of Filipinos affected by major typhoons and other disasters each year. In these situations, the timely delivery of food, water, medicines, and other essential supplies is critical. Yet transportation and freight costs remain a practical obstacle, particularly in geographically isolated and severely affected communities. Resources that should go directly to relief operations are instead spent on transporting donated goods. This measure seeks to provide free freight services for relief goods intended for calamity-stricken areas, subject to proper government coordination and verification. By reducing or eliminating transportation costs, the measure will enable government agencies, local government units, humanitarian organizations, and legitimate donors to deliver more assistance, faster, to families affected by disasters. In times of calamity, relief should not be delayed because of freight costs. Every available resource must be directed toward saving lives, protecting communities, and helping affected families recover. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 11066
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE AUTOMATIC PENSION ESCALATION MECHANISM FOR RETIREMENT, DISABILITY, DEATH, AND SURVIVOR PENSIONERS OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM (SSS), PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Retirement should provide security and dignity to those who have spent their productive years contributing to the Social Security System (SSS). Yet, the purchasing power of pensions can gradually decline as the cost of food, healthcare, utilities, and other basic necessities increases. Without a predictable mechanism for periodic adjustment, pensioners may find it increasingly difficult to meet their daily needs. The SSS has recognized the need to improve pension adequacy through its pension reform initiatives, including increases for retirement, disability, death, and survivor pensioners. These measures demonstrate the importance of providing pensioners with meaningful and predictable adjustments while taking into account the long-term sustainability of the Social Security Fund. This measure seeks to institutionalize an automatic pension escalation mechanism so that pension increases will no longer depend solely on periodic administrative action or discretionary adjustments. Under the proposed measure, retirement and disability pensioners shall receive an annual increase of ten percent (10%) or the official annual average inflation rate, whichever is higher, while death and survivor pensioners shall receive an annual increase of five percent (5%) or the official annual average inflation rate, whichever is higher. The adjustment shall be applied to the pension in effect immediately prior to the adjustment and shall be compounded annually. The ten percent (10%) and five percent (5%) rates are intended not merely to offset inflation but also to improve pension adequacy and provide a predictable minimum annual enhancement to pension income The proposed mechanism provides pensioners with a predictable minimum increase while protecting the purchasing power of their pensions against higher inflation. At the same time, the measure does not diminish any existing pension benefit or increase granted under existing law. Recognizing the importance of maintaining the long-term viability of the SSS, the measure requires an annual actuarial valuation and review of the Social Security Fund. The review will assess the financial impact of the pension escalation and consider contribution collections, investment income, membership growth, demographic trends, reserves, and other factors affecting the Fund. It will also provide Congress and the Department of Finance with timely information necessary to ensure the continued sustainability of the pension system. The measure further provides for a periodic Congressional review every five (5) years, allowing Congress to assess the adequacy of pension benefits in light of prevailing economic and demographic conditions while ensuring the long-term sustainability of the Social Security Fund. Through this measure, pensioners are provided with a fair, predictable, and inflation-responsive mechanism for maintaining the value of their pensions, while preserving the financial integrity of the SSS. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11067
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY AND WEAPON PREVENTION PROGRAM, MANDATING THE COLLABORATIVE IMPLEMENTATION OF PREVENTIVE MEASURES BY THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AND BARANGAYS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The safety and security of learners, teachers, and school personnel are essential to the delivery of quality education. Schools must remain safe and secure environments where children can learn, develop, and participate in school activities free from the threat of firearms, weapons, violence, and other preventable dangers. The increasing complexity of school security concerns calls for a comprehensive and preventive approach. While existing laws, regulations, and Department of Education policies provide important safeguards, there is a need to institutionalize a coordinated framework that brings together schools, families, local government units, barangays, law enforcement agencies, and social welfare institutions. This measure, to be known as the “S.A.F.E. (Secure and Firearm-Free Education) Schools Act,” seeks to establish such a framework. It recognizes that school safety cannot depend solely on security personnel or law enforcement after an incident has occurred. Prevention, early identification of threats, responsible reporting, appropriate intervention, and secure school environments must form part of a unified school safety system. The bill directs the Department of Education to establish national standards for school access control, security risk assessments, an Anonymous Digital Tip Line, behavioral threat assessment, conflict resolution, peace education, and de-escalation training. It likewise requires public and private basic education institutions to adopt appropriate access- control procedures, reasonable security inspections, parental engagement, incident reporting, and environmental safety measures. The measure further strengthens the participation of local government units and barangays by providing for appropriate support for school security infrastructure, community coordination, school-zone safety, and preventive patrols. These measures are intended to complement, and not replace, the responsibilities of national government agencies and school authorities. Recognizing that children require a distinct and protective approach, the bill expressly provides that interventions involving minors shall be undertaken in accordance with Republic Act No. 9344, otherwise known as the “Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006,” and other applicable child- protection laws and regulations. The objective is not merely to punish misconduct, but to prevent violence while ensuring that children are afforded appropriate intervention, rehabilitation, counseling, and family support. The bill also promotes safe and responsible reporting of weapons and threats through confidential or anonymous mechanisms and encourages schools to establish controlled procedures for the voluntary surrender of prohibited items. These measures are intended to provide students with a safe avenue to prevent dangerous incidents before they occur, without diminishing accountability under existing laws. At the same time, the proposed framework recognizes the importance of privacy, dignity, due process, and the protection of personal information. Security measures must therefore be implemented in a manner that is reasonable, non-discriminatory, child-sensitive, and consistent with existing laws on data privacy and the rights and welfare of children. Ultimately, the S.A.F.E. Schools Act seeks to institutionalize a whole- of-community approach to school safety. By combining prevention, physical security, early intervention, responsible reporting, community participation, and child-sensitive measures, this Act aims to ensure that every school in the country remains a secure and supportive environment conducive to learning. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11068
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL DISABILITY SUPPORT ALLOWANCE PROGRAM AS A SOCIAL PROTECTION AND SUPPORT MEASURE TO PROMOTE THE INDEPENDENT LIVING, EMPOWERMENT, EQUAL PARTICIPATION, AND FULL INCLUSION OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES IN SOCIETY, PROVIDING FOR A REGULAR DISABILITY SUPPORT ALLOWANCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Persons with disabilities continue to face significant barriers to full and effective participation in society. Beyond the challenges arising from their impairments, many persons with disabilities incur additional costs for transportation, personal assistance, medicines, rehabilitation, assistive devices and technologies, education, communication, and other disability-related needs. These additional costs can increase household expenses, limit opportunities for education and employment, and contribute to poverty, exclusion, and inequality. While existing laws and social protection programs provide important benefits and assistance to persons with disabilities, these measures do not always adequately address the recurring extra costs associated with disability. There is therefore a need for a targeted and disability-responsive social protection measure that directly assists persons with disabilities in meeting such costs and supports their independent living, economic security, and full participation in society. This measure seeks to establish a National Disability Support Allowance Program (DSAP) that will provide a regular Disability Support Allowance of at least Two Thousand Pesos (₱2,000.00) per month to eligible persons with disabilities. The allowance shall be periodically reviewed and adjusted to preserve its purchasing power and shall complement, rather than replace or diminish, existing benefits and privileges granted under other laws. The proposed measure adopts a phased implementation to ensure that the Program can be progressively expanded in accordance with available resources and administrative capacity. The initial phase prioritizes children with disabilities and adults with significant disabilities, followed by persons with moderate disabilities and, ultimately, other eligible persons with disabilities who incur disability-related extra costs. Eligibility shall be determined through a Disability and Needs Assessment System (DNAS) that takes into account functional limitations, support requirements, disability-related extra costs, and barriers to participation. The measure further seeks to improve coordination and data management among relevant government agencies through a Disability Management Information System (DMIS), while ensuring compliance with applicable data privacy and information security laws. The measure also strengthens accessibility in the application and payment of benefits, establishes a clear appeal and grievance mechanism, provides safeguards against fraudulent registration and misuse of benefits, and requires regular monitoring and periodic evaluation of the Program. This bill is filed as the House counterpart measure to Senate Bill No. 2386, which seeks to establish a National Disability Support Allowance Program for persons with disabilities. While maintaining the core objectives and framework of the Senate measure, this proposed House version further clarifies the coverage and phased implementation, strengthens eligibility and assessment procedures, protects existing benefits, improves payment and appeal mechanisms, reinforces data privacy safeguards, and promotes greater accountability and transparency in implementation. The enactment of this measure will strengthen the country's social protection framework for persons with disabilities and affirm the State's commitment to ensuring that disability-related costs do not become a barrier to dignity, independence, equal participation, and full inclusion in society. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11069
title: AN ACT EXPANDING PHILHEALTH COVERAGE TO INCLUDE BENEFIT PACKAGE FOR ALL MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The proposed bill addresses a critical gap in the Philippine healthcare system by treating mental health care not as an expensive luxury, but as a fundamental human right. While existing legislation recognizes the importance of mental well-being, the prohibitive costs of psychiatric evaluation, psychological services, neurological services, and long-term treatment prevent millions of Filipinos from seeking essential care. By explicitly mandating the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) to develop and implement a comprehensive benefit package within one year of its effectivity, this bill removes the financial barriers that have historically marginalized individuals with mental health conditions. This measure requires coverage for all mental health disorders, extending specific protections to minors, and incorporating emergency interventions, continuing care, and evidence-based services alongside the World Health Organization’s Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP). Furthermore, this bill strengthens the legal and financial frameworks necessary to sustain nationwide mental healthcare. It aligns national policy with international human rights standards and with Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as the “Mental Health Act,” while explicitly recognizing individuals with mental health conditions under the protections of the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons (RA 7277) to curb systemic stigma and discrimination. Rather than creating a new budgetary burden, the Act utilizes PhilHealth’s existing revenue structure, funding the package through a combination of direct contributor premiums and government subsidies for indirect contributors. PhilHealth shall undertake the necessary actuarial and financial assessment to ensure that the benefit package is sustainable and appropriately integrated into its existing benefit structure. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11070
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE INSTALLATION OF BEHIND-THE-METER ELECTRICITY GENERATION AND ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "ELECTRIC POWER INDUSTRY REFORM ACT OF 2001”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face the challenges of high electricity costs, grid congestion, energy security, and the need to accelerate the adoption of renewable energy and energy storage technologies. Behind-the-meter electricity generation and energy storage systems, including rooftop solar photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems, enable households, businesses, and other electricity end-users to generate and store electricity primarily for their own consumption. These systems can reduce dependence on electricity supplied through the distribution system, improve energy resilience, and contribute to the reduction of system losses and peak demand. Existing regulatory and administrative requirements, however, may unnecessarily increase the cost and delay the installation of such systems, particularly where the system is designed and equipped to prevent the export of electricity to the distribution system. This Act seeks to remove unnecessary regulatory and administrative barriers while preserving legitimate electrical, structural, fire, environmental, and public safety requirements. It distinguishes between behind-the-meter systems that are incapable of exporting electricity and systems capable of exporting electricity to the distribution system, subjecting the latter to appropriate interconnection requirements. Accordingly, this measure promotes consumer choice, encourages private investment in distributed energy resources, strengthens energy security, and facilitates the wider adoption of renewable energy and energy storage technologies. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. title: AN ACT REINFORCING, PROTECTING, AND MANAGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION’S OWNERSHIP OF LOTS OCCUPIED BY PUBLIC SCHOOLS, PROVIDING FOR THE SUMMARY TITLING OF ALL REAL PROPERTIES USED AS PUBLIC SCHOOL SITES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many public schools occupy lands that remain untitled, are covered only by incomplete records, or are still registered under previous jurisdictions. These unresolved property issues hinder the construction and improvement of school facilities and expose public investments to ownership disputes. The problem is widespread. As of May 2026, the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) reported that only 7,075 public schools, or sixteen percent (16%), had sites titled in the name of the Department of Education (DepEd). Titling was ongoing for 7,373 schools, while 32,424 schools, or sixty-nine percent (69%), remained untitled. Of the untitled schools, 6,045 were already experiencing congestion.1 This bill creates a unified and expedited process for identifying, acquiring, titling, and managing lands used for public education. It also strengthens coordination among concerned government agencies while safeguarding due process, just compensation, environmental protection, and 1 According to the report of EDCOM II. the rights of affected landowners and communities. The land on which learning takes place should be as secure as the right to education it serves. Resolving the legal status of public school sites will protect government investments, remove obstacles to urgently needed infrastructure, and preserve these properties for the benefit of present and future generations of Filipino learners. Securing public school sites will protect government resources and provide schools with a stable foundation for their continued development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MIRO S. label: HB 11072
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PURPOSES AND APPLICATION OF THE SPECIAL EDUCATION FUND (SEF), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 100 AND 272 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Teachers should be able to devote their time and energy to teaching. Yet EDCOM II found that teachers were burdened with more than fifty ancillary and administrative tasks, while nearly half worked over fifty hours a week.1 This excessive workload takes valuable time away from lesson preparation, classroom instruction, assessment, and direct learner support. At the same time, access to the Special Education Fund (SEF) remains deeply unequal. EDCOM II reported a 68-fold resource gap between first- and sixth-class local government units, as well as a 394-fold difference in SEF resources per learner. In Makati, the SEF amounted to ₱25,587 per learner, compared with only ₱65 per learner in Guihulngan. Despite these disparities and the urgent needs of schools, ₱16.3 billion in SEF remained unutilized in 2022.2 This bill therefore expands the lawful uses of the SEF to allow schools to hire administrative and other non-teaching personnel and provide more responsive support to learners. label: HB 11073
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE “LARO’T SAYA SA PARKE” PROGRAM, PROMOTING WEEKEND COMMUNITY SPORTS AND RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES IN PUBLIC PARKS, STRENGTHENING SPORTS DEVELOPMENT AMONG YOUTH AND COMMUNITIES, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports and recreational activities are essential components of youth development, physical health, mental well-being, and nation-building. They foster discipline, teamwork, resilience, and social cohesion among individuals and communities. Despite the constitutional mandate recognizing the role of sports in fostering self-reliance and national development, access to safe and organized recreational spaces remains limited in many communities. Public parks, which are intended as communal spaces for recreation and social engagement, are often underutilized or lack structured programs that encourage active participation in sports and physical activities. 1 This bill seeks to institutionalize the “Laro’t Saya sa Parke (LSP)” Program, that was created under the Memorandum Circular No. 49 issued by the Office of the Presidential, as a national initiative that promotes organized sports and recreational activities in public parks during weekends. It aims to encourage active lifestyles, strengthen community engagement, and provide accessible sports opportunities for children, youth, and families. By leveraging public parks as inclusive spaces for recreation and sports development, this measure seeks to address sedentary lifestyles, promote mental and physical well-being, and cultivate a culture of sportsmanship and community participation among Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11074
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL EARLY-CAREER MENTORSHIP PROGRAM, ESTABLISHING THE EARLY CAREER MENTORSHIP ACCESSIBILITY FRAMEWORK, PROMOTING ONLINE AND INSTITUTION-BASED MENTORSHIP PLATFORMS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The transition from education to employment remains one of the most critical yet underserved stages in the development of Filipino youth. Many graduates and early-career professionals face significant barriers in accessing guidance, professional networks, and industry exposure necessary for successful career entry. While various government agencies, educational institutions, and private organizations implement mentorship initiatives, these programs remain fragmented, unevenly distributed, and largely inaccessible to youth outside urban centers or elite academic institutions. There is currently no unified national framework that ensures equitable, structured, and measurable access to early-career mentorship opportunities. This bill seeks to institutionalize the Early Career Mentorship Accessibility Act by establishing a national framework that integrates mentorship programs across government agencies, educational institutions, and private sector partners. It shall 1 promote the use of digital platforms to ensure accessibility, scalability, and inclusivity, particularly for geographically isolated, disadvantaged, and underrepresented youth. By formalizing mentorship pathways, standardizing program implementation, and strengthening public-private collaboration, this measure aims to bridge the gap between education and employment, enhance youth employability, and support the development of a competent, competitive, and future-ready Filipino workforce. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11075
title: AN ACT MANDATING FREE COLLEGE ENTRANCE EXAMINATIONS IN STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES AND LOCAL UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES, PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION BASED ON INABILITY TO PAY TESTING FEES, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to higher education begins with access to college admission. However, for many Filipino students, especially those from low-income households, entrance examination fees remain a significant barrier to opportunity. While RA No. 12006 otherwise known as the ‘Free College Entrance Examinations Act’ has provided relief by mandating private higher education institutions to waive entrance examination fees for qualified students, its coverage remains limited. The law applies only to private institutions and imposes eligibility conditions, thereby excluding many deserving students who may not meet specific academic or income thresholds. Moreover, there is currently no uniform national policy mandating all State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) and Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs) to provide free entrance examinations, nor is there an explicit prohibition against exclusion due to inability to pay testing fees. 1 This bill seeks to institutionalize a universal, rights-based approach by mandating all SUCs and LUCs to provide free entrance examinations to all applicants, regardless of socioeconomic status, and to prohibit any form of exclusion or discrimination based on inability to pay. By removing financial barriers at the point of entry, the State ensures that access to higher education is determined by merit and potential, not by financial capacity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11076
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CREDIT ACCESS FOR SMALL FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK, MANDATING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO ALLOCATE A PORTION OF THEIR LOAN PORTFOLIOS FOR AGRI- FISHERY BORROWERS, ESTABLISHING AN AGRI CREDIT GUARANTEE FUND, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture and fisheries remain vital sectors of the Philippine economy, sustaining millions of livelihoods and ensuring food security. However, small farmers and fisherfolk continue to face significant barriers in accessing affordable credit, including high interest rates, stringent collateral requirements, and limited financial inclusion. Despite existing policies such as the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (Republic Act No. 8435) and the Agri-Agra Reform Credit Act of 2009 (Republic Act No. 10000), access to financing for small-scale producers remains inadequate. Many financial institutions continue to fall short of meaningful support, and compliance mechanisms have not fully addressed the structural constraints faced by the sector. 1 To address these gaps, this bill mandates financial institutions to allocate a portion of their loan portfolio specifically for agri-fishery borrowers, ensures affordable interest rates, removes collateral barriers through a government-backed guarantee mechanism, and strengthens institutional support for inclusive agricultural financing. By establishing an Agri Credit Guarantee Fund and promoting accessible, low-interest, and collateral-free loans, this measure seeks to empower small farmers and fisherfolk, increase productivity, reduce rural poverty, and enhance national food security. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11077
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH CORPS, ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL VOLUNTEER PROGRAM FOR TRAINED YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH ADVOCATES, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to confront a worsening mental health crisis notwithstanding advances in public discourse and the enactment of Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as the “Mental Health Act,” which established the country’s landmark policy framework on mental health. Despite its passage, significant gaps in implementation and service delivery persist nearly a decade thereafter. In 2023, the mental health experts characterized the situation as ‘a rising epidemic’, a condition that remains evident to date, as reflected in the increasing volume of crisis calls reported by the National Center for Mental Health (NCMH)1. This growing demand is further exacerbated by a shortage of mental health professionals which constraint attainment of access to timely, adequate and quality care. The urgency of addressing the country’s deteriorating mental health landscape 1 ABS-CBN (October 2025). NCMH Crisis Hotline receives more call; causes point to depression. https://www.abs- cbn.com/news/health-science/2025/10/28/ncmh-crisis-hotline-receives-more-calls-causes-point-to-depression-1947 1 has likewise been recognized in the present Congress, as manifested in inquiries initiated under Senate Resolution No. 992. Similarly, the 1987 Philippine Constitution, under Article II, Section 13, recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building. Notwithstanding the growing call for mental health-responsive communities and collective action, the potential of the youth remains underutilized due to fragmented and uncoordinated platforms for engagement. In 2021, UNICEF reported that young people increasingly seek mental health information and demonstrate a heightened willingness to participate in mental health discussions, as well as peer support programs and mechanisms3. Globally, there has likewise been a notable rise in youth engagement in mental health advocacy, peer counseling, and volunteer-driven initiatives4. Thus an urgent need to complement professional services with trained peer support systems that can provide immediate psychosocial assistance and facilitate early intervention at the primary care service level. Empowering the youth as mental health advocates not only expands access to care but also reduces stigma and promotes a culture of help-seeking behavior to expand. This bill seeks to establish a Youth Mental Health Corps, a national volunteer program composed of trained youth advocates equipped with skills in psychosocial first aid, suicide prevention, peer counseling, and crisis listening. By mobilizing the youth as frontliners of mental health support in schools, communities, and disaster settings, the State strengthens its commitment to safeguarding the mental well-being of every Filipino and uphold mental health as a fundamental human right In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 2 Senate of the Philippines (October 2025). label: HB 11078
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL BARANGAY HEALTH EQUITY INDEX, MANDATING THE DEVELOPMENT OF A HEALTH EQUITY SCORECARD FOR EVERY BARANGAY TO IDENTIFY DISPARITIES AND GUIDE TARGETED INTERVENTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes health as a fundamental right of every Filipino and mandates the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development. In the current health landscape, landmark to this obligation is the enactment of Republic Act No. 11223, or otherwise known as the “Universal Health Care Act” which further institutionalizes a system that guarantees equitable access to quality and affordable health care for all Filipinos1. Despite these commitments, significant health disparities persist across communities, particularly at the barangay level. Many barangays continue to experience unequal access to health services due to variations in socioeconomic conditions, geographic isolation, infrastructure gaps, 1 LawPhil. Republic Act No. 11223. https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html 1 and uneven distribution of health personnel and resources. These disparities contribute to differences in health outcomes such as maternal and child mortality, disease burden, nutrition status, and access to preventive services2. However, current national and local planning mechanisms often lack a standardized, granular tool that systematically measures and compares these inequalities across barangays. This proposed measure seeks to address this gap through the establishment of a Barangay Health Equity Index (BHEI) and a corresponding Barangay Health Equity Scorecard for every barangay in the country. The BHEI will serve as a composite, data-driven index that measures key indicators of health status, disease burden, access to services, and the social determinants of health. Meanwhile, the Scorecard will function as an annual performance and monitoring tool that identifies priority health gaps, vulnerabilities, and necessary interventions at the barangay level. By institutionalizing a standardized equity-based measurement system, this measure will enable the government to adopt more evidence-driven health planning, targeted interventions, and responsive resource allocation. The BHEI and Scorecard will guide national agencies and local government units (LGUs) in prioritizing communities with the greatest health needs, strengthening primary care networks, improving service delivery, and ensuring that health investments are directed where they are most needed. Moreover, the proposed system will promote transparency and accountability in local health governance. The public availability of barangay-level health scorecards will empower communities to participate in monitoring health outcomes and encourage stronger coordination among the Department of Health, LGUs, and other relevant stakeholders. Ultimately, the establishment of a Barangay Health Equity Index will provide the national government and local governments with a powerful policy instrument to systematically identify and reduce health inequities across the country. Through better data, more strategic planning, and targeted public health action, this measure aims to strengthen the implementation of Universal Health Care and ensure that no community is left behind in the pursuit of health equity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 2 Paredes, K.P.P. label: HB 11079
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE PRODUCTIVE UTILIZATION OF IDLE LANDS THROUGH TAX REFORMS, INCENTIVES FOR AGRICULTURAL USE, AND PARTNERSHIPS WITH FARMERS AND COOPERATIVES, AMENDING PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Land is one of the most vital resources of the Philippines. Yet vast tracts of land across the country remain idle, underutilized, or deliberately held for speculative purposes. According to data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), the total farm area in the country was estimated at around 7.27 million hectares based on the 2012 Census of Agriculture and Fisheries, highlighting the vast land resources available for agricultural production1. Despite the country’s vast agricultural potential, a significant portion of cultivable land remains idle or underutilized due to various constraints such as absentee landownership, financial limitations, lack of labor, or insufficient technical support2. Idle lands worsen food insecurity, deny local governments potential revenues, and contribute to inequitable land ownership. 1 Philippine Statistic Authority. Technical Notes on the Census of Agriculture and Fisheries (CAF). 2 Lebrilla, M. 2016. Idle Land Tax: Implementation Issues and Challenges. Congressional Policy and Budget Research Department. 1 The Constitution recognizes the duty of the State to promote the equitable distribution and productive use of land to advance national development. While the Republic Act No. 7160 or otherwise known as “Local Government Code of 1991” already authorizes local governments to impose taxes on idle lands, the existing framework has proven insufficient to deter speculative landholding or prolonged neglect of cultivable land. At the same time, many landowners are unable to cultivate their lands due to financial limitations, lack of labor, or absence from rural areas. However, these lands could be productively utilized by tenant farmers, agrarian reform beneficiaries, and agricultural cooperatives if appropriate institutional mechanisms and incentives were established. This measure therefore adopts a balanced and integrated approach to idle land reform. First, it strengthens idle land taxation to discourage land hoarding and speculative holding. Second, it introduces tax incentives and relief measures for landowners who voluntarily allow farmers, agrarian reform beneficiaries, or agricultural cooperatives to cultivate idle lands through formal utilization agreements. Third, it establishes a policy framework to facilitate land matching, support agricultural production, and ensure that idle lands contribute to national food security. The bill also provides for the allocation of revenues generated from idle land taxation to support agricultural modernization programs of the Department of Agriculture and land reform support services of the Department of Agrarian Reform. These resources will help farmers gain access to credit, farm inputs, and technical assistance necessary to ensure the productivity of newly utilized lands. By transforming idle lands into productive agricultural assets, the State can increase domestic food production, expand opportunities for small farmers, stimulate rural economies, and promote equitable and sustainable land use. 2 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11080
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CHILD-CENTERED, FAMILY-BASED, AND REINTEGRATIVE VISITATION AND CARE STANDARDS IN ALL BAHAY PAG-ASA FACILITIES, ESTABLISHING A HOLISTIC SUPPORT SYSTEM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State affirms its constitutional duty to uphold the best interests of the child, particularly for children in conflict with the law (CICL), who require protection, rehabilitation, and meaningful reintegration into society. Under Republic Act No. 9344, Bahay Pag-asa facilities were established as child-caring institutions that provide temporary residential care and intervention services. These facilities are central to the country’s juvenile justice and welfare system and are intended to operationalize a child-centered and restorative approach to justice. Over the years, the Philippines has seen significant progress in reducing juvenile delinquency. Data from the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Council indicate that cases involving CICL declined from 26,850 in 2017 to 4,383 in 2024, reflecting the effectiveness of diversion and rehabilitation programs. However, recent trends suggest potential increases in cases, highlighting the need to strengthen existing mechanisms and prevent regression. Despite these gains, persistent gaps in Bahay 1 Pag-asa operations continue to undermine the delivery of holistic and rights-based care. Among the most critical gaps is the absence of a standardized, enforceable framework on child-sensitive visitation and reintegration practices. While family contact is widely recognized as essential to a child’s emotional well-being and successful reintegration, current practices across facilities remain inconsistent and, in some cases, unregulated. Visitation is often conducted without proper risk assessment, structured supervision, or meaningful child participation. Inadequate documentation and lack of post-visit psychosocial support further weaken the system. These deficiencies expose children to risks of retraumatization, coercion, manipulation, and continued exposure to harmful environments—factors that may ultimately undermine rehabilitation and increase the likelihood of recidivism. Compounding these issues are infrastructure and service delivery challenges faced by Bahay Pag-asa facilities nationwide. With approximately 118 operational centers, many experience overcrowding, limited resources, and insufficient facilities for safe and child-friendly visitation. Moreover, the shortage of trained personnel to manage visitation and reintegration processes constrains the ability of institutions to implement child-sensitive interventions effectively. International standards, including the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, emphasize that children deprived of liberty have the right to maintain contact with their families in a manner consistent with their well-being and best interests. Such contact must be facilitated within a safe, structured, and child- sensitive environment, with appropriate safeguards and professional oversight. The absence of a national framework places the implementation of these standards at risk of inconsistency across local government units. This proposed measure seeks to address these gaps by institutionalizing a Child-Centered Reintegration and Visitation Standards Framework in all Bahay Pag- asa facilities. It mandates the development of individualized visitation and reintegration plans, grounded in social case studies and psychological assessments, and subject to regular review. It establishes risk-based visitor screening and accreditation, ensuring that only individuals who do not pose harm to the child are granted access. The measure also defines levels of visitation—including supervised, therapeutic, and virtual modalities—tailored to the needs and circumstances of each child. 2 Crucially, the bill ensures that children are recognized as active rights-holders by requiring their participation and assent in visitation decisions, while safeguarding them from forced or distressing interactions. It mandates the provision of safe, child- friendly visitation spaces, as well as strict prohibitions against abuse, coercion, and other harmful conduct during visits. To strengthen accountability, the measure requires comprehensive documentation, monitoring, and post-visitation assessment, enabling timely intervention and continuous improvement of care. Furthermore, the bill integrates visitation within a broader child-centered reintegration strategy, recognizing that meaningful family engagement, when properly managed, can significantly improve emotional recovery, strengthen support systems, and reduce reoffending. By embedding visitation within a structured and trauma-informed framework, the State ensures that family contact becomes a tool for healing rather than a source of harm. Ultimately, this measure reinforces the principle that children in conflict with the law are not merely subjects of legal processes but individuals in need of care, guidance, and opportunity. By establishing clear, enforceable standards for visitation and reintegration, the State strengthens its commitment to restorative justice and the long-term well-being of every child. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11081
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL ADULT IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM PROVIDING FREE VACCINES AGAINST INFLUENZA, PNEUMOCOCCAL DISEASE, AND HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS (HPV), ADOPTING A LIFE-COURSE IMMUNIZATION STRATEGY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Vaccination is one of the most cost-effective and impactful public health interventions for preventing disease, reducing healthcare expenditures, and saving lives. While the Philippines has made significant progress in childhood immunization, adult immunization remains fragmented and limited in scope, leaving millions of Filipinos vulnerable to vaccine-preventable diseases. Seasonal influenza continues to contribute to substantial morbidity and productivity loss, particularly among the elderly and individuals with underlying health conditions. Pneumonia remains a leading cause of mortality nationwide, disproportionately affecting senior citizens and immunocompromised individuals. Meanwhile, Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is a major cause of cervical cancer and 1 other HPV-related diseases, which continue to impose a significant burden on the healthcare system. Despite the availability of safe and effective vaccines, access remains inequitable due to financial barriers, limited government coverage, and persistent vaccine hesitancy. A life-course approach to immunization—extending protection beyond childhood—is essential to achieving universal health care and strengthening preventive health systems. This measure seeks to institutionalize a National Adult Immunization Program that ensures free and equitable access to priority vaccines, beginning with high-risk populations and progressively expanding coverage. It integrates national and local health systems, strengthens vaccine supply chains, addresses demand-side barriers, and ensures accountability through robust monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11082
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL ORGAN TRANSPLANT REGISTRY, PROVIDING FINANCIAL AND MEDICAL SUPPORT FOR INDIGENT ORGAN TRANSPLANT RECIPIENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Organ transplantation remains one of the most critical life-saving medical interventions for patients suffering from end-stage organ failure. While the Philippines has long recognized the importance of organ donation through Republic Act No. 7170, otherwise known as the ‘Organ Donation Act of 1991’, gaps persist in the implementation of a centralized, transparent, and efficient system for organ allocation and transplant coordination. The absence of an integrated national registry, coupled with the high cost of transplantation and post-operative care, continues to limit access—especially for indigent patients. Thousands of Filipinos suffer from chronic kidney disease, liver failure, and other organ-related conditions that could be treated through transplantation. Despite advancements in medical science, many patients are unable to receive timely and adequate care due to financial constraints and fragmented information systems for organ donation and recipient matching. 1 At present, the absence of a comprehensive national transplant registry hampers the efficient allocation of donated organs, resulting in delays, inequities, and preventable loss of life. Moreover, indigent patients often face insurmountable financial barriers, including costs related to surgery, hospitalization, post-operative care, and lifelong immunosuppressive therapy. This measure seeks to establish a National Organ Transplant Registry that integrates donor and recipient data, ensures equitable allocation of organs based on medical need and ethical standards, and strengthens government oversight. It likewise institutionalizes financial and medical support mechanisms for indigent patients, thereby promoting equitable access to transplantation services. In strengthening existing laws and addressing systemic gaps, this bill aims to save lives, uphold human dignity, and advance universal health care in the Philippines. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11083
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A VARSITY SPORTS AND PARA-SPORTS PROGRAM IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS, STRENGTHENING INCLUSIVITY IN BASIC EDUCATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIV, Section 19 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the State shall promote physical education and encourage sports programs, league competitions, and amateur sports, including training for international competitions, to foster self-discipline, teamwork, and excellence for the development of a healthy and alert citizenry. It further mandates all educational institutions to undertake regular sports activities in cooperation with athletic clubs and other sectors. Consistent with this mandate, Republic Act No. 9155, otherwise known as the “Governance of Basic Education Act of 2001,” recognizes school sports and physical fitness as integral components of the basic education curriculum. Likewise, Republic Act No. 5708, otherwise known as the “Schools Physical Education and Sports Development Act of 1969,” underscores the importance of providing opportunities for the athletic development of children and youth. Complementarily, Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta for Disabled Persons,” as amended, affirms the State’s duty to promote the rehabilitation, self-development, and full participation of persons with disabilities in society, including through sports and physical development programs. Despite these policy directives, opportunities for systematic and sustained athletic and para-athletic development at the basic education level remain limited. While competitions such as the Palarong Pambansa and other school-based meets provide exposure, they do not fully address the need for continuous training, early talent identification, accessibility support, and structured development pathways for young athletes and para-athletes. Many student-athletes and student-para-athletes lack access to organized varsity sports and para-sports programs, competent coaching, adaptive training systems, accessible facilities, adequate equipment, and regular competition at the elementary and secondary levels. This results in missed opportunities to nurture athletic potential at an early stage, which is critical in building a strong pipeline of athletes and para-athletes for higher-level competition, including collegiate, national, and international tournaments. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize varsity sports and para- sports programs in public and private elementary and secondary schools by encouraging the organization of varsity teams, strengthening coaching systems, and improving access to facilities, training, competitions, and adaptive sports support systems. It also establishes mechanisms for athlete and para-athlete identification, performance profiling, and the creation of a national registry of student-athletes and student-para-athletes to support long-term athletic development. The bill likewise promotes collaboration among schools, local communities, local government units, and national sports institutions, including the Philippine Sports Commission, National Sports Associations, the Philippine Olympic Committee, and the Philippine Paralympic Committee, to ensure that training programs align with national, international, and adaptive sports standards. It further recognizes disparities in institutional resources and establishes mechanisms for inter-school clustering and resource-sharing to expand opportunities for learners from underserved and marginalized communities. Ultimately, this measure aims to expand the base of Filipino student- athletes and student-para-athletes, strengthen grassroots sports and para-sports development, and enhance the country’s competitiveness in international sporting events. By institutionalizing varsity sports and para-sports programs in basic education, the State invests in the development of disciplined, healthy, resilient, and high-performing youth, while promoting inclusivity and equal opportunities in sports participation. 2 Similar bills have been filed since the 17th Congress and were primarily referred to the Committee on Basic Education and Culture. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 11084
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING FOOD SECURITY COLD STORAGE FACILITIES IN EVERY PROVINCE OF THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 5, Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to support agriculture through appropriate technology, research, and adequate financial, production, and marketing services. In line with this policy, the State must establish mechanisms that preserve perishable agricultural goods, reduce post-harvest losses, and ensure a stable and sufficient food supply for the population. Food security remains a fundamental national concern, closely linked to economic stability, public welfare, and national resilience. As an agricultural country, the Philippines continues to face persistent challenges in ensuring a stable and sufficient food supply, particularly in the context of post-harvest losses, price volatility, and inefficiencies in the distribution of perishable goods. A major contributor to these challenges is the lack of adequate cold storage infrastructure nationwide. Perishable agricultural products, such as fruits, vegetables, fish, and meat, are highly vulnerable to spoilage due to insufficient storage and handling facilities. The limited availability of accessible and strategically located cold storage facilities results in significant post-harvest losses, reducing farmers’ incomes and contributing to supply constraints and price volatility that ultimately burden consumers. Access to existing cold chain systems also remains uneven, particularly in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas and in provinces with high agricultural production. As a result, many farmers, fisherfolk, and small-scale food processors are compelled to sell their produce immediately at lower prices or risk spoilage, weakening the agricultural value chain and undermining overall food security. This proposed measure seeks to address these challenges by establishing food security cold storage facilities in every province. By ensuring the availability of temperature-controlled storage infrastructure, the State aims to reduce post- harvest losses, extend the shelf life of perishable goods, and enable more efficient distribution and market timing of agricultural products. The measure further promotes accessibility by requiring strategic placement of facilities and prioritizing underserved and high-producing areas through a phased implementation approach. It also designates the Department of Agriculture as the lead implementing agency and mandates coordination with local government units to ensure the effective establishment, operation, and maintenance of the facilities. Ultimately, the establishment of food security cold storage facilities is expected to strengthen the agricultural value chain, improve farmers’ incomes, stabilize food prices, and enhance the country’s capacity to respond to supply disruptions. By investing in critical post-harvest infrastructure, the State affirms its commitment to achieving long-term food security and building a more resilient and efficient food system. Measures seeking the establishment of cold storage facilities have been filed as early as the 8th Congress, although most were limited to specific local government units. Recognizing their growing importance, similar nationwide measures were also filed during the 19th Congress. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G.
