label: HB 11314
title: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE RISE RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to create the Philippine Rise Resource Development Authority as the lead agency responsible for the management, protection, study, and development of the Philippine Rise. It ensures that the State effectively exercises its sovereign rights over the area and manages its resources in accordance with national interests and principles of sustainable development. Formerly known as Benham Rise and renamed under Executive Order No. 25, series of 2017, the Philippine Rise is a vast undersea plateau within the Philippines’ Exclusive Economic Zone and continental shelf. It includes the area recognized as part of the Philippines’ extended continental shelf under the recommendations of the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS). Its natural resources, scientific value, and strategic location create opportunities for research, fisheries, energy, maritime connectivity, investment, and tourism. This bill provides a development framework for the Philippine Rise that shall guide the coordination, implementation, and monitoring of programs, projects, and activities in the area. It shall facilitate public and private investments, provide technical and planning assistance, and recommend policies that support the sustainable and long-term development of the Philippine Rise. The measure strengthens the State’s capacity to assert and protect its rights over the Philippine Rise and to ensure that its resources serve the Filipino people. It recognizes the Philippine Rise not merely as an area of economic and scientific potential, but as a national asset whose protection, responsible development, and preservation are matters of enduring national interest. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11315
title: AN ACT CREATING PERMANENT SCHOOL SECURITY OFFICER POSITIONS IN ALL PUBLIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS NATIONWIDE AND ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY AND SECURITY PROGRAM FOR ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to create permanent School Security Officer (SSO) positions in all public schools, and establish a comprehensive school safety and security program for all public and private basic education institutions nationwide. The right to quality education cannot be fully realized when learners and school personnel remain exposed to preventable threats within school premises and during school-related activities. Schools must first and foremost maintain an environment that protects its community from physical, psychological, digital, and other hazards that may compromise their safety and well-being. The bill creates permanent SSO plantilla positions under the Department of Education (DepEd). This ensures that school security in all public schools is supported by a stable workforce rather than relying solely on contractual or outsourced personnel. Private schools shall likewise comply with applicable safety and security requirements, with compliance as one of the conditions to renew their license and permits. Through these, this measure establishes a baseline of protection while allowing security measures to respond to the emerging risks and threats. School safety must not depend on whether or not a tragedy has already occurred. Every learner deserves to enter a school knowing that measures are in place to protect them, and every parent deserves the assurance that the institution entrusted with their child’s education is prepared to keep them safe. The State must act before lives are lost, not only after. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11316
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING WORKPLACE BULLYING, HARASSMENT, AND OTHER FORMS OF VIOLENCE, PROVIDING FOR ITS PREVENTION, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to prohibit workplace bullying, harassment, and other forms of violence. It provides for its prevention, reporting, investigation, and resolution in both the public and private sectors. Workplace bullying may manifest in physical, verbal, psychological, social, digital, or financial forms. Repeated humiliation, intimidation, threats, malicious conduct, exclusion, and abuse of authority can cause physical, psychological, and emotional harm and cultivate negative workplace dynamics. Such conduct may also impair professional relationships, disrupt the performance of duties, and undermine a workplace culture founded on respect, fairness, and accountability. The bill establishes uniform standards for workplaces in the public and private sectors and defines workplace bullying to cover physical, verbal, psychological, social, digital, and authority-based conduct. It requires employers and heads of offices to adopt written anti-bullying policies, establish accessible and confidential reporting mechanisms, act promptly on complaints, and ensure impartial investigations with due process. It likewise requires the protection of complainants, witnesses, and persons who report or assist in an investigation from retaliation. Every worker deserves to perform his or her duties in an environment free from bullying, intimidation, humiliation, and abuse. Workplace dignity should be protected as a matter of law, not left to the discretion or goodwill of certain employers or offices. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11317
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING DRUGSTORES IN EVERY BARANGAY IN THE COUNTRY, TO BE CALLED AS “BOTIKA NG BARANGAY”, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to create a Botika ng Barangay (BNB) in every barangay in the country and make essential medicines more accessible and affordable to Filipino families. It directs the Department of Health (DOH) to implement a nationwide establishment program within three (3) years, with priority to economically depressed and underserved communities. The DOH’s BNB program has brought affordable medicine closer to communities, but the continuing need to strengthen access to essential medicine calls for its institutionalization. A nationwide program of this scale requires a framework that shall ensure its continued implementation beyond administrative issuances. This measure establishes operational standards to make BNBs responsive to community needs. Each BNBs shall carry medicines included in the core list of the Philippine National Drug Formulatory and shall be managed by a trained BNB Aide. It further requires the establishment of a standardized inventory monitoring and replenishment system, with medicine supplies replenished at least once every quarter to prevent prolonged stockouts. A Botika ng Barangay must be a dependable community source of essential medicines, particularly for families who have limited access to commercial drugstores. Ensuring that every barangay has a reliable source of affordable medicines shall strengthen the State’s commitment to bringing essential health services closer to every Filipino. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11318
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ISSUANCE OF INJUNCTIONS AND TEMPORARY RESTRAINING ORDERS AGAINST WAGE ORDERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 126 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to prohibit the issuance of injunctions and temporary restraining orders against the issuance, publication, implementation, or enforcement, or effectivity of Wage Orders. It amends Article 126, entitled “Prohibition against injunction” of Presidential Decree No. 442, otherwise known as the “Labor Code of the Philippines” to ensure that wage adjustments duly determined under the law are implemented without judicial restraint. Republic Act No. 6727, otherwise known as the “Wage Rationalization Act”, authorizes the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards (RTWPBs), under the supervision of the National Wages and Productivity Commission (NWPC), to determine and adjust minimum wage rates based on prevailing economic and labor conditions through public hearings and tripartite consultations. Some parties, however, may seek temporary restraining orders or injunctions from regular courts to prevent the implementation of Wage Orders. The implementation of Wage Order No. NCR-27 on July 2026, which granted an Eighty-five pesos (Php 85.00) increase in the daily minimum wage of private-sector workers in the National Capital Region, was suspended following the issuance of a temporary restraining order by the Regional Trial Court of Pasig City in connection with a petition for declaratory relief filed by two private companies. Such judicial intervention can prevent a duly promulgated wage adjustment from taking effect even after the competent wage-setting bodies have completed the process prescribed by law. The bill expressly prohibits any court, tribunal, or other entity from issuing a preliminary or permanent injunction or temporary restraining order against the issuance, publication, implementation, enforcement, or effectivity of any Wage Order or resolution issued by the NWPC or the RTWPBs. It thereby protects the integrity of the statutory wage-setting mechanism and prevents duly determined wage adjustments from being rendered ineffective through judicial restraint. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11319
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REHABILITATION AND SUPERVISION OF CHILDREN EXEMPT FROM CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY WHO COMMIT SERIOUS CRIMES, ESTABLISHING REGIONAL REHABILITATION CENTERS FOR YOUTH, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9344, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “JUVENILE JUSTICE AND WELFARE ACT OF 2006”, AS AMENDED, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a Regional Rehabilitation Center for Youth (RRCY) in every region of the country, under the direction of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), with an Intensive Juvenile Intervention and Support Center in each RRCY. It amends Republic Act (RA) No. 9344, otherwise known as the “Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006”, as amended by RA No. 10630, to strengthen the rehabilitation and supervision of children exempt from criminal responsibility who commit serious crimes. Despite the enactment of RA No. 9344, as amended, the increasing number of cases involving children in conflict with the law provides an opportunity to strengthen the existing rehabilitation system. The current framework places significant responsibility on local government units (LGUs) for the establishment and operation of Bahay Pag-Asa facilities which results in uneven capacity to provide secure and specialized care. The bill transfers the primary responsibility for specialized residential rehabilitation to the DSWD, and strengthens the protection and assistance afforded to victims and their families. It likewise preserves the right of victims to recover restitution, indemnity, damages, and other civil remedies notwithstanding the child’s exemption from criminal liability. The protection of children and the protection of society are not competing obligations. A just juvenile justice system gives children a genuine opportunity to change while giving victims, families, and communities the assurance that serious offenses will be met with meaningful intervention and appropriate action. This measure gives the State the capacity to fulfill both responsibilities, because rehabilitation must be a system capable of protecting lives, restoring families, and giving children the chance to return to society as better and more responsible individuals. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 11320
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES EXTENSION SYSTEM TO ACCELERATE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES DEVELOPMENT, CREATING THE BUREAU OF AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The agriculture and fisheries sector remains fundamental to the Philippine economy and to the country's food security. Yet despite the sector's importance, farmers and fisherfolk continue to face persistent challenges in productivity, technology adoption, market access, climate resilience, and access to timely and appropriate technical assistance. The latest data of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) show both the importance of the sector and the continuing need to strengthen the systems that support our agricultural producers. In 2025, the value of production in Philippine agriculture and fisheries reached approximately P1.79 trillion at constant 2018 prices. Agriculture, forestry, and fishing likewise grew by 3.1 percent in 2025 and accounted for 7.9 percent of the country's GDP. However, growth in the sector remains uneven. The PSA reported that in 2025, the value of livestock production declined by 2.3 percent, while fisheries production declined by 0.3 percent in value. The volume of crop production also registered a decline in the fourth quarter of 2025, with palay production down by 5.2 percent during the period. The PSA's latest 2025 Official Poverty Statistics estimate that 9.7 percent of Filipinos, or approximately 11.08 million people, were living below the national poverty threshold in 2025. While national poverty has declined, poverty reduction must continue to reach the communities whose livelihoods depend heavily on agriculture and fisheries. At the same time, the government already recognizes the importance of agricultural extension as a means of transferring knowledge, technology, skills, and innovations from government institutions, researchers, and other stakeholders directly to farmers and fisherfolk. The Agricultural Training Institute continues to conduct capacity-building programs for agricultural extension workers and has been strengthening digital planning, monitoring, and evaluation of the agriculture and fisheries extension system. In 2026, ATI undertook initiatives to strengthen the competencies of agricultural extension resource persons and improve the use of its extension planning and monitoring system. Despite these efforts, there remains a need for a stronger, more coherent, adequately funded, and professionalized national extension system. The proposed measure therefore seeks to strengthen the national agriculture and fisheries extension system by transforming and strengthening the Agricultural Training Institute into a Bureau of Agricultural Extension (BAE) that will serve as the national apex organization for a unified and efficient extension system. The measure provides for a national Agricultural Extension Development Roadmap covering ten (10) years, stronger coordination among the Department of Agriculture, Commission on Higher Education, state universities and colleges, local government units, national government agencies, farmers and fisherfolk organizations, civil society, and the private sector, and a more systematic delivery of education, training, technology transfer, farm and business advisory services, and other extension interventions. It likewise seeks to professionalize agricultural extension work by establishing a dedicated plantilla of personnel, providing opportunities for training and scholarships, developing career paths, strengthening qualification standards, and providing appropriate incentives and benefits to agricultural and fisheries extension workers. Particularly important is the provision requiring a minimum of three (3) agricultural and fisheries extension workers in every municipality, while giving existing LGU extension workers the opportunity to join the national system without diminution of their existing benefits. The proposed institutionalization of the Bureau of Agricultural Extension is therefore not simply an administrative reorganization. It is a strategic investment in the people who produce the country's food. A strong agricultural sector requires not only seeds, machinery, irrigation, credit, infrastructure, and markets. It also requires people on the ground who can bring knowledge and technology to farmers and fisherfolk, understand their problems, connect them with institutions and markets, and help them adapt to changing economic, technological, and climatic conditions. By strengthening the national agricultural and fisheries extension system, this measure seeks to ensure that government assistance reaches farmers and fisherfolk more effectively, that public investments in agriculture generate greater impact, and that Filipino agricultural producers are equipped with the knowledge, skills, and support necessary to become more productive, competitive, resilient, and economically secure. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 11321
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MULTI-FAITH PRAYER AND QUIET ROOMS IN PUBLIC OFFICES AND PUBLIC-FACING ESTABLISHMENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is a diverse nation composed of people belonging to different religions, denominations, and belief systems. The Constitution protects the freedom of religion and guarantees the free exercise thereof. Despite this constitutional protection, many Filipinos who are away from their homes, places of worship, or communities may have limited access to an appropriate and peaceful space for prayer, reflection, meditation, or quiet contemplation while transacting business or accessing services in public offices and other public places. This measure seeks to promote inclusivity and respect for religious diversity by providing for the establishment or designation of Multi-Faith Prayer and Quiet Rooms (MFPQRs) in government offices and encouraging their establishment in public-facing establishments. The proposed MFPQRs are intended to be neutral spaces that may be used by persons of different faiths, as well as individuals who simply need a quiet place for reflection. The measure does not promote or favor any particular religion. Rather, it seeks to provide reasonable accommodation while upholding the constitutional principles of religious freedom, non-discrimination, and inclusivity. The measure also provides practical standards for these facilities, including cleanliness, adequate lighting and ventilation, appropriate flooring, signage, flexible spaces, and, when practicable, an accessible ablution area. It recognizes, however, that the availability of space and resources may vary among government offices and establishments. For local governments, the bill provides that the voluntary establishment and maintenance of MFPQRs may be recognized as a non-obligatory indicator under the Seal of Good Local Governance. It also allows MFPQR-related projects to be considered among eligible projects under the Local Government Support Fund, subject to existing budgetary rules. Ultimately, this measure seeks to promote a more respectful, inclusive, and accommodating public environment where every Filipino, regardless of faith or belief, may have a safe and peaceful space for prayer, reflection, or quiet contemplation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 Businesses have the resources to make a significant difference in the communities that sustain them. label: HB 11324
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING FOOD WASTE REDUCTION AND PREVENTION EDUCATION IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE BASIC EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS, PROMOTING RESPONSIBLE FOOD CONSUMPTION AMONG LEARNERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Food waste remains a pressing challenge in the Philippines, with substantial quantities of edible food discarded daily despite the continued prevalence of food insecurity and hunger. Many Filipino students likewise attend classes with inadequate nutrition, adversely affecting their learning, school participation, and overall development. Addressing food waste not only promotes food security but also supports better educational outcomes for learners. Schools play a vital role in shaping lifelong values and habits. Integrating food waste reduction and prevention into the basic education system will enable learners to appreciate the value of food, practice responsible consumption, and understand the link between food waste, nutrition, environmental sustainability, and climate change. Equipping teachers with the necessary knowledge and instructional resources will further ensure that these principles are effectively integrated into classroom instruction and school activities. This measure seeks to institutionalize food waste reduction and prevention education in all public and private basic education institutions through curriculum integration, teacher capacity-building, and school-based initiatives that promote responsible food management. By fostering a culture of responsible consumption among learners, this bill advances the State's commitment to quality education, food security, environmental protection, and sustainable development. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. title: AN ACT RECLASSIFYING AND CONVERTING PARCELS OF TIMBERLAND WITH A TOTAL AREA OF SEVENTY-SIX THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED NINETY-FIVE SQUARE METERS LOCATED IN POBLACION, BACACAY, ALBAY INTO ALIENABLE AND DISPOSABLE LANDS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Land is highly valued not only because it is the people’s shared heritage, but also because it is an essential factor of production. Land is a witness to the struggles, dreams and aspirations of those who labor hard on it as well as those who unconscionably live off some poor tillers’ backs. Consistent with the constitutionally upheld principle that the use of property bears a social function, the use and ownership of lands are subject to reasonable restrictions by the State in order to promote distributive justice and optimized production. It is in the aforementioned context that this bill seeks to reclassify and convert parcels of timberland in Poblacion, Bacacay, Albay into alienable and disposable lands. The proposed disposable timberland covers a total of seventy-six thousand one hundred ninety-five (76,195) square meters which is a portion of the three hundred fifty-five thousand nine hundred forty-three (355,943) square meters timberland fringing the coastal areas of Bacacay. The area recommended for alienation and disposition had been thoroughly subjected to evaluation by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR). The Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) initially expressed reservations against the reclassification as the identified assessed areas are prone to natural hazards like rain-induced landslides and floods. Further assessment, however, reconsidered that the 76,195 square meters portion of the current timberland is a built-up area, already inhabited and developed with concrete structures. Thus, reclassification and conversion will enhance the integration into the local government unit’s development plan of: 1) sustainable land use, 2) human settlements, 3) food production, 4) environmental protection, 5) infrastructure requirements, and 6) disaster risk reduction. Additionally, the legitimization of economic enterprises established in the unconverted timberland would increase the LGU’s revenues. To allay the apprehensions relative to susceptibility to hazards, the bill provides for health and safety and environmental safeguards that include: 1) declaring areas within the high hazard zones not suitable for commercial, industrial, residential and institutional development, and for evacuation centers; 2) construction of appropriate high integrity flood control mitigation structures, and 3) strict implementation of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act (R.A. 9003). In view of the foregoing, approval of this measure is earnestly sought. CIELO KRISEL B. label: HB 11330
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is not merely a geographic feature; it is the ecological backbone of Luzon and the country’s primary natural shield against increasingly devastating tropical cyclones. As the widest remaining tropical rainforest in the region, its ecosystems store carbon, sustain endemic biodiversity, and regulate critical climate and water flows. Despite its irreplaceable role in national survival, water security, and disaster resilience, the Sierra Madre remains under severe threat from illegal logging, destructive mining, wildlife trafficking, and unchecked land conversion. Current conservation efforts are severely hampered by fragmented governance and misaligned economic incentives. Existing decision systems permit extractive and conventional development to generate immediate financial returns, while transferring the heavy ecological costs—such as flooding, landslides, and water insecurity—directly to the public. Furthermore, the institutions, Indigenous Peoples, and local communities acting as long-term stewards of the landscape do not receive reliable support proportionate to the essential ecosystem services they maintain. This bill seeks to correct this systemic imbalance by enacting the “Sierra Madre Mountain Range Protection, Conservation, and Sustainable Development Act”. It establishes the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority (SMMRA), an attached agency under the Office of the President, tasked to spearhead a 25-year comprehensive Sierra Madre Master Plan. This measure shifts the paradigm toward an integrated, ridge-to-reef, landscape-scale approach, establishing binding ecological limits and no-go areas across the entire mountain range. Crucially, the measure introduces a Nature-Based Solutions-First policy for climate and disaster risk investments. It pioneers the Sierra Madre Nature Credit System, which requires Covered Enterprises—businesses that financially benefit from or materially depend on the mountain's ecosystem services—to satisfy Nature Credit Purchase Obligations, thereby mobilizing private capital directly to the lawful rights holders and communities protecting the area. To deter environmental crimes, the bill institutionalizes the Sierra Madre Environmental Enforcement System (SMEES) and creates a specialized Anti- Illegal Logging Task Force and Forest Protection Corps, supported by satellite and geospatial monitoring technologies. It also mandates strict accountability, requiring those who cause environmental damage to fully restore affected ecosystems independently of other existing penalties. All these interventions are designed to interface seamlessly with existing laws, strictly safeguarding the rights of Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) to their ancestral domains and customary governance. Protecting the Sierra Madre is an urgent matter of national security and intergenerational equity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. label: HB 11336
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9003, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ECOLOGICAL SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT ACT OF 2000,” TO RECOGNIZE WASTE THERMAL TREATMENT AS AN ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT OPTION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the “Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000,” established a comprehensive framework for the proper management of solid wastes, emphasizing source reduction, reuse, segregation, recycling, composting, resource recovery, and the proper treatment and disposal of residual wastes. However, more than two decades after its enactment, the country continues to face serious solid waste management challenges. Increasing waste generation, limited waste diversion and recovery capacity, and inadequate treatment and final disposal facilities continue to place pressure on local governments and communities. Recent incidents underscore the urgency of strengthening the country’s solid waste management system. In January and February 2026, major trash slides occurred at sanitary landfills in different parts of the country, resulting in loss of lives and persons reported missing. These incidents prompted the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to undertake a nationwide review of operating sanitary landfills. More recently, on August 11, 2026, tons of garbage were reported to have clogged the water channel linking Parañaque and Pasay, underscoring the continuing challenge of keeping critical waterways and drainage systems free from solid waste. These incidents, although different in nature, highlight the need for a more comprehensive solid waste management system that addresses not only waste generation and diversion, but also the safe and proper treatment and final disposal of residual wastes. This proposed measure seeks to amend Republic Act No. 9003 to expressly recognize Waste Thermal Treatment as an environmentally sound option for the treatment of residual solid wastes, subject to strict environmental, health and safety safeguards and compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations. It defines Waste Thermal Treatment and Waste Thermal Treatment Facility and establishes a regulatory framework for their establishment and operation. The measure does not intend to make thermal treatment a substitute for waste prevention, segregation, recycling, composting, or other waste diversion measures. Rather, it provides an additional treatment option for residual wastes remaining after feasible source reduction, reuse, segregation, recycling, composting, and other waste diversion and recovery measures. Waste Thermal Treatment Facilities shall not be used to undermine or replace mandatory waste diversion programs under Republic Act No. 9003. To ensure safe and environmentally sound operations, the measure requires compliance with applicable emission and environmental quality standards, proper waste characterization and feedstock management, the use of appropriate and environmentally sound technology, continuous monitoring and reporting, and proper management and final disposal of ash and other residues. The necessary environmental permits and authorizations must also be secured before a facility may operate. The establishment of Waste Thermal Treatment Facilities shall not be mandatory for every province, city, or municipality. Such facilities may be established or utilized only where warranted by the applicable local solid waste management plan, waste characterization, technical and economic feasibility, environmental safeguards, and availability of appropriate feedstock. The measure likewise directs the DENR, in consultation with concerned agencies, local government units, and other stakeholders, to establish detailed technical and environmental standards for their operation. The proposed amendments seek to strengthen, and not weaken, the ecological solid waste management framework established under Republic Act No. 9003. By providing a properly regulated treatment option for residual wastes that cannot feasibly be diverted, the measure seeks to complement existing waste diversion programs, reduce pressure on limited treatment and final disposal capacity, and enable local governments to manage residual wastes more safely, efficiently, and sustainably. For the Filipino people, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The exponential rise of the digital economy has transformed retail and consumer behavior across the Philippines. While e-commerce platforms and digital marketplaces have provided unparalleled convenience and expanded market access for thousands of businesses, this shift has also resulted in a dramatic surge in single-use plastic waste. Daily parcel deliveries generate vast amounts of secondary and tertiary packaging materials such as bubble wrap, plastic mailers, courier pouches, and adhesive tape. The use of such secondary and tertiary packaging materials created a severe burden on local solid waste management systems and marine ecosystems. In 2022, Republic Act No. 11898 amended Republic Act No. 9003 (the “Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000”) by institutionalizing Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). This framework mandates large product producers to recover and manage their post-consumer plastic footprint. However, a critical regulatory gap persists regarding online retail logistics: the majority of e-commerce parcel packaging bypasses the EPR regime because individual micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) sellers do not qualify as "obliged enterprises," leaving the platform-facilitated plastic footprint largely unaccounted for. This bill seeks to address that loophole by extending EPR obligations to large-scale operators of e-commerce platforms and digital marketplaces. Specifically, this measure proposes to: a) explicitly define platform operators as product producers responsible for the aggregate plastic packaging generated through their networks; b) establish criteria for "obliged enterprises" in the e-commerce sector based on total assets, revenue, and logistics infrastructure (e.g., fulfillment centers, sorting hubs, and warehouses; and c) mandate a centralized digital tracking mechanism requiring platforms to monitor, account for, and compute the total platform-facilitated plastic footprint generated by transactions and third-party merchant deliveries. By requiring digital marketplace giants to take full institutional responsibility for the plastic waste generated through their ecosystems, this bill ensures a level playing field, supports circular economy initiatives, and protects our environment from mounting packaging waste. Further, the mechanisms that will be created in this proposed legislation will ensure that the endeavours to minimize plastic waste will come from all fronts, making a more wholistic effort to protect the environment. For the Filipino people, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11339
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A MAGINHAWANG BUHAY SUPPORT FRAMEWORK FOR LOW- INCOME AND MIDDLE-CLASS HOUSEHOLDS, PROVIDING A TWENTY PERCENT (20%) DISCOUNT ON ESSENTIAL NEEDS INCLUDING BASIC UTILITIES, HEALTHCARE, EDUCATION, AND HOUSING, ESTABLISHING AN INFLATION-RESPONSIVE AND INTEGRATED DELIVERY MECHANISM, PROVIDING FOR BENEFIT CEILINGS, TARGETING, FISCAL SAFEGUARDS, INTER-AGENCY COORDINATION, TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND CONGRESSIONAL OVERSIGHT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In every economy, there is a quiet line that separates stability from vulnerability. It is the line where income, though earned honestly and steadily, is no longer enough to keep pace with the cost of living. For millions of Filipino families, particularly those in the low-income and middle-class sectors, that line has been crossed not because of idleness or failure, but because prices have risen faster than wages, and essential needs have become increasingly unaffordable. Electricity, water, healthcare, education, and housing are not discretionary expenses. They are the fixed costs of dignity. When these become too expensive, households are forced into painful trade-offs—between food and medicine, tuition and rent, work and care. Over time, these trade-offs accumulate into deeper inequality, poorer health outcomes, educational attrition, and economic fragility. This proposed measure seeks to correct that imbalance by institutionalizing a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework, grounded on the principle that every Filipino household is entitled to a basic social floor of economic security, regardless of income level, so long as they remain within the broad low-income and middle- class spectrum. In this sense, the measure draws from a universal income perspective—not by distributing cash, but by protecting real income at the point where it matters most: the price of essentials. Persistent inflation in recent years has eroded household purchasing power, disproportionately affecting families whose incomes are fixed or slow-moving. While emergency subsidies and conditional assistance programs have provided temporary relief, these measures are often reactive, fragmented, and dependent on discretionary political action. Moreover, existing social protection mechanisms are largely targeted at the poorest households, leaving a growing segment of the middle class exposed—too “rich” to qualify for aid, yet too financially constrained to absorb rising costs. This condition has created a silent crisis. Middle-income households increasingly rely on debt, reduce preventive healthcare, delay education, or accept substandard housing conditions. The long-term cost of these decisions is borne not only by families, but by the State itself, through higher healthcare expenditures, lower educational attainment, reduced productivity, and social instability. 2 There is therefore a clear need for a permanent, automatic, and inflation- responsive mechanism that stabilizes household welfare before economic stress turns into economic damage. This bill establishes a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework that grants qualified low-income and middle-class households a twenty percent (20%) discount on essential needs, specifically basic utilities, healthcare, education, and housing expenses. The discount is designed as a baseline social protection measure that operates continuously, rather than episodically. The measure is carefully integrated with existing lifeline rates, PhilHealth benefits, free tuition and scholarship programs, and housing subsidies, ensuring that it supplements rather than replaces current entitlements. It introduces a national beneficiary registry, anchored on official statistics and interoperable government databases, to ensure accurate targeting, transparency, and protection against leakage. Recognizing the cyclical nature of inflation, the bill further provides for an automatic, time-bound expansion of benefits when inflation breaches defined thresholds, thereby avoiding the delays and uncertainty of ad hoc emergency legislation. To ensure fiscal sustainability, the measure adopts a cost-sharing mechanism with the private sector, requiring covered service providers to grant discounts upfront, while allowing reimbursement solely through tax credits and incentives, subject to fiscal ceilings, audit, and verification. No direct cash reimbursement is allowed, and no new or special appropriation is mandated. 3 Oversight is institutionalized through an inter-agency council attached to the Office of the President, supported by a permanent secretariat, and complemented by congressional oversight and sunset review provisions. The immediate impact of this measure is the protection of real household income. By reducing the price of essentials, the bill functions as a form of universal income stabilization, ensuring that earned income retains its purchasing power even during inflationary periods. Unlike cash transfers, which may be inflationary, this approach directly lowers effective prices and moderates second- round inflation effects. Economically, the measure is expected to stabilize consumption, particularly among low- and middle-income households with high marginal propensity to spend. This sustains local demand, supports small and medium enterprises, and mitigates economic contraction during periods of price volatility. Socially, the bill reduces the risk of preventable health crises, educational dropouts, housing insecurity, and debt accumulation. Over time, these effects translate into lower public health costs, higher educational completion rates, a more resilient workforce, and a broader tax base. From a governance perspective, the measure shifts social protection from discretion to design—from reactive relief to automatic response—thereby strengthening public trust and policy credibility. At its core, this measure affirms a simple but powerful idea: income is only meaningful if it can meet the cost of living. By institutionalizing a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework, the State acknowledges that protecting dignity in times of economic stress is not charity, but responsibility. 4 This bill does not promise abundance. It promises stability. And in an economy shaped by uncertainty, stability is the foundation upon which opportunity, growth, and shared prosperity are built. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE

label: HB 11340
title: AN ACT PRESERVING AND PROMOTING THE INDIGENOUS GAMES OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Culture shapes values. In this digital era, Filipino children spend most of their time with game consoles or mobile gadgets either at home or in internet cafés, in contrast with the children of the past who spent their leisure time interacting with other children and playing traditional street games. These games include patintero, tumbang preso, siato, and taguan, to name a few. These indigenous games have shaped generations of Filipinos and have imparted values of teamwork, resilience, and sportsmanship. They have been part of our childhood and our cultural heritage. This proposed measure seeks to preserve indigenous games to ensure that future generations of Filipinos can still enjoy them. This bill has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives for three consecutive Congresses (17th, 18th, and 19th) but failed to be passed into law due to time constraints. We seek to revive efforts to make this worthwhile advocacy a law. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11341
title: AN ACT REQUIRING LAND, AIR, AND SEA TRANSPORT PROVIDERS TO PROVIDE PRIORITY SEATING FOR THE ELDERLY, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9257 AND 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZEN’S ACT OF 2010”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE It is the duty of the State to ensure that public utilities and transportation services are accessible to all people, especially those in vulnerable groups such as senior citizens and persons with disabilities. In furtherance of this mandate, Batas Pambansa Bilang 344, or the Accessibility Law, and Republic Act No. 9994, or the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010, were enacted to improve access to public transportation for persons with disabilities and senior citizens. Under these laws, public transport providers are required to designate seats for persons with disabilities, and the Department of Transportation is directed “to develop a program to assist senior citizens to fully gain access to public transport facilities.” Administrative issuances, including Department of Transportation Department Order No. 2014-013, likewise provide for reserved or priority seating for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and pregnant women in certain public transportation facilities. However, existing law and regulations do not establish a comprehensive statutory requirement expressly prescribing priority seating for senior citizens across all modes of public transportation— land, rail, air, and sea—along with uniform standards on seat designation, labeling, reservation, enforcement, and penalties. As a result, senior citizens continue to experience difficulties in accessing priority seats. They often find themselves standing in cramped, moving vehicles while non-eligible passengers occupy seats that should be available to them. The lack of clear statutory rules and consistent enforcement undermines the intent of existing accessibility and senior-citizen laws. In recognition of the invaluable contributions of senior citizens to nation-building, it is only right and just to provide them with additional privileges, particularly in public transportation. By ensuring priority seating for the elderly, this measure promotes their mobility and access, enabling them to continue participating actively in the life of their communities. This bill seeks to strengthen the Expanded Senior Citizens Act by expressly requiring priority seating for senior citizens in land, air, and sea transport, including rail services. It further provides for appropriate penalties for public transport operators who fail to comply with this requirement. It is the hope of this measure to mainstream mobility and access for senior citizens in public transportation, so that we may continue to support them in their daily lives and in their ongoing efforts to contribute to nation-building. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11342
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DISPLAY OF NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE MENU OF FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Good nutrition has been attributed to healthier food choices and, generally, a healthier diet. The presence of nutritional information on the food labels helps people maintain their healthy diet and nutrition because of informed choices. This, in turn, helps prevent the rise of various diseases attributed to an unhealthy diet. The World Health Organization indicates that 80 percent of premature heart disease, stroke, and Type II Diabetes and 40 percent of cancers can be prevented through a healthy diet. Thus, consumers have now become more discerning in their choice of food, always checking the nutritional information and calorie count on food labels. Filipinos, however, are not as informed when dining in restaurants. They are often unaware of the calorie and nutritional content of a meal, leading them or misleading them into an unhealthy eating pattern. This bill aims to mandate the disclosure and display of the nutrition content information on each standard menu in all types of restaurants, including fast food chains, in order to enable and empower consumers with the right to choose the food they want to eat without compromising their health. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11343
title: AN ACT ALLOWING AND REGULATING THE USE OF MOTORCYCLES AS PUBLIC UTILITY VEHICLES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LAND TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State provides that it shall protect and promote the rights and obligations of commuters, drivers, and operators through an efficient and fair transport system for the commuting public. As such, Republic Act 4136, otherwise known as the “Land Transportation and Traffic Code,” was enacted, providing for the control, registration, and operation of motor vehicles and the licensing of owners, dealers, conductors, drivers, and similar matters. While the law covers relevant provisions for privately owned and for-hire motor vehicles, the law lacks coverage for motorcycles-for-hire which have become a growing mode of public transportation in recent years. In 2022, there were at least 682,000 registered motorcycles and tricycles for hire in the country. For many commuters, these motorcycle taxis are sometimes the better option of transportation because of their accessibility, efficiency, and reliability. The growing demand for motorcycles as public utility vehicles also led to the operation of non-registered motorcycles-for-hire, which in turn have posed risks for many commuters since riders do not necessarily have the proper training or insurance coverage to protect themselves and even their passengers. The proposed amendments to RA 4136 shall ensure that the law includes motorcycles-for-hire among the defined public transportation, and as such guarantee their roadworthiness while assuring the safety of the riding public. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of the bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11344
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A BILL OF RIGHTS FOR AIR PASSENGERS, PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State has established that it shall protect the interest of all consumers, promote their general welfare, and establish standards of conduct for business and industry. With the vital role of the air transport industry in fostering inclusive economic growth, it is imperative to guarantee that the air transport sector operates effectively. The industry is experiencing phenomenal growth and has not only regained but, in some indicators, surpassed its pre-pandemic levels, as shown by the sustained rise in business and leisure travel since mobility limitations were relaxed. According to the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), total passenger movements reached about 27.3 million in 2023, 25.2 million in 2024, and 24.5 million in 2025, reflecting robust recovery in domestic and international air travel.1 As the industry offers services to travelers from all socioeconomic backgrounds, issues looming in air travel have continuously affected many air passengers, including but not limited to flight delays, airline overbooking, baggage loss, the disappearance of bookings, and trouble with refunds, among many others. These concerns persist despite the existence of the DOTC-DTI Joint Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2012 (the Air Passenger Bill of Rights), which was further updated by the Civil Aeronautics Board through Economic Regulation No. 9 in January 2024 to strengthen carrier obligations and passenger entitlements for delays, cancellations, denied boarding, and baggage issues.2 1 Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), “Aircraft, Passenger, and Cargo Movements” annual reports: 27,305,261 passenger movements in 2023; 25,194,580 in 2024; 24,450,723 in 2025, https://www.caap.gov.ph/aircraft-passenger-and-cargo-movements/; 2 DOTC-DTI Joint Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2012 (Air Passenger Bill of Rights), issued December 10, 2012; Civil Aeronautics Board, Economic Regulation No. 9 (updated Air Passenger Bill of Rights), effective January This proposed measure aims to focus on the right of air passengers to receive the full value of the service they have purchased and the convenience it offers. Consequently, it protects air passengers, especially during events when their flights are canceled or delayed, and their baggage is lost or damaged, to name a few. It establishes a mechanism to address the grievances of affected air passengers and maintains their right to full and truthful information regarding the contract of carriage. This bill institutionalizes and updates the Joint DOTC-DTI Administrative Order No. 1 issued on 10 December 2012, incorporating developments such as the CAB’s 2024 amendments, with the intent of ensuring the rights of air passengers in the country and promoting efficient air transport service. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE BILL OF RIGHTS OF COMMUTERS, PROMOTING EFFICIENT, SAFE, CONVENIENT, ACCESSIBLE AND INCLUSIVE PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Greater Manila Area is home to millions of commuters daily who need to move from their homes to their workplaces or schools by taking buses, jeepneys, taxis, trains, tricycles, and pedicabs. With the existing road-based public transport system, a regular commuter in Metro Manila will have spent about 15 to 59 minutes 1 on a regular day or worse, 3 hours for a 13-kilometer distance2 , and will have transferred from at least two modes of Public Utility vehicles before he or she gets to work. For those taking trains or buses, an additional of at least 30 to 40 minutes on average will be allotted for waiting time alone. A study on commuting in Metro Manila finds that Filipinos spend about 16 days a year stuck in traffic, costing them about 100,000 Philippine pesos ($2,000) a year in lost income 3 or an estimated economic loss of 4.6% of the GDP4. With the evident economic losses and the commuter’s daily ordeal, it is the State’s obligation to remedy the public’s outcry for better, efficient, and dignified transport system. 1 “Duration of daily Commute in the Philippines as of June 2022” https://www.statista.com/forecasts/1274764/philippines- duration-of-daily-commute Accessed on September 20, 2022 2 Metro Manila Development Authority 2019 3 Ana P. Santos, 2019. “Carmageddon: The indignity of commuting in Metro Manila” https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2019/10/24/carmageddon-the-indignity-of-commuting-in-metro-manila Accessed on September 21, 2022 4 Asian Development Bank, 2012 “ Transport Sector Assessment, Strategy and Roadmap” https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/institutional-document/33700/files/philippines-transport-assessment.pdf Accessed on September 21, 2022 This bill seeks to promulgate and implement policies and programs that will ensure the welfare and dignity of the commuting public, address challenges of mobility amidst rapid urbanization, promote road safety, reduce road congestion and air pollution, mitigate transport-related health hazards, and improve access to services and markets, thereby fostering social equity, economic development, and ecological balance. When the system for mass transportation is efficient and effective, fewer people will take private cars, leading to less cost, less pollution, and a more dignified overall commute experience. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11346
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF TRICYCLE DRIVERS AND OPERATORS, INSTITUTIONALIZING MECHANISMS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Tricycles are considered the “vehicle of the masses”. It is often the transportation option of many low-income households to reach major thoroughfares, and a significant income source of many Filipinos displaced in the formal working sector due to a lack of employable skills. Oftentimes, driving a tricycle will be the only mode of livelihood until retirement. According to the 2023 Annual Report of the Land Transportation Office, there are more than 7 million registered private motorcycles and tricycles in the country. It is high time that we give value to our tricycles in the country. It is high time that we give value to our tricycle drivers and operators for their contribution to the daily life of the ordinary Filipinos and to economic development. This measure ensures the welfare of the tricycle drivers and operators for a more organized sector by defining the requirements for proper operation of tricycles and simplifying the registration system imposed in the application and issuance of motorized tricycle operator permit (MTOP). It also mandates the establishment of a one-stop shop in every local government unit to cater to all the transactions of tricycle drivers and operators. It advances the welfare of the tricycle sector by mandating the Social Security System and the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation to assure their provision of health care and social benefits. The measure outlines the significant role of the Local Government Units and other government agencies in supporting the sector. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11347
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE PREVENTION OF ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY, STRENGTHENING THE FAMILY AND COMMUNITY SUPPORT FOR ADOLESCENTS, AND PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY PREVENTION AND EDUCATION PROGRAM
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health, education, and social protection concern in the Philippines. While recent data show encouraging improvements1, the persistence of pregnancies among adolescents, particularly among younger girls and those from disadvantaged households, demonstrates the need for a comprehensive and sustained national response. The figures reveal that teenage pregnancy is closely linked to socioeconomic disadvantage. The PSA's 2022 National Demographic and Health Survey reported that 10.3 percent of women aged 15 to 19 in the poorest wealth quintile had experienced pregnancy, compared with only 1.8 percent among those in the wealthiest quintile.2 These disparities demonstrate that adolescent pregnancy cannot be addressed solely as a matter of individual choice. It is also a question of unequal access to information, health services, education, protection, and opportunities. Of even greater concern are pregnancies involving very young adolescents. PSA data showed that registered births to mothers aged 10 to 14 increased from 1,903 in 2016 to 2,113 in 2020, an increase of 11 percent. During this period, an average of five to seven births each day were registered to mothers aged 10 to 14.3 Pregnancies at such young ages require particular attention from the State because they may be associated with abuse, exploitation, coercion, or other circumstances that compromise a child's safety and rights. 1 Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), 2025 National Demographic and Health Survey: Teenage Pregnancy. The 2025 NDHS reports that 4.9 percent of women aged 15–19 had ever been pregnant, compared with 5.4 percent in 2022. 2 Philippine Statistics Authority, 2022 National Demographic and Health Survey: Teenage Pregnancy. The PSA defines teenage pregnancy as the percentage of women aged 15–19 who have ever been pregnant. The survey reported a prevalence of 10.3 percent among women in the lowest wealth quintile and 1.8 percent among those in the highest wealth quintile. 3 Philippine Statistics Authority, Adolescent Pregnancy in the Philippines: 2016–2020, PSA Reference No. 2022-477, 8 December 2022. The report states that registered births to mothers aged 10–14 increased from 1,903 in 2016 to 2,113 in 2020, equivalent to an 11.0 percent increase. Page 1 The consequences of adolescent pregnancy can extend beyond pregnancy and childbirth. A young mother may face difficulty continuing her education, increased economic vulnerability, diminished employment opportunities, and greater dependence on her family or social protection programs. These consequences can, in turn, reinforce an intergenerational cycle of poverty. The response of government must never be to stigmatize adolescent parents. A young person who becomes pregnant remains entitled to education, health care, protection, and opportunities to build a productive and dignified life. Prevention and support must therefore go hand in hand. The proposed Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention Act seeks to adopt a prevention-centered, family-supported, values-based, and age- and development- appropriate approach to adolescent pregnancy. It recognizes that no single government agency, program, or intervention can adequately address the problem. The measure therefore establishes the Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention Inter-Agency Council which shall serve as the policy-making body responsible for the development of a national framework that shall be called the National Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention and Education Program. The measure shall strengthen, at the community level age, culturally-sensitive and responsive, and age- and development-appropriate education on responsible decision-making, healthy relationships, self-respect, self-discipline, personal boundaries, and the consequences of early and unplanned pregnancy and childbearing for all adolescents through the development and delivery of the Adolescent Pregnancy and Reproductive Health Education. The measure further recognizes the importance of parents, families, schools, communities, and local governments. Government programs will have limited impact if young people lack supportive environments in which they can ask questions, obtain reliable information, seek help, and make responsible decisions without fear of stigma. The bill therefore promotes stronger family and community engagement and clearer coordination among service providers. Education continuity shall be an important component of the national strategy through School-Based Programs to be implemented by the Department of Education which includes interventions such as educational, career, and life-planning support, and continuing educational support and reintegration of adolescent parents. The proposed Act shall likewise strengthen mechanisms for the early identification and referral of adolescents who may be at heightened risk of pregnancy, school disengagement, abuse, exploitation, or other forms of vulnerability. Particular attention shall be given to children and adolescents in communities with persistently high rates of adolescent pregnancy or other identified risk factors. label: HB 11350
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most important natural ecosystems and a vital environmental and disaster-resilience asset. Stretching across eastern Luzon, it serves as a natural barrier that helps lessen the impacts of typhoons, heavy rainfall, flooding, landslides, and other natural calamities. In line with this, this measure seeks to strengthen the protection, conservation, restoration, and sustainable management of the Sierra Madre Mountain Range by establishing a dedicated Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority and providing a comprehensive framework for its long-term management. Among its salient features are: (1) the creation of a dedicated authority to coordinate conservation, enforcement, restoration, climate adaptation, and disaster- risk reduction efforts; (2) the formulation of a 25-year Sierra Madre Master Plan integrating biodiversity conservation, watershed management, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, sustainable livelihoods, land-use planning, and the rights and traditional knowledge of Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples; and (3) the establishment of landscape zoning, ecological corridors, restoration measures, and stronger enforcement against activities that degrade the mountain range. The measure is firmly anchored in Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution which declares the State’s duty to protect and advance the people’s right to a balanced and healthful ecology. It also advances the State’s responsibility to protect the nation’s natural resources for present and future generations. By treating the Sierra Madre as a critical natural foundation for disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, and public safety, the bill gives concrete effect to the constitutional mandate of environmental protection. The protection of the Sierra Madre is therefore not merely an environmental concern. It is a matter of public safety, national resilience, food and water security, and national survival. The mountain range functions as one of Luzon’s principal natural defenses against typhoons and extreme weather, while healthy forests and watersheds help reduce flooding and landslide risks. The bill accordingly recognizes the Sierra Madre as a critical natural foundation for national security, disaster risk reduction, and climate resilience, and directs government agencies to integrate ecosystem-based approaches into disaster and national security planning. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. PERCIVAL V. CENDAÑA Akbayan Representative JOSE MANUEL TADEO DADAH KIRAM ISMULA “CHEL” I. label: HB 11352
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FAIR TREATMENT OF CERTAIN SENIOR CITIZEN PENSIONERS BY GRANTING ANNUAL CHRISTMAS CASH GIFT, THIRTEENTH-MONTH PENSION, AND PENSION INCREASES TO PENSIONERS OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM AND GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM WHO ARE BENEFICIARIES OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7699, “AN ACT INSTITUTING LIMITED PORTABILITY SCHEME IN THE SOCIAL SECURITY INSURANCE SYSTEMS BY TOTALIZING THE WORKERS’ CREDITABLE SERVICES OR CONTRIBUTIONS IN EACH OF THE SYSTEMS”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 7699, otherwise known as the “Limited Portability Law,” allows workers who have rendered service or made contributions under both the Social Security System (SSS) and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) to totalize their creditable periods for purposes of qualifying for benefits. This recognizes the contributions and years of service of workers who have moved between the private and public sectors. Despite this recognition, pensioners who qualify under the portability scheme have not always received benefits on the same basis as similarly situated old-age pensioners of the respective systems, particularly with respect to supplemental pension benefits and pension increases. This measure seeks to ensure fair and equal treatment by granting qualified pensioners under Republic Act No. 7699 the same annual Christmas cash gift, thirteenth-month pension, and pension increases granted to similarly situated pensioners of the SSS and GSIS. A pensioner receiving pensions from both systems shall be entitled to the applicable benefits from both systems, based on the pension payable by each. The measure further seeks to protect existing benefits and ensure that the implementation of the law shall not result in the diminution or reduction of benefits already enjoyed by portability pensioners. The passage of this measure will uphold the principle that workers who have contributed to both social insurance systems should not be placed at a disadvantage merely because their pension entitlement was established through the portability scheme. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11353
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AUTISM CENTERS AND EARLY DETECTION PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects many Filipino individuals and families who continue to face significant challenges in accessing timely developmental screening, diagnosis, intervention, therapy, healthcare, education, and community support services. These challenges are compounded by the limited availability of specialized facilities and trained professionals, financial barriers, and unequal access to developmental services, particularly in underserved and geographically disadvantaged areas. This proposed measure seeks to establish a nationwide network of accessible and affordable Autism Centers that will serve as regional hubs for developmental screening, diagnostic assessment, intervention, rehabilitation, family support, educational coordination, and referral services. It likewise seeks to strengthen early detection and intervention by integrating developmental screening into existing health and community-based programs and by training frontline healthcare, education, and community personnel to recognize developmental concerns and facilitate timely referrals. The measure further promotes inclusive education and community support, strengthens the capacity of healthcare professionals, therapists, educators, and other service providers, and encourages research and data-driven policymaking to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, and affordability of autism-related services. Recognizing that timely and continuous support is essential to improving outcomes, the bill provides for coordinated referral mechanisms among Autism Centers and relevant healthcare, education, social welfare, skills training, and employment institutions. It also encourages the expansion of appropriate health coverage and financial assistance for indigent and financially vulnerable families. Consistent with Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta for Persons with Disability,” as amended, Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as the “Mental Health Act,” Republic Act No. 11223, otherwise known as the “Universal Health Care Act,” Republic Act No. 11650, otherwise known as the “Instituting a Policy of Inclusion and Services for Learners with Disabilities in Support of Inclusive Education Act,” and other relevant laws, this measure adopts a rights-based, inclusive, family-centered, community-based, and evidence-informed approach to autism care and support. By establishing accessible Autism Centers and strengthening early detection, referral, intervention, and support systems nationwide, this measure seeks to reduce disparities in access to services and enable persons with ASD and their families to receive timely, appropriate, and continuing support regardless of their place of residence or economic circumstances. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11354
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE RECRUITMENT, TRAINING, AND EDUCATION QUOTA FOR WOMEN IN THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 58 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE REFORM AND REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1998,” AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Women play an indispensable role in modern law enforcement. Their presence in the police service strengthens the capacity of law enforcement institutions to respond effectively and sensitively to cases involving women and children, sexual and gender-based violence, domestic abuse, and other crimes and situations requiring gender-responsive policing. Recognizing this need, Republic Act No. 8551, otherwise known as the “Philippine National Police Reform and Reorganization Act of 1998,” established women's desks in police stations and provided for the prioritization of women for recruitment and training. Section 58 of the law currently requires the Philippine National Police (PNP) to reserve ten percent (10%) of its annual recruitment, training, and education quota for women. The statutory quota was established more than two decades ago. The evolving demands of policing and the continuing need for a more representative and gender-responsive police organization warrant a progressive increase in the participation of women in the PNP. This measure therefore seeks to increase the existing quota from ten percent (10%) to fifteen percent (15%) during the first five (5) years from the effectivity of the proposed law, and to twenty percent (20%) beginning on the sixth (6th) year and every year thereafter. The measure does not dispense with the qualifications, merit, fitness, eligibility, and other requirements prescribed by law for appointment to the PNP. Rather, it seeks to ensure that qualified women are given meaningful and increased opportunities to enter the police service within the reserved quota. The measure likewise requires the PNP to incorporate the women's quota in its recruitment and manpower planning and to undertake reasonable and sustained efforts to attract, recruit, and qualify women applicants. This will help ensure that the statutory quota is treated as an integral component of PNP recruitment policy and not merely as an after-the-fact numerical target. To promote accountability, the measure establishes a monitoring and reporting mechanism requiring the PNP to submit an annual report to the NAPOLCOM and Congress on its compliance with the women's quota, including the number of women who applied, qualified, were appointed, and underwent training, as well as any unfilled portion of the reserved quota and the reasons therefor. The measure further recognizes that increasing the number of women in the PNP should not confine them to women's desks. Women recruited and trained under the program should be afforded equal opportunities for assignment, promotion, professional development, and career advancement throughout the police organization. This is consistent with the existing statutory policy that the women's-desk provisions should not restrict the assignment of policewomen to other positions or be used to prevent their promotion. By progressively increasing the representation of women in the PNP, this measure seeks to build a more representative, professional, responsive, gender- sensitive, and effective police force capable of providing accessible and appropriate police services to all sectors of Philippine society. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPLOYMENT OF MOBILE HEALTH CLINICS TO GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AND DISADVANTAGED AREAS (GIDAs) AND OTHER UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE REGULAR MOBILE HEALTH SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to basic healthcare remains a significant challenge for Filipinos living in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs) and other underserved communities, where distance, inadequate health facilities, and shortages of healthcare personnel can prevent timely access to essential medical services. This measure seeks to establish a Mobile Rural Health Clinic Program under the Department of Health (DOH) to provide regular, accessible, and community-based healthcare services in areas where permanent health facilities are limited or difficult to reach. The Program shall provide primary and preventive care, diagnostics, medicines, maternal and child health services, mental health services, emergency care, health education, and referral assistance, as appropriate to the needs of the communities served. The measure likewise strengthens coordination among the DOH, local government units, PhilHealth, and other concerned agencies to ensure continuity of care and integration with existing health systems, while providing appropriate standards for mobile clinic operations, personnel, equipment, and digital health systems. By bringing essential healthcare services closer to underserved Filipinos, this measure seeks to advance equitable access to healthcare and strengthen the delivery of primary health services in communities that need them most. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11356
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ACCESSIBLE, SAFE, CLEAN, GENDER-RESPONSIVE, AND WELL- MAINTAINED PUBLIC TOILETS AND SANITATION FACILITIES IN PUBLIC PLACES, TRANSPORT TERMINALS, TOURIST AREAS, MARKETS, PARKS, AND GOVERNMENT CENTERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to clean, safe, accessible, and well-maintained toilet and sanitation facilities is a basic public-health and public-dignity concern. Yet in many public places, including markets, parks, transport areas, tourist destinations, and government centers, adequate sanitation facilities remain insufficient, inaccessible, poorly maintained, or unavailable to the public. The absence of reliable public sanitation facilities can contribute to poor hygiene, environmental contamination, open defecation, and preventable health and safety risks. It disproportionately affects children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, pregnant person, persons with mobility limitations, workers, commuters, and other vulnerable members of the public. While existing laws provide sanitation and accessibility requirements for particular establishments and facilities, there remains a need for a coordinated framework that specifically addresses public access to sanitation facilities across high-use public places. This measure therefore mandates the provision, maintenance, or designation of compliant public toilets and sanitation facilities; establishes minimum standards for cleanliness, water, handwashing, safety, privacy, accessibility, and gender responsiveness; and requires local government units to prepare Public Sanitation Access Plans identifying existing facilities, access gaps, priority areas, maintenance responsibilities, and financing options. The measure also promotes the use and upgrading of existing facilities before new construction, provides for phased implementation, and establishes coordination among the Department of Health, local government units, and other concerned agencies. It further harmonizes the measure with existing sanitation and accessibility laws, including Republic Act No. 11311, to avoid duplication and double penalties. The enactment of this measure will strengthen the country's sanitation system by ensuring that the public can reasonably access facilities that are not only available, but also safe, clean, accessible, functional, and worthy of human dignity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines, with over 36,000 kilometers of coastline, relies on healthy marine ecosystems for food security, livelihoods, tourism, and coastal protection. Yet these resources face growing threats from marine litter, particularly plastic waste. The World Bank estimates that the country generates about 1.7 million metric tons of post-consumer plastic waste annually, with roughly 0.75 million metric tons of mismanaged plastic entering the ocean each year. 1 Existing laws—such as R.A. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act), R.A. 9275 (Clean Water Act), R.A. 11038 (Expanded NIPAS Act), and R.A. 11898 (Extended Producer Responsibility Act)—provide a policy framework for waste management and environmental protection. However, marine litter persists due to gaps in implementation, inconsistent data collection, and limited coordination among agencies, local government units (LGUs), and stakeholders. The proposed bill institutionalizes a National Coastal Cleanup Program under the DENR, in coordination with DILG, DepEd, CHED, CSC, PNP, AFP, LGUs, and other partners. It mandates quarterly nationwide cleanup activities covering coastal areas, marine environments, inland waterways, esteros, and 1 “World Bank. 2024. Guidance on the Development of a Roadmap for Managing Plastic Waste and Reduction of Non-Recyclable Single-use Plastics in the Philippines creeks, and establishes standardized reporting of trash data and cleanup reports. Collected data will support evidence-based waste management, pollution prevention, and enforcement. Recent cleanup efforts demonstrate both the scale of the problem and public willingness to act. In 2024, over 74,000 volunteers collected approximately 352,479 kilograms of waste from 250 coastal sites nationwide. 2 By transforming cleanup activities into a coordinated, data-driven national program, this measure advances the constitutional right to a balanced and healthful ecology and ensures that coastal and marine ecosystems remain productive for present and future generations.
