label: HB 11361
title: AN ACT DECLARING EVERY 10TH OF FEBRUARY OF EACH YEAR AS NATIONAL SAFER INTERNET DAY IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines ranks as the top country in the Asia-Pacific with the highest daily online usage. About 76.7 million Filipino internet users spend an average of more than 10 hours every day scouring the World Wide Web. With the forecasted improvements in the internet infrastructure, about 15.5 million households are predicted to be connected to the internet by 2025. The availability of the internet throughout the nation has facilitated people's connectivity and daily activities, including those related to education, commerce, and entertainment. Digital operations have increased the efficiency of daily transactions by reducing the time required for otherwise in- person, human transactions and making collaboration doable even for colleagues who are miles apart. While the potential of internet efficiency has improved our daily lives, it has also presented a number of safety and security challenges to its users both children and adults. In 2021 alone, there were more than 98,000 cyberattacks recorded and around 2.8 million cybercrimes listed, including fraud, sexual abuse and exploitation, bullying and identity theft. It is our belief that appropriate steps towards lowering the risks of internet users against cybercrimes can be achieved by first raising awareness among the people. In the pursuit of making the online world a safer space for its users, this bill seeks to declare one day every year as National Safer Internet Day. By making Filipino internet users conscious of their online activities and the potential threats of their digital interactions, their vulnerabilities to scammers, hackers, and online syndicates can be dramatically reduced and prevented. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11362
title: AN ACT ENSURING THE AVAILABILITY, ADEQUACY, ACCESSIBILITY, AND SAFETY OF FOOD TO EVERY FILIPINO
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is a country that is regularly hit by natural and human- induced disasters, and the need for early warning systems is paramount. Access to such information ensures that vulnerable communities have the capacity for evidence-based and timely decision-making even before a crisis arises. The huge and fast-growing population in the Philippines is often cited as the main factor driving the country’s global competitiveness and improve attractiveness to investment. While reports indicate that there is enough food to feed the entire country, many Filipinos, especially children below the age of five, continue to suffer from malnutrition due to inadequate intake of food and nutrients. In the 2022 Global Food Security Index (GFSI) by Economist Impact, the Philippines ranked 67th out of 113 countries, with an overall score of 59.3 out of 100.1This represents an improvement from its 70th place in 2018, but the country’s performance has been uneven: it rose to 64th in 2019, slipped to 73rd in 2020, recovered to 64th in 2021, and then settled at 67th in 2022.2 Among sub-categories, the country again ranked first in only one—nutritional standards—underscoring a recurring pattern: strong performance in policy 1 Economist Impact and Corteva Agriscience. 2022. Global Food Security Index 2022: Global Report. September 2022 2 Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS). 2022. “Is Food Supply Accessible, Affordable, and Stable? The State of Food Security in the Philippines.” and standard-setting, but persistent gaps in implementation and systemic resilience. Among its many provisions, the foregoing measure explicitly lists governmental obligations of the State to respect, protect, and fulfill every Filipino’s right to adequate food. It also lays out specific percentage targets for the reduction of hunger, ultimately aiming for zero incidences of forced hunger within ten years. This measure seeks to address the following concerns: 1) food availability, stability, and adequacy; 2) food quality and safety; 3) the determination of standards on the minimum amount of food to be given to any person suffering from hunger or undernutrition; 4) physical and economic access to food; and 5) well-functioning distribution, processing, and market systems. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11365
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL FORENSIC DNA DATABASE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine justice system continuously faces the challenge of solving crimes efficiently, accurately, and fairly. Modern forensic science, particularly Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) technology, provides law enforcement agencies and courts with a powerful scientific tool for identifying individuals, linking biological evidence to persons, excluding innocent individuals, and assisting in the resolution of otherwise difficult or unsolved cases. DNA evidence may be recovered from biological materials found at crime scenes and from other sources relevant to criminal investigations. When properly collected, analyzed, stored, and compared, DNA profiles can establish associations between crime-scene evidence and individuals with a high degree of scientific reliability. A national forensic DNA database can therefore complement existing investigative techniques and strengthen the evidentiary foundation of criminal investigations and prosecutions. Several legislative measures have previously recognized the need for a Philippine forensic DNA database. Among these are House Bill No. 94 of the 19th Congress, which sought to institutionalize a national forensic DNA database for criminal investigations, identification of missing persons and unidentified human remains, and related purposes, as well as House Bill No. 1179 filed during the 20th Congress, which similarly proposed the establishment of a forensic DNA database in the Philippines. Despite these legislative initiatives, there remains a need for a comprehensive statutory framework that will establish, maintain, regulate, and ensure the proper use of a Philippine National Forensic DNA Database. The proposed measure seeks to provide such a framework while ensuring that the collection and processing of DNA information are conducted in accordance with law, scientific standards, due process, privacy rights, and other constitutional safeguards. The proposed Philippine National Forensic DNA Database shall serve as a centralized forensic resource for authorized government agencies. It shall facilitate the comparison of DNA profiles obtained from crime-scene evidence with legally obtained reference profiles, subject to the requirements and safeguards provided under the proposed Act. At the same time, the use of DNA information presents legitimate concerns involving privacy, confidentiality, data security, consent, unlawful collection, unauthorized access, and misuse of genetic information. The proposed legislation therefore intends to establish clear rules governing the collection, submission, storage, retention, access, disclosure, use, and destruction of DNA samples and profiles. Appropriate safeguards should be incorporated to ensure that the database is utilized strictly for legitimate forensic and law-enforcement purposes and is not used for unauthorized discrimination, surveillance, or other purposes inconsistent with law. The establishment of a national forensic DNA database will also promote greater coordination among the Philippine National Police, National Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice, courts, forensic laboratories, and other authorized government agencies. A unified system can help minimize duplication of forensic records, facilitate lawful information-sharing, and improve the country's capacity to investigate and resolve crimes through scientifically supported evidence. Importantly, DNA evidence should complement—not replace—the constitutional rights of persons accused of crimes. A DNA match must be evaluated together with other evidence and the applicable rules of evidence and procedure. The proposed Act therefore seeks to balance the legitimate needs of law enforcement with the fundamental rights to due process, privacy, and protection against unreasonable searches and seizures. The experience of previous legislative proposals demonstrates the continuing recognition of the importance of establishing a forensic DNA database in the Philippines. Senate Bill No. 1456 of the 19th Congress and Senate Bill No. 357 of the 20th Congress, for example, both proposed legislations establishing a forensic DNA database, with the latter specifically proposing a Philippine National Police forensic DNA database. This measure is therefore intended to provide the Philippines with a modern, scientifically grounded, secure, and accountable forensic DNA infrastructure capable of supporting criminal investigations, improving the identification of offenders and exoneration of innocent persons, assisting in the identification of missing persons and unidentified remains, and strengthening the administration of justice. For these reasons, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. ANTONIO T. KHO REP. ELISA “OLGA” T. label: HB 11366
title: AN ACT REGULATING THE POSSESSION AND OPERATION OF UNMANNED SYSTEMS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid development and widespread availability of unmanned systems have brought significant technological, economic, and social benefits to the Philippines. Unmanned aircraft and other unmanned systems are increasingly being used in agriculture, infrastructure inspection, mapping and surveying, disaster response, environmental monitoring, photography, logistics, research, public safety, and other legitimate activities. At the same time, the increasing accessibility of unmanned systems presents emerging challenges to public safety, national security, privacy, property, and the orderly use of public spaces and airspace. Improper or unauthorized operation may endanger persons and property, interfere with aircraft operations, compromise restricted or sensitive areas, or facilitate other unlawful activities. The Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) has already established regulatory requirements for remotely piloted aircraft systems, including registration, personnel or controller certification, operator requirements, operational limitations, and sanctions for violations. CAAP likewise recognizes the need to ensure that unmanned aircraft operations do not compromise aviation and public safety. However, the continuing development of unmanned technology calls for a comprehensive legislative framework that will complement existing aviation regulations and provide clear rules concerning the possession, registration, operation, use, and accountability of unmanned systems. This measure therefore seeks to establish a national policy governing unmanned systems while respecting the existing mandate of CAAP and other government agencies with jurisdiction over particular applications of unmanned technology. The proposed Act seeks to ensure that persons who possess and operate unmanned systems do so responsibly, safely, and in accordance with established standards. It shall provide appropriate requirements for registration, identification, licensing or certification, and operation, as may be applicable to the type, weight, capability, and intended use of the unmanned system. The measure likewise seeks to establish reasonable restrictions on the operation of unmanned systems in areas where their operation may pose a substantial risk to public safety or security, including airports, aerodromes, restricted or prohibited airspace, government and military installations, correctional facilities, emergency response areas, and other areas designated by competent government authorities. CAAP's existing regulations, for example, recognize different categories of remotely piloted aircraft and impose additional requirements depending on the type of operation. Certain operations may require controller certification, operator certification, or special flight permits, particularly for operations involving controlled or prohibited airspace, nighttime operations, operations beyond visual line of sight, operations near airports, or operations above prescribed altitude limits. The proposed legislation also recognizes that unmanned systems should not be regulated solely from the perspective of aviation. Their operation may affect public order and safety, privacy, national security, telecommunications, environmental protection, and the protection of critical infrastructure. Accordingly, the bill provides for appropriate coordination among CAAP, the Philippine National Police, the Armed Forces of the Philippines, the National Telecommunications Commission, local government units, and other concerned government agencies, within their respective mandates. The measure further seeks to promote responsible use of unmanned systems by establishing clear obligations on owners and operators, including compliance with applicable registration and operational requirements, observance of designated no-fly or restricted areas, maintenance of the unmanned system in safe operating condition, and compliance with lawful instructions issued by competent authorities. The proposed Act shall likewise provide penalties for unauthorized possession or operation, operation in prohibited or restricted areas, reckless or dangerous operation, interference with aircraft or other critical operations, failure to comply with registration or identification requirements, and other acts that may endanger persons, property, public safety, or national security. At the same time, the bill recognizes that regulation must be reasonable, proportionate, and consistent with constitutional rights. Legitimate recreational, educational, scientific, commercial, agricultural, humanitarian, and other lawful uses of unmanned systems should not be unnecessarily restricted. The regulatory framework should therefore distinguish between activities that present different levels of risk and impose requirements proportionate to the nature and circumstances of the operation. The bill also recognizes the increasing use of unmanned systems for disaster response and public service. Government agencies and authorized responders may use unmanned systems for search and rescue, disaster assessment, emergency response, environmental monitoring, and other public- interest purposes, subject to appropriate safety and operational protocols. Furthermore, the proposed legislation shall be implemented in coordination with existing laws and regulations, including Republic Act No. 9497, otherwise known as the “Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008,” and applicable Philippine Civil Aviation Regulations. CAAP is already mandated to establish and prescribe rules and regulations concerning aircraft registration and operations and to enforce laws governing air transportation. The bill therefore does not intend to diminish the authority of CAAP over civil aviation. Rather, it seeks to provide a broader statutory framework for the responsible possession and operation of unmanned systems while preserving the respective mandates of government agencies under existing laws. title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE JONI VILLANUEVA GENERAL HOSPITAL IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BOCAUE, PROVINCE OF BULACAN, INTO A LEVEL III GENERAL HOSPITAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to appropriate hospital care depends not only on the presence of a health facility, but also on whether that facility has the capacity, services, equipment, and personnel required to respond to the needs of the population it serves. The 1987 Constitution directs the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people. Consistent with this mandate, the Universal Health Care Act seeks to ensure that all Filipinos have equitable access to quality and affordable health care services through an integrated and responsive health system. Enacted in 2022, Republic Act No. 11720 established the Joni Villanueva General Hospital (JVGH) in the Municipality of Bocaue, Province of Bulacan, as a Level II general hospital under the direct control and supervision of the Department of Health (DOH). In the years since its establishment under R.A. No. 11720, JVGH has experienced substantial growth in the utilization of its services. Its bed occupancy rate increased from 34.05% in 2023 to 125.97% in 2024 and 119.71% in 2025, and further reached 145.15% as of June 2026. Admissions rose from 656 in 2023 to 10,494 in 2025, while emergency room visits increased from 10,638 to 36,352 and outpatient visits from 26,551 to 60,144 during the same period. This increasing utilization has placed corresponding pressure on the hospital's existing capacity. JVGH currently has a licensed capacity of 100 beds, while its implementing bed capacity as of 2026 already ranges from 120 to 150 beds. The sustained rise in admissions, emergency cases, and outpatient consultations supports the continued expansion not only of bed capacity, but also of hospital facilities, service capability, and human resources. The hospital has already begun developing the institutional capacity required for a higher level of care. Its Hospital Development Plan identifies the progressive strengthening of critical care, specialty services, advanced diagnostics, health human resources, infrastructure, and referral networks as part of its strategic direction toward Level III capability. The plan likewise envisions JVGH as a stronger frontline referral facility for critical cases and expressly includes the pursuit of legislation upgrading the hospital to Level III. The need to upgrade JVGH must likewise be considered in relation to the size and continuing development of the population it serves. Based on the 2024 Census of Population of the Philippine Statistics Authority, Bulacan had a population of 3,876,806 as of 1 July 2024, while Central Luzon had a total population of 12,989,074. Bulacan was the most populous province in the region, accounting for about 29.8% of Central Luzon’s population. Central Luzon’s population increased from 12,422,172 in 2020 to 12,989,074 in 2024, equivalent to an average annual population growth rate of 1.08%. The province’s substantial population, together with continuing urbanization and economic and industrial development, reinforces the need for accessible and adequately distributed hospital facilities capable of providing specialized and subspecialized care. This need is reflected in the Philippine Health Facility Development Plan (PHFDP) 2020–2040, which provides the national strategic framework for health-facility development based on population need, equitable access, and the coordinated expansion of infrastructure, equipment, and human resources for health. For Central Luzon, the PHFDP reported a supply of only 2,094 Level III hospital beds in 2019, against a projected requirement of 8,468 beds by 2025, indicating a gap of 6,374 beds between the reported baseline supply and projected 2025 need. The PHFDP further projects additional requirements of 1,417 Level III or apex beds by 2030, 1,596 by 2035, and 1,793 by 2040, bringing the cumulative Level III bed requirement for Central Luzon for 2025–2040 to 13,274 beds. The regional shortfall is particularly relevant to Bulacan. JVGH is the province’s DOH-retained hospital and presently provides Level II public hospital capability. At the tertiary level, the province has only one Level III hospital, with an authorized bed capacity of 300 beds. Based on the current provincial hospital inventory, Bulacan has 3,008 authorized hospital beds, of which 2,031 are in private facilities and 977 are in public hospitals. Public-sector capacity consists of 577 Level I beds, 100 Level II beds, and 300 Level III beds. The province has 141 intensive care unit beds, only 39 of which are in public hospitals, including 35 in the public Level III hospital. These figures illustrate the limited public tertiary and critical care capacity available to a province of nearly 3.9 million people. The proposed upgrade of JVGH would therefore address more than the needs of a single institution. It would strengthen Bulacan’s public referral network, expand access to higher-level care, and contribute to addressing the broader deficiency in Level III hospital capacity identified for Central Luzon. It is likewise consistent with the development trajectory already set out in the JVGH Hospital Development Plan, which calls for the progressive expansion of infrastructure, equipment, specialty and critical-care services, personnel, and teaching and training capability necessary for Level III operations. This bill therefore seeks to upgrade the Joni Villanueva General Hospital from a Level II to a Level III general hospital, provide for the corresponding upgrading of its professional health care services and facilities, authorize the necessary increase in its workforce, and allow future increases in bed capacity to be guided by its Hospital Development Plan, the Philippine Health Facility Development Plan, and applicable DOH standards. Strengthening a public hospital requires both recognition of present demand and preparation for future need. label: HB 11373
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE LATERAL ENTRY PROGRAM OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 33 OF REPUBLIC ACT 6975, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine National Police (PNP) plays a vital role in maintaining peace and order, protecting lives and property, preventing and investigating crimes, and ensuring public safety. The effectiveness of the police organization depends not only on adequate resources and modern equipment, but also on having a competent, professional, and well- qualified corps of officers and personnel. Republic Act No. 6975, otherwise known as the Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990, provides for the organization and administration of the Philippine National Police. Section 33 thereof provides for the lateral entry of officers into the PNP, particularly for line and technical positions, in recognition of the need to bring into the organization individuals who possess specialized knowledge, skills, training, and professional qualifications that may not be sufficiently available through the regular recruitment and promotion system. However, the existing qualification framework for lateral entry may unduly limit the pool of qualified applicants by recognizing only certain baccalaureate degrees or professional qualifications for particular positions. With the increasingly complex nature of law enforcement, modern policing requires expertise in a broad range of disciplines, including information technology, cybersecurity, forensic science, criminology, psychology, guidance and counselling, medicine, engineering, and other fields relevant to police operations and administration. There is likewise a need to provide greater career mobility and professional advancement opportunities to police non-commissioned officers and non-uniformed personnel who are already in government service. Many of these personnel have acquired relevant baccalaureate degrees, professional licenses, specialized training, and substantial experience in the performance of police and police-support functions. Their institutional knowledge, practical experience, and familiarity with the operations of the PNP constitute valuable assets that should be recognized and utilized in filling appropriate vacancies. The proposed measure therefore seeks to amend Section 33 of Republic Act 6975 to broaden the qualifications for lateral entry into PNP by allowing other appropriate baccalaureate degrees. This will enable the organization to recruit and appoint individuals possessing diverse educational and professional backgrounds necessary for modern and specialized policing. More importantly, the bill seeks to ensure that qualified police non- commissioned officers and non-uniformed personnel already in the service are given meaningful opportunities to qualify for lateral entry into appropriate line and technical officer positions. Such a policy recognizes the principle that career advancement should not be limited by one’s initial mode of entry into the organization, particularly when an incumbent personnel has subsequently obtained the education, qualifications, training, and experience required for a higher position. This measure will also promote merit, competence, professionalism, and equal opportunity within the PNP. By opening lateral entry opportunities to qualified personnel already serving the organization, the PNP can retain experienced and capable individuals while encouraging its personnel to pursue higher education, professional development, and specialized training. The proposed legislation is therefore intended to strengthen the PNP by expanding its pool of qualified officers, maximizing the talents and experience of its existing personnel, and providing equitable opportunities for career advancement. It seeks to ensure that the qualifications for police leadership and technical positions remain responsive to the evolving demands of law enforcement and public safety. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. MAURICIO G. label: HB 11374
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most vital ecological assets. Extending from Cagayan to Quezon, it encompasses forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems that provide essential services for water security, agriculture, livelihoods, infrastructure, and local economies. It also serves as a natural defense against typhoons, flooding, landslides, drought, and other climate-related hazards. Despite its importance, the Sierra Madre continues to face degradation from illegal logging, destructive extraction, incompatible land conversion, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity loss. Its management is likewise dispersed among various agencies, jurisdictions, and regulatory systems, making integrated, range-wide governance difficult. This proposed measure seeks to address these gaps by establishing the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority (SMMRA) as a government-owned or -controlled corporation with an original charter, attached to the Office of the President for policy coordination and administrative supervision. The Authority shall lead the policy, planning, coordination, and regulation of the integrated management of the Sierra Madre, without diminishing the mandates of the DENR, local government units, NCIP, Protected Area Management Boards, and other competent institutions. The bill establishes a 25-year Sierra Madre Ecological Integrity and Sustainable Development Master Plan to provide a unified, science-based framework for ecological limits, management zones, restoration priorities, permitted and prohibited uses, and measurable outcomes. It adopts a landscape-scale, ridge-to-reef approach and a Nature-Based Solutions-First policy for addressing climate, disaster, watershed, and coastal risks. The proposed framework strengthens environmental standards, monitoring, enforcement, restoration obligations, and accountability, while protecting the constitutional and statutory rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including ancestral-domain rights, participation, benefit-sharing, and Free and Prior Informed Consent where applicable. This landmark legislation seeks to establish a permanent, integrated, and accountable framework for the protection and sustainable management of the Sierra Madre Mountain Range. More than an environmental measure, it is an investment in the country’s water and food security, disaster resilience, biodiversity, livelihoods, and long-term national development. By safeguarding the Sierra Madre today, the State protects an ecological foundation upon which present and future generations of Filipinos depend. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 11375
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A PHILIPPINE MEDICAL ACT, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2382, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MEDICAL ACT OF 1959
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 2382, otherwise known as the “Medical Act of 1959,” has governed the practice of medicine in the Philippines for more than six decades. The rapid development of medical science and technology, the changing needs of the health-care system, and the emergence of new modes of medical education and practice necessitate the updating and modernization of the law. This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive Philippine Medical Act that will strengthen the regulation of medical education, internship, licensure, postgraduate training, and the practice of medicine. It creates appropriate institutional mechanisms, including the Medical Education Council, the Professional Regulatory Board of Medicine, and the Postgraduate Medical Education Council, while integrating the medical profession under a national professional organization. The measure also promotes innovative medical education, recognizes telemedicine as part of the practice of medicine, strengthens standards for physician licensure and specialization, and provides safeguards for the welfare, working conditions, and grievance mechanisms of resident and fellow trainees. These reforms are intended to develop competent, ethical, and globally competitive physicians while ensuring that patient welfare, safety, and access to quality health care remain paramount. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine International Trading Corporation (PITC) was created under Presidential Decree No. 252, with its charter subsequently revised by Presidential Decree No. 1071, otherwise known as the “Revised Charter of the Philippine International Trading Corporation.” Under Section 2 of P.D. No. 1071, PITC is authorized to exist for fifty (50) years, with its present corporate term set to expire on 25 January 2027. For decades, PITC has served as a government corporate vehicle in advancing the State’s objectives in international trade, including facilitating trade, promoting Philippine products and enterprises, and supporting government procurement and marketing activities within the scope of its charter. With the impending expiration of its corporate term, there is a need to ensure the continuity of PITC’s juridical personality, operations, contracts, obligations, assets, liabilities, and other lawful commitments. The proposed measure therefore seeks to provide PITC with a perpetual corporate term, unless otherwise provided by law. Perpetual existence, however, shall not exempt PITC from government oversight and accountability. The Corporation shall remain subject to the evaluation, monitoring, and other appropriate actions of the Governance Commission for Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GCG) pursuant to Republic Act No. 10149, or the “GOCC Governance Act of 2011,” and other applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Such evaluation may consider PITC’s relevance, financial viability, operational efficiency, governance, performance, and contribution to Philippine international trade. The proposed measure does not expand PITC’s substantive powers and functions under P.D. No. 1071. Rather, it seeks to provide institutional continuity while preserving the authority of Congress and the appropriate government agencies to evaluate, amend, or otherwise take lawful action concerning the Corporation when warranted. The immediate enactment of this measure will prevent disruption arising from the expiration of PITC’s corporate term and enable the Corporation to continue performing its existing mandate in support of Philippine international trade, subject to continuing government oversight and accountability. In view of the foregoing, the immediate enactment of this measure is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 11381
title: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO BARANGAY TANOD MEMBERS 22 Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 25 SECTION 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the “Barangay Tanod Hazard Pay Act”. 28 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. — The State recognizes the role of the Barangay Tanod, which was duly created under the Local Government Code, as an indispensable instrument in maintaining the peace, safety, and protection of their barangay, even during times of calamity and crisis.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 In February 2025, a barangay tanod in Binondo, Manila, Peton Biazon, was fatally stabbed while responding to an alleged e-bike theft. His death is a tragic reminder that barangay tanods can face serious and life-threatening risks while carrying out their duties to protect their communities. 26 Barangay tanods serve as the eyes and ears of their communities, often the first to respond when help is needed most. While the Local Government Code allows them to receive honoraria, allowances, and other benefits, there is no specific statutory hazard pay recognizing the risks they assume in the performance of their duties. 31 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to provide hazard pay of not less than Five Hundred Pesos (₱500.00) per day to qualified barangay tanods who render service under conditions that expose them to substantial risks to their health, safety, or lives. 35 When they are called upon to respond to emergencies, confront dangerous situations, or remain on duty during calamities, they place their own safety at risk for the safety of others. Their service deserves not only appreciation, but meaningful compensation that recognizes the dangers they willingly face. 40 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 42 43 44 REP. label: HB 11382
title: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO WORKERS IN CRITICAL INDUSTRIES DURING A STATE OF CALAMITY OR EMERGENCY OR PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY 24 Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 27 Section 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the “Hazard Pay for Workers in Critical Industries Act.” 30 SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. — The State shall promote the protection of all workers and ensure their health and safety during a state of calamity or emergency or public health emergency concern. Towards this end, workers in critical industries shall be provided with additional benefit for the duration of these events, taking into account the nature of their functions and exposure to various hazards by reason of their functions.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 When calamity strikes, most people are told to stay home for safety. There are, however, workers who cannot simply “stay home”. While communities seek safety, these workers continue to report for duty, keep hospitals operating, deliver food and medicine, maintain essential utilities, transport people and goods, and ensure that vital services continue. 27 These workers face greater risks to their health and safety precisely when their services are most needed. Their families also bear the worry and uncertainty of having a loved one leave home to serve others during dangerous conditions. 31 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to grant hazard pay equivalent to at least twenty five percent (25%) of the worker's daily basic salary to qualified workers in critical industries who actually render service during a state of calamity, emergency, or public health emergency. The State must, in turn, recognize the sacrifice of those who continue to serve the public in these trying times. Those who keep our communities running in times of calamity and emergency should not be left without additional protection and compensation. Their service is essential, and so is their safety. 39 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 41 42 43 REP. JERNIE JETT V. label: HB 11383
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MANDATORY INSURANCE COVERAGE, BENEFITS AND HAZARD PAY FOR JOURNALISTS, EMPLOYEES OF MEDIA ENTITIES ON FIELD ASSIGNMENTS AND FREELANCE JOURNALISTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES 26 Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 29 Section 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the "Journalists Protection Act of 2026.” 32 SEC. 2. Declaration of Policies and Objectives. - The State recognizes the invaluable role of the free press in the protection and promotion of democracy, good citizenship, civic mindedness, and good governance. Towards this end, the State shall provide the necessary support to ensure that the journalists are properly compensated and insured as they practice their profession.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 Journalists go where the story takes them, even when that means entering places where others are trying to escape. In conflict areas, disaster zones, and other dangerous surroundings, they risk their safety and their lives simply to bring the truth to the public. 26 Behind every journalist who goes into harm's way is a family waiting for their safe return. When injury, disability, or death occurs, the consequences are not borne by the journalist alone, but also by the loved ones who depend on them. 30 This proposed measure seeks to provide mandatory insurance coverage and hazard pay for journalists, field assigned media employees, and qualified freelance journalists exposed to dangerous conditions in the performance of their work. Their duty to inform the public should not come at the cost of leaving them and their families without adequate protection. 36 Those who risk their lives so that the public may know what is happening deserve the assurance that, when the worst happens, they and their families will not be left without support. 40 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 42 43 44 REP. title: AN ACT CREATING A TRIPARTITE COUNCIL TO ADDRESS UNEMPLOYMENT, UNDEREMPLOYMENT, AND THE JOB-SKILLS MISMATCH PROBLEM IN THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR 25 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 28 SECTION 1. Declaration of Policy. – It is declared the policy of the State to promote the sustained development of a skilled citizenry and maintain a reservoir of national talents consisting of Filipino scientists, entrepreneurs, professionals, managers, high-level technical manpower, and skilled workers and craftsmen in all fields. Skills development can reduce unemployment and underemployment, increase productivity, and improve the standards of living. 35 To this end, the State shall ensure the relevance and adequacy of academic courses in the higher education curriculum and training programs offered in technical-vocational institutions in relation to the needs and requirements of the business and industry sectors and the over-all human resource requirement of the country pursuant to its economic development goals. 41 SEC. 2. Creation of a Tripartite Council. – There is hereby established a Tripartite Council, hereinafter referred to as the Council, that shall formulate policies and programs to address the job-skills mismatch in the country. It shall be a coordinating body among the government, academe and industry sectors to primarily monitor economic trends in the global and domestic markets, including those pertaining to business and commerce and the local labor market, and to generate information relative to employment, unemployment, underemployment, and job-skills mismatch. The Council shall be made up of representatives from the government, academe, and industry. 51 The government representatives shall be composed of the following: a Commissioner of the Commission on Higher Education (CHED); a Deputy Director-
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 22 The country already has government agencies responsible for education, technical training, employment, and industry. However, these efforts are handled separately. There is no single body that specifically specializes in regularly bringing government, academe, and industries together to monitor changes in the labor market, identify the skills employers need, and determine whether the courses and training being offered are keeping pace with those needs. 29 Without this coordination, gaps can remain between what students are taught and what the labor market requires. 32 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to create a Tripartite Council composed of representatives from government, academe, and industry. The Council will regularly gather information on employment, unemployment, underemployment, and skills requirements, review existing academic and technical training programs, and recommend policies and programs based on the actual needs of the labor market. 38 Formal education and hands-on training should keep pace with the jobs available, and the skills of Filipino workers should keep pace with the needs of the industries that employ them. 42 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 44 45 46 REP. title: AN ACT REGULATING THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF COMMUNITY FUND POOLING OR PALUWAGAN GROUPS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF 25 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 28 CHAPTER I TITLE AND DEFINITIONS 31 SECTION 1. Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Bagong Paluwagan ng Bayan Act”. 34 SEC. 2. Declaration of Policies. – It is hereby declared the policy of the State to pursue a program that emboldens the people to achieve financial autonomy through capacity building and self- financing activities. The Filipino people shall be encouraged to come together and undertake self-financing activities to inspire them to cultivate a culture of entrepreneurship, meet their basic needs, improve their financial resources, and promote income security. 41 In this regard, the State shall place great importance on facilitating easy and efficient access to necessary funds and credits, which are crucial elements in realizing the people's aspirations towards financial stability and self-reliance. 45 To achieve this end, the paluwagan, a traditional community fund pooling system for savings and investments, shall be formalized and strengthened for the protection and benefit of the people. Through this system, the people shall have access to affordable credit and financial assistance, and shall be empowered to engage in entrepreneurial activities and other forms of self-sustenance. 51 SEC. 3. Definitions. – As used in this Act: (a) Community Paluwagan refers to a small group of persons with residence or employment in a defined community, created in accordance with the
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 22 Every payday, Ana sets aside ₱500 for her paluwagan. She does this faithfully because she hopes that when her turn comes, the money will be enough to pay her child’s school expenses. She trusts the person keeping the contributions because the group is made up of people from her own community. 27 But when the time comes to collect her share, she learns that the money is no longer there. The person who managed the contributions has disappeared, leaving Ana and the other members with little protection and no clear way to recover their savings. 31 This is the risk faced by many Filipinos who rely on informal paluwagan arrangements. While paluwagan can help people save and access money for their needs, the absence of a clear legal framework and government supervision as well as intervention, when appropriate, can leave members vulnerable to fraud, misuse of funds, and poor financial management. 37 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to establish rules for the organization and operation of community paluwagan, provide supervision and safeguards for members' contributions, and give registered groups access to affordable credit, insurance, financial education, and entrepreneurship programs to make better use of the contributions without affecting liquidity. 43 For families who save what little they can, every contribution matters. Their trust and hard-earned money deserve protection. 46 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 48 49 50 REP. JERNIE JETT V. title: AN ACT PRESERVING THE INDIGENOUS GAMES OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR 23 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 26 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Philippine Indigenous Games Preservation Act.” 29 SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. – Article II, Section 22 of the Constitution provides that the State shall recognize and promote the rights of indigenous cultural communities within the framework of national unity and development. Furthermore, Article 31.1 of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples enjoins all State signatories to take effective measures to recognize and protect the exercise of the indigenous peoples’ rights which include the maintenance, control, and development of their cultural heritage, traditional knowledge and expression, oral traditions, literatures, designs, sports, and traditional games. 39 Pursuant to the aforesaid mandates, it is incumbent upon the State to lay down specific policy directives to promote the interest of our indigenous peoples, preserve the intangible cultural heritage as living heritage and help people connect with their historical roots. The State shall take the necessary steps to preserve the indigenous peoples’ games which serve as the best avenue for their self- expression, and for promoting peace, harmony, goodwill, and camaraderie among them. 47 SEC. 3. Indigenous Games. – The term “indigenous games” refer to the traditional sports and games distinctly connected and rooted in the traditions, customs, and practices, and reflect the rich cultural heritage of the different indigenous cultural communities or indigenous peoples, handed down from generation to generation such as bunong braso, ginnuyudan, hilahang lubid, kadang-kadang, karera sa sako, luksong-tinik, patintero, syato, unggoy-unggoyan. These include
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 22 The State has a responsibility to ensure that this heritage is not lost to modernization and changing ways of life. When an indigenous game disappears, a part of the culture and knowledge carried by generations may disappear with it. 26 Preserving these games therefore means preserving our cultural diversity, strengthening the identity of indigenous communities, and ensuring that future generations remain connected to their roots and the story behind it. 30 This proposed measure now seeks to preserve and promote indigenous games through regular competitions, educational activities, documentation, research, and continued community participation, in consultation with the indigenous peoples to whom these traditions belong. Cultural heritage is not only something to be remembered. It is something that must be kept alive. 36 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 38 39 40 REP. label: HB 11388
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE SAFE STORAGE AND SECURE CUSTODY OF FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10591, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “COMPREHENSIVE FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION REGULATION ACT,” AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 10591, the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, governs who may own a firearm in this country. It says almost nothing about what an owner must do with that firearm for the remaining hours of the day. Section 9 of the Act disposes of the entire question of safekeeping in a single sentence: that “a vault or a container secured by lock and key or other security measures” is an acceptable requirement. It fixes no standard for that container, imposes no continuing duty of custody, and attaches no consequence whatsoever to an owner or an accountable custodian whose carelessness places a deadly weapon within the reach of a child, a person in crisis, or a criminal. A locked drawer and a bank-grade safe are, under present law, legally indistinguishable. That silence has a body count. On June 22, 2026, two minors aged fifteen and fourteen opened fire at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, killing three students and injuring twenty others, fifteen of them by gunfire. The weapons were a Glock 17 pistol that was the service firearm of a Philippine National Police officer related to one of the assailants, and a .38-caliber revolver registered to a private security agency in Cebu City but kept in the home of a former security guard. On August 18, 2026, a minor killed two students and wounded nine others at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University Junior High School, livestreaming the attack; the firearm was issued by the Bureau of Customs to his father. Between these events, authorities intercepted a fourteen-year-old at Lut-od National High School in Pinamungajan, Cebu, carrying a revolver said to belong to his grandfather. On September 18, 2026, a Grade 9 student opened fire at Banga National High School in South Cotabato, killing and wounding fellow students before taking his own life. These four incidents share a pattern that this Congress should find intolerable. In no case was the firearm a loose or black-market weapon. Every one of them was a firearm the State itself had licensed, registered, or issued — and in three of the four, the firearm had been placed in the custody of a public officer or a security professional. This is the gap the present measure closes, and it closes it at the point where the evidence says the failure actually occurs. This measure addresses the narrower and more tractable problem to which the last four tragedies point: the licensed, registered, and government-issued firearm that was lawfully acquired and then left within reach of a child. That firearm is already in the State’s records. Its custodian is already known. The only thing missing is a duty and a consequence. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTONINO B. It says almost nothing about what an owner must do with that firearm for the remaining hours of the day. Section 9 of the Act disposes of the entire question of safekeeping in a single sentence: that “a vault or a container secured by lock and key or other security measures” is an acceptable requirement. It fixes no standard for that container, imposes no continuing duty of custody, and attaches no consequence whatsoever to an owner or an accountable custodian whose carelessness places a deadly weapon within the reach of a child, a person in crisis, or a criminal. A locked drawer and a bank-grade safe are, under present law, legally indistinguishable. That silence has a body count. On June 22, 2026, two minors aged fifteen and fourteen opened fire at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, killing three students and injuring twenty others, fifteen of them by gunfire. label: HB 11393
title: AN ACT ENHANCING CLIMATE RESILIENCE IN AGRICULTURE TO ADVERSE CLIMATE EVENTS BY INSTITUTIONALIZING THE USE OF CROP CLIMATE CALENDARS, EQUIPPING FARMERS FOR CLIMATE- SENSITIVE DECISION-MAKING, AND PROVIDING ACCESS TO LOCALIZED WEATHER AND CLIMATE INFORMATION
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is highly vulnerable to climate-related hazards that threaten agricultural production, rural livelihoods, and food security. From 2012 to 2022, adverse weather and climate events caused average annual damages of approximately ₱44 billion to the country’s agriculture sector. Agriculture accounted for about 60 percent of total disaster-related property damage, making it the sector most affected by extreme climate events. 1 The continuing vulnerability of the sector is further demonstrated by data from the Department of Agriculture showing that agricultural production losses reached approximately ₱57.78 billion in 2024. These losses were attributed to El Niño, tropical cyclones, pests and diseases, volcanic activity, and other weather-related events. They affected approximately 1.4 million farmers and fisherfolk, damaged an estimated 993,823 hectares of agricultural land, and resulted in the loss of approximately 2.18 million metric tons of agricultural production.2 The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events— including droughts, typhoons, floods, excessive rainfall, and prolonged periods of extreme heat—have caused substantial damage to crops, livestock, fisheries, agricultural infrastructure, and farm livelihoods. These events 1 Galang, Ivory Myka R., and Roehlano M. Briones. Culprit and Victim: Scenarios for Philippine Agriculture amidst Climate Change. PIDS Discussion Paper Series No. 2024-36, Philippine Institute for Development Studies, December 20, 2024. https://doi.org/10.62986/dp2024.36 2 Rappler. “Agri Losses Due to Calamities Hit P57.8 Billion in 2024.” Rappler, January 29, 2025. https://www.rappler.com/philippines/agriculture-losses-record-2024-due-calamities/ disrupt planting and harvesting schedules, reduce productivity, increase production costs, and threaten the stability of the country’s food supply. Climate change further intensifies these risks. Farmers, particularly smallholder farmers and those dependent on rain-fed agriculture, often make critical production decisions without timely, accessible, and location-specific information on weather and climate conditions. Without appropriate guidance on the timing of land preparation, planting, crop management, harvesting, and other farm activities, farmers may be exposed to avoidable losses. There is, therefore, an urgent need to strengthen the country’s institutional capacity for climate-resilient agriculture. The use of crop climate calendars can help align agricultural activities with local climate conditions, seasonal weather patterns, and projected climate risks. When combined with localized weather forecasts, climate advisories, early-warning systems, and appropriate technical assistance, these tools can enable farmers to make better-informed and climate-sensitive decisions. This measure recognizes that farmers must be at the center of the country’s climate adaptation and disaster-risk-reduction efforts. It seeks to institutionalize the development, updating, dissemination, and use of crop climate calendars for major crops and production areas; provide farmers with accessible and understandable weather and climate information; strengthen coordination among relevant government agencies, local government units, academic institutions, research organizations, and civil society organizations; and equip farmers with the knowledge and tools necessary to adjust their production practices in response to changing climate conditions. By promoting timely and localized decision-making, the proposed measure will help reduce production losses, improve agricultural planning, strengthen food security, and protect the livelihoods of farmers and fisherfolk. It will also support the adoption of climate-smart and science-based agricultural practices while ensuring that national climate-resilience initiatives respond to the actual conditions and needs of local farming communities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11394
title: AN ACT CREATING A SYSTEM OF PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PEOPLE’S COUNCIL IN EVERY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Democratic governance is strengthened when citizens are given meaningful opportunities to participate in decisions that directly affect their communities. Civil society organizations—including people’s organizations, non- government organizations, labor groups, community organizations, professional associations, foundations, and other organized citizens—provide valuable knowledge, experience, and perspectives that can help the government identify local needs and develop more responsive policies. The proposed measure recognizes CSOs as partners in local governance and seeks to create a formal system through which their participation can become more consistent, organized, and effective. It defines CSOs and people’s organizations and establishes a registration system for qualified organizations operating within cities and municipalities. The bill proposes the establishment of a Local People’s Council in every local government unit, composed of accredited CSOs, to provide an institutional mechanism for citizen participation in local governance. Registered CSOs would be able to participate in joint undertakings with local governments involving basic services, capacity-building, livelihood, economic, environmental, cultural, and good-governance projects. The measure also provides for a convention of accredited CSOs to facilitate the organization of the Local People’s Council and requires the local Sanggunian to recognize the Council upon compliance with the prescribed requirements. The proposed People’s Councils are intended to give organized citizens a substantive role in the formulation and implementation of local policies and programs. Upon recognition, the Councils may elect or appoint representatives to LGU boards, councils, committees, task forces, and other special bodies; observe and participate in government deliberations; vote where authorized; evaluate government projects and activities; and propose legislation. The bill likewise provides for representation at the provincial level, thereby creating a mechanism through which community-level concerns can be elevated into broader local policy discussions.1 This framework builds upon Article XIII, Section 15 of the Constitution, which recognizes the role of independent and autonomous people’s organizations in enabling citizens to pursue and protect their legitimate and collective interests and aspirations through peaceful and lawful means. Meaningful participation, however, requires both institutional channels and practical means for citizens to communicate with the government. The bill therefore directs LGUs to provide the necessary facilities for the participation of People’s Councils, requires funding for CSO capacity-building and Council operations, and establishes information boards and suggestion boxes in accessible public places, with LGUs required to respond to suggestions within fifteen working days. By institutionalizing these mechanisms, the measure seeks to transform citizen participation from an occasional exercise into a continuing partnership between communities and local governments, promoting greater transparency, responsiveness, accountability, and public ownership of local development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11395
title: AN ACT TO INSTITUTIONALIZE AND ENCOURAGE PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN AGRICULTURE VILLAGE FARM MANAGEMENT (AVFM) ENTERPRISES AND SMALLHOLD FARMERS AND FISHERFOLKS IN ORDER TO HASTEN THE DOUBLING OF RURAL HOUSEHOLD INCOMES THROUGH THEIR ADOPTION OF BETTER PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, MARKETING, LOGISTICS AND FINANCING TECHNOLOGIES, AND BY ESTABLISHING ECONOMIES OF SCALE THROUGH SYNCHRONIZED COMMUNITY AGRICULTURE AND CONSOLIDATION OF PRODUCTION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State provides that it shall empower the agriculture and fisheries sectors to develop and sustain themselves by promoting industrialization and full employment based on sound agricultural development and agrarian reform and through market-oriented policies in agricultural production. For decades, the Government has introduced and implemented many affirmative action and support programs to help the Filipino farmers. Billion pesos in taxpayers' money have been spent on a wide array of programs and projects with the intent of boosting Philippine agriculture from its low levels of productivity. Most of the agriculture support programs have centered on government agencies providing not only the policy guidance and technology choices but also the personnel and extension workers, resources and inputs, credit and funding. Despite all the government initiatives and assistance in the agricultural sector, for most small-hold farmers, innovation and technology adoption have not advanced successfully. The country’s overall annual agricultural output reportedly shrank due to the decline in fisheries, livestock and crop production1. This Act seeks to adopt and encourage a new approach and direction in the development of the country’s rural sector with the objective of doubling our farmers’ incomes by capitalizing on the resources and technical expertise of professional agriculturists. It seeks to promote productivity-enhancing partnerships between small-hold farmers and the proposed Agriculture Village Farm Management (AVFM) enterprises formed by professional agriculturists and private sector investors. By linking the production and the marketing side of agriculture, this bill hopes to address the long-standing gaps of fragmented efforts of the State to alleviate the overall agricultural status of the country. If properly enacted, the bill should serve as a pillar for Filipino farmers in improving not only their income but also in ensuring sustainable agricultural and environmental practices, and most importantly in ensuring food security for every Filipino. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. VARGAS Fifth District, Quezon City 1 Business World. label: HB 11401
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE COMPREHENSIVE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM ABUSE, NEGLECT, AND EXPLOITATION AND PROMOTION OF THEIR OVERALL HEALTH AND WELFARE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE “Ang kabataan ang pag-asa ng bayan.” This has been a line that has been used repeatedly to the point of cliché. However, it rings true then and it still rings true today. The youth will be the next nation builders of the Philippines. It is then necessary to realize that policies we will make today will ultimately affect them significantly in the future. Unfortunately, it is also a reality that their sector has been and is currently one of those marginalized and exploited. Their youth is sometimes seen as an instrument and opportunity for abuse. At least 17,600 cases of child abuse were reported in 2023 alone, with many such cases violating Republic Act No. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination.1 If we are going to believe in the potential that the youth has, it is equally important that they be protected from all kinds of abuse. The next generation is, and will still be, worth fighting for. It is for these reasons, and to strengthen the R.A. 7610, that further robust protection is given to children and the youth. It is for the foregoing premises that the approval of this Bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11402
title: AN ACT SETTING MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR THE OPERATION OF INTERNET CAFES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE It is an understatement when one says that technology has impacted our lives. Breakthroughs in communications technology, computing, and entertainment have significantly improved our lives and has enabled many individuals to pursue aspirations that were never thought of to be possible. As technology became faster, smaller, and cheaper more people have come into contact with it. With the rise of the internet and technology, internet cafes also sprouted one after the other. These internet cafes became community hubs in which this groundbreaking technology is made more accessible to the general populace. It is not far off to say that internet cafes are of vital importance in the daily lives of the people. Thus, it is the duty of the State to enact standards and regulations to see to it that these community hubs continue to perform their stated functions for the general populace in a safe and orderly manner; and to ensure that these facilities are used responsibly towards meaningful ends. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is urgently sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11403
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10870 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE CREDIT CARD INDUSTRY REGULATION LAW
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Due to the advancement of technology, it cannot be denied that the use of credit cards has become indispensable in making consumer credit readily available to all Filipinos. It allowed Filipinos to transact conveniently without the need to shell out cash, plan purchases, and subsequently avail of advantageous rates in their purchases. With this growth in credit card use, some Filipinos have been taken advantaged by malicious and nefarious groups by noting their credit card information and details and have used these cards for their own gain. Fraudsters can get hold of one’s personal information in many ways, from hacking retailers to buying one’s data on the dark web, a shady corner of the internet that’s not accessible via search engines like Google. Or criminals can trick one into handing over your information through online scams. This is why we need to introduce more measures to protect consumers who are availing these credit card services. While there are laws currently in place that already aim to protect the consumers, the growing number of people being victimized despite these measures shows the need to introduce further programs and practices that will allow the public to trust the banking system and the convenience of using credit cards. It is for these foregoing premises that approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11404
title: AN ACT TO PROTECT FILIPINOS FROM THE HARMFUL EFFECTS OF TRANS- FATTY ACIDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) killed 43 million people in 2021, equivalent to 75% of all non-pandemic-related deaths globally.1 In the Philippines, NCDs account for 68% of all deaths and is the number one cause of mortality and morbidity in the country.2 One in every three Filipinos is likely to die before the age of 70 from one of the four major NCDs: cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory diseases. CVDs, particularly coronary heart disease (CHD), account for nearly half of the world’s NCD related deaths. 2021 data shows that over 700,00 deaths in the country were due to NCDs,3 and is still trending upwards and may account more larger and larger share of premature deaths.4 High intake of trans-fatty acids (TFA) increases the risk of death from any cause by 34% and CHD mortality and morbidity by as much as 23% and 28%, respectively. Every year, more than half a million deaths are attributed to TFA globally. Dubbed as the “tobacco of nutrition,” TFA has no health benefits and is completely replaceable with no difference in taste or cost of food. Thus, the WHO published the REPLACE Technical Action Package as a road map towards a trans-fat free world. Denmark, Argentina, Thailand and Singapore have introduced policies to limit TFA consumption by banning partially hydrogenated oils (PHOs), the major source of TFA, and/or limiting TFA content in food. Countries that regulated TFA 1 Noncommunicable Diseases, World Health Organization, 25 September 2025, available at: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/noncommunicable-diseases 2 Health Philippines Alliance, available at: https://phealthalliance.ph/ncds-tracker/ 3 Ibid 4 Dexter Cabalza, “WHO: Premature death risk due to NCDs in PH among highest in region,” Inquirer, 18 October 2024, available at: https://globalnation.inquirer.net/252790/risk-of- premature-deaths-in-ph-due-to-ncds-among-highest-in-western-pacific-region have seen a significant decline in CHD deaths. Denmark’s regulation limiting TFA content to 2g per 100g of fat in food products contributed to a 75% reduction in CHD- related deaths. In Argentina, an estimated 301 to 1,517 cardiac deaths every year were averted by eliminating industrially-produced TFA, saving the government as much as USD 87 million in healthcare costs annually. The FDA Circular No.2021-028-A effectively banned TFA and is geared towards eliminating industrially-produced Trans-Fatty Acids (TFA) in the Philippines food supply chain.5 This Act aims to once and for all forbit TFA in the Philippine food supply chain. The importance of addressing the problem of CHDs and CVDs as a whole has never been more pronounced than now, as we recover from the pandemic early this decade, and pose to tackle emerging health risks as both the food industry and Filipino diet evolve. Now more than ever, the need for preventative health care and healthy lifestyle promotion must be realized in line with the vision of universal health care. According to the WHO, TFA elimination is considered as one of the simplest and most straightforward public health interventions to reduce the risk of CVDs and improve nutritional quality of diets. As more countries regulate TFA, countries without regulations become vulnerable to dumping of TFA-rich imported food. Together, let us protect all Filipinos from the harmful effects of TFA and promote healthy hearts for all. It is for these foregoing reasons that the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11405
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE PERSONNEL ECONOMIC RELIEF ALLOWANCE OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In light of the consistently high inflation rate along with increases in various tax rates, the insufficient amount of the Personnel Economic Relief Allowance (PERA) of public school teachers has now become an alarming issue. In addition to the insufficiency, public school teachers, through the latest Salary Standardization Law (SSL) updates, only saw superficial grants vis-à-vis those granted to our uniformed personnel. As such, it has become necessary to grant the much-deserved increase in the benefits given to our public school teachers. Considering that the lowest salary grade available to teachers (i.e. Salary Grade 11 for Teacher I), after the first tranche of increase through the latest SSL falls far below the approximate living wage for a family of five, it is appropriate to increase the PERA of public school teachers by an amount which would, at the very least, initially cover for the said discrepancy. Hence, it is proposed in this Bill that the PERA granted to public school teachers must be increased to at least P8,000, an amount which would, at the onset, substantially cover the disproportion between the current monthly wage of public school teachers and the approximated living wage in the Philippines for a family of five. The State, through this increase, will be able to demonstrate its full commitment in enhancing and uplifting the living and working conditions of its employees, particularly those in the field of education. It is for the foregoing premises that the approval of this Bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11406
title: AN ACT PROVIDING TAX RELIEF IN AREAS UNDER A STATE OF CALAMITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Natural and human-induced calamities repeatedly inflict heavy loss of life, property damage, and prolonged disruption of basic services and local economies. In their wake, families and enterprises face severe cash flow stress from lost income and destroyed assets, even as tax obligations remain due and enforceable. This mismatch slows recovery and delays the return of normal economic activity. This measure establishes a predictable system of tax relief in areas placed under a state of calamity. It authorizes time-bound and clearly defined interventions that ease immediate burdens while preserving government revenues in the medium term, namely: 1. Extension of deadlines for filing returns and paying national taxes; 2. Suspension of penalties, surcharges, and interest during the relief period; 3. Deferment or partial waiver of tax obligations when warranted by the extent of damage and loss; 4. Suspension of the assessment and collection of real property taxes in affected localities for one fiscal year, with payments to resume afterward in staggered installments. To support private relief and rehabilitation efforts, the bill also grants an automatic exemption from donor’s tax for donations intended for calamity victims, subject to a ceiling that not more than ten percent of the donated amount may be used for administrative expenses. The policy goal is simple and practical: give disaster-stricken communities immediate fiscal breathing room so they can rebuild livelihoods, restore services, and restart local commerce, while setting clear rules for the resumption of obligations once minimal stability returns. By institutionalizing timely and targeted tax relief, the State affirms its duty to advance social justice, protect vulnerable sectors, and strengthen economic resiliency through partnership with local governments and the private sector. In view of the foregoing, the early passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. JAIME EDUARDO MARC D. label: HB 11407
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE AUTHORIZED BED CAPACITY OF THE CONGRESSMAN ENRIQUE "HENRY" M. COJUANGCO MEMORIAL DISTRICT HOSPITAL IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF MONCADA, PROVINCE OF TARLAC, FROM SEVENTEEN (17) TO ONE HUNDRED (100) BEDS, UPGRADING ITS FACILITIES, SERVICES, AND MANPOWER, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Congressman Enrique "Henry" M. Cojuangco Memorial District Hospital (CEHMCDH) located in San Julian, Moncada, Tarlac, serves as a vital healthcare lifeline for its primary catchment areas spanning five (5) municipalities in Tarlac (Moncada, Paniqui, Anao, Pura, and San Manuel) and two (2) municipalities in Nueva Ecija (Cuyapo and Nampicuan), serving hundreds of thousands of residents. Since assuming office, the hospital administration of CEHMCDH has observed a steady and critical surge in its Bed Occupancy Rate (BOR) over the past several years. From 71.09% in 2022, the BOR rose sharply to 95.83% in 2023 and reached 176.87% in 2024. Currently, for the calendar year, the bed occupancy rate is an alarming 238%, forcing the hospital to use hallways as temporary areas to accommodate patients. Furthermore, the current nurse-to-patient ratio and overall manpower are severely stretched, structurally ill-suited to its meager authorized bed capacity of 17 beds. With the massive influx of patients and the expanding health demands of the community, the existing 17-bed capacity is grossly inadequate to deliver efficient, effective, and quality medical care. Upgrading the authorized bed capacity to one hundred (100) beds, alongside the corresponding enhancement of its facilities, medical equipment, and professional workforce, is an urgent necessity to bridge these healthcare gaps and ease the burden on both patients and healthcare providers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. JAIME EDUARDO MARC D.
