title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING BAMBOO AS A HIGH-VALUE AND INDUSTRIAL CROP, FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE HIGH-VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT ACT BY INSTITUTIONALIZING THE NATIONAL HIGH- VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT AND BIOECONOMY PROGRAM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7900, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HIGH-VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT ACT OF 1995”” 22
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 24 Republic Act No. 7900, or the High-Value Crops Development Act of 1995, established the national framework for the production, processing, marketing and distribution of high-value crops. Three decades later, climate change, biotechnology, plant-variety innovation, stricter product standards, supply-chain disruptions and growing demand for renewable and bio-based materials require a more integrated, science-based, market-oriented and institutionally sustained approach. 31 This bill expressly includes bamboo as a high-value crop and recognizes it as a strategic industrial crop. Bamboo can provide food, fiber, biomass, engineered and construction materials, furniture, packaging, bioenergy, biochar, biomaterials, and other value-added products. Developed through appropriate agroforestry and multi- storey farming systems, it can diversify rural livelihoods and support climate, soil, water, and ecosystem objectives, subject to environmental, biodiversity, land-use, agrarian reform and ancestral-domain laws. 39 The measure establishes within the Department of Agriculture the Office of the Undersecretary for High-Value Crops Development, Innovation, and Bioeconomy. The Office shall provide policy guidelines on technology management and innovation, exercise direct oversight over the National High-Value Crops and Bioeconomy Development Program, and supervise the functional roles, mandates and performance of its component offices. The bill also proposes the creation of one (1) Assistant Secretary position to support the Undersecretary and lead the agricultural statistics and data science, knowledge management, market intelligence, geospatial services, monitoring, evaluation and results reporting. A National High-Value Crops Program Management Office will be created and headed by Director position to coordinate implementation, provide technical services, farming systems, bamboo and industrial- crop development, agribusiness, processing, standards, investment, and markets. 13 The bill further integrates research, innovation, biotechnology, genetic resources, plant-variety development, quality planting materials, climate-resilient production, integrated development areas, processing, enterprise development, financing, standards, trade, and agricultural bioeconomy applications. It strengthens the High-Value Crops Development Fund and permits the Department to propose an indicative initial program envelope of Fifty Billion Pesos to support the five-year implementation of the act, subject to the regular budget process and without creating an automatic appropriation. 22 The proposed structure is designed as an integrating and coordinating mechanism. It preserves the statutory mandates of the Philippine Statistics Authority and other competent regulatory, research, standards, environmental, and local- government institutions, while requiring compliance with government-optimization, civil service, position-classification, budgeting, accounting and auditing laws. 28 In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. 30 31 JOSE MANUEL F. label: HB 11487
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION, CONSERVATION, AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE SIERRA MADRE MOUNTAIN RANGE, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE SIERRA MADRE MOUNTAIN RANGE AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most important natural assets. Stretching from Cagayan in the north to Quezon in the south, it forms a vast interconnected landscape of forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems. Its ecological functions extend far beyond the mountain range itself, providing essential services that sustain communities, agriculture, water systems, infrastructure, livelihoods, and economic activities in both upland and downstream areas. The Sierra Madre likewise serves as a critical natural defense against typhoons, flooding, landslides, storm surges, drought, and other climate-related hazards. Its forests, watersheds, wetlands, riparian areas, ecological corridors, and coastal ecosystems regulate water flows, store and sequester carbon, support biodiversity, and contribute to the resilience of communities and critical infrastructure. The protection and restoration of the Sierra Madre are therefore not merely matters of environmental conservation, but matters of national development, public safety, water security, climate resilience, and national security. Despite its importance, the Sierra Madre remains vulnerable to continuing degradation arising from illegal logging, destructive extraction, incompatible land conversion, habitat fragmentation, biodiversity loss, and other activities that undermine ecological integrity. Existing governmental mandates and management arrangements, while important, operate through different agencies, jurisdictions, plans, and regulatory systems. Such fragmentation makes it difficult to manage the Sierra Madre as one interconnected ecological system and to consistently account for impacts that cross administrative boundaries. This proposed measure seeks to address this institutional and ecological gap by establishing the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority (SMMRA) as a government- owned or -controlled corporation with an original charter, attached to the Office of the President for policy coordination and administrative supervision. The Authority is envisioned as the lead policy, planning, coordinating, and regulatory body for range-wide ecological governance, while preserving the lawful mandates of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), local government units, Protected Area Management Boards, the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, and other competent institutions. At the center of the proposed framework is the Sierra Madre Ecological Integrity and Sustainable Development Master Plan, a comprehensive, science-based, geospatially explicit, 25-year plan that will establish ecological limits, management zones, no-go areas, permitted and prohibited uses, restoration priorities, measurable outcomes, investment requirements, and implementation responsibilities. The Master Plan will provide a common framework for harmonizing national, regional, local, ancestral-domain, and sectoral plans affecting the Sierra Madre. The measure adopts a landscape-scale and ridge-to-reef approach to conservation. Rather than treating forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems 1 as isolated units, the proposed framework recognizes their ecological and hydrological interdependence. It provides for the identification and protection of ecological corridors, riparian buffers, critical habitats, key biodiversity areas, and other connectivity systems necessary to maintain biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. The bill further advances a Nature-Based Solutions-First policy. Government interventions addressing flooding, landslides, erosion, watershed degradation, water insecurity, coastal hazards, and climate risks will be required to consider the feasibility of nature-based, green, or green-gray solutions before relying solely on conventional infrastructure. The proposed approach recognizes natural ecosystems as functional infrastructure capable of providing long-term disaster-risk reduction, water-security, and climate-adaptation benefits. Recognizing that conservation cannot be sustained without viable communities and economic incentives, the proposed measure promotes sustainable livelihoods, including agroforestry, ecotourism, and sustainable non-timber forest products. It also provides avenues for Indigenous Peoples, upland communities, and lawful tenure holders to participate in conservation and restoration activities and benefit from verified ecological outcomes. A significant innovation of the measure is the establishment of a Sierra Madre Nature Credit System. The system is intended to create a transparent and independently verified mechanism through which measurable protection, restoration, biodiversity, watershed, water- security, and climate-resilience outcomes may be recognized and financed. Covered enterprises that materially depend upon Sierra Madre ecosystem services may be required to satisfy Nature Credit Purchase Obligations, thereby helping align economic activity with the ecological services upon which such activity depends. The system expressly does not authorize prohibited activities or substitute for environmental, tenure, protected-area, or Indigenous Peoples safeguards. To support the long-term implementation of the law, the bill establishes a Sierra Madre Fund and provides for lawful and transparent financing mechanisms, including national government appropriations, certain environmental charges, penalties and restoration recoveries when legally assignable, grants and technical assistance, and other lawful sources. The Fund is limited to the Authority’s statutory public-good and market-governance functions and is subject to government accounting, procurement, auditing, transparency, and disclosure requirements. The measure also strengthens accountability by establishing ecological standards, monitoring systems, restoration obligations, environmental liability mechanisms, and stronger prohibitions against destructive ac

label: HB 11488
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXTENSION OF TERMS OF PROTECTION OF COPYRIGHT AND RELATED RIGHTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 213 AND 215 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES"
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines, or Republic Act No. 8293, provides protection to authors, performers, producers of sound recordings, and broadcasting organizations for their creative works and contributions. The existing law provides specific periods of protection for copyright and related rights, which this measure seeks to strengthen in view of the continuing development of the creative and digital industries. This measure seeks to extend the period of copyright protection for works covered under Sections 172 and 173 of Republic Act No. 8293 from fifty (50) years to seventy-five (75) years. It likewise extends the protection for photographic works and audio-visual works to seventy-five (75) years. For performers and producers of sound recordings, the period of protection is similarly proposed to be extended from fifty (50) years to seventy-five (75) years. The protection granted to broadcasting organizations is also proposed to be increased from twenty (20) years to fifty (50) years. The extension of these terms will provide Filipino authors, performers, producers, and other rights holders with a longer period within which they may benefit from their creative works. For performers and producers, in particular, a longer period of protection will allow them to continue receiving economic benefits from works that may remain commercially valuable for many years after their creation or initial release. It will likewise provide rights holders greater opportunity to recover investments made in the creation, production, marketing, and distribution of creative works. By strengthening the period of protection granted to creative works and related rights, this measure seeks to provide greater incentives for the creation, dissemination, preservation, and continued commercial exploitation of Filipino works. It will likewise contribute to the development of the Philippine creative industry, encourage investment in creative works, and help ensure that Filipino creators and rights holders continue to benefit from their intellectual and artistic contributions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMOB.B.RODRIGUEZ, MAXIMO RODRIGUEZ,JR. JR. label: HB 11489
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE RECRUITMENT, HIRING, AND TRAINING OF SCHOOL-BASED LICENSED GUIDANCE COUNSELORS, PSYCHOLOGISTS, SCHOOL SOCIAL WORKERS AND MENTAL HEALTH PERSONNEL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The mental health and psychosocial well-being of students are essential to their ability to learn, develop, and participate meaningfully in school and community life. Schools are often among the first places where behavioral, emotional, social, and psychological difficulties among children and young people may be identified. This measure seeks to provide public elementary and secondary schools with additional personnel who can provide counseling, psychosocial support, early intervention, referral, and other appropriate services to students. It likewise recognizes the important role of teachers, school personnel, and parents in identifying concerns and supporting the overall well-being of students. By strengthening the availability of qualified professionals within schools, the proposed Act aims to address mental, emotional, behavioral, and psychosocial concerns at an earlier stage and help create a more supportive learning environment. The measure therefore provides for the recruitment and training of appropriate school-based personnel, establishes supervision and service guidelines, and provides the necessary funding through the annual General Appropriations Act. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 11490
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHTS OF PATIENTS AGAINST HOSPITAL DETENTION ON THE GROUND OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS AND MEDICAL EXPENSES AND PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9439, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Patients should not be deprived of their liberty, nor should their families be prevented from securing their release or obtaining necessary medical documents, solely because of their inability to immediately settle hospital bills and medical expenses. Republic Act No. 9439, otherwise known as the “Anti-Hospital Detention Law”, was enacted to protect patients from being detained in hospitals and medical clinics on account of unpaid hospital bills or medical expenses. Despite the protection provided by law, cases continue to arise where patients and their families experience difficulty securing discharge, obtaining medical documents, or claiming benefits. There is therefore a need to strengthen the safeguards provided under the law and ensure that its protections are effectively implemented. This measure seeks to expressly prohibit the detention of patients, their relatives, representatives, or caregivers, as well as the withholding of newborn children, solely on account of unpaid hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees. It likewise seeks to ensure the prompt release of the remains of deceased patients and the timely issuance of the necessary documents. The bill further provides reasonable mechanisms by which financially incapacitated patients may secure their unpaid obligations. The enactment of this measure will strengthen the protection of patients and their families, promote humane and dignified treatment in health facilities, and ensure that inability to immediately pay for medical treatment does not become a ground for unlawful detention or withholding of essential documents. For these reasons, the immediate passage of this bill is urgently sought. REP. EDUARDO R. label: HB 11491
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY FRAMEWORK, ENSURING THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF LEARNERS AND SCHOOL PERSONNEL, AND PROMOTING A SAFE AND SUPPORTIVE SCHOOL COMMUNITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every learner has the right to study in an environment that is safe, healthy, inclusive, and supportive. Schools should not only provide quality education but also protect learners and school personnel from violence, abuse, bullying, discrimination, harassment, disasters, health emergencies, and other threats to their safety and well-being. The continuing prevalence of violence and bullying among children underscores the need to strengthen school safety measures. The 2015 National Baseline Study on Violence Against Children, conducted by the Council for the Welfare of Children and UNICEF, found that 65% of Filipino children and youth aged 13 to 24 experienced peer violence, while 64.2% experienced physical violence and 61.5% experienced psychological violence during childhood. More recently, the Department of Education reported 2,500 bullying cases in the National Capital Region during School Year 2024–2025, demonstrating that bullying and violence continue to pose significant concerns within the school environment. These circumstances show that school safety must go beyond physical security. It must also address the mental, emotional, psychosocial, and digital well-being of learners and school personnel. With the increasing use of digital technologies, schools must likewise be prepared to address cyberbullying, online abuse, cybersecurity risks, and other emerging threats. This measure seeks to institutionalize a Comprehensive School Safety Framework for public and private basic education institutions. It provides common standards for the prevention of risks, preparedness for emergencies, response to incidents, and recovery and support for affected members of the school community. Under the proposed measure, every school shall develop a School Safety Plan and maintain a School Safety Handbook containing appropriate procedures for emergency response, learner protection, reporting and referral, mental health and psychosocial support, digital safety, disaster preparedness, and off-campus activities. The bill also strengthens the roles of school personnel and promotes coordination among the Department of Education, Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare and Development, Department of the Interior and Local Government, Philippine National Police, local government units, and other concerned agencies and stakeholders. It further provides for appropriate safety infrastructure, risk assessments, emergency drills, disaster preparedness, and mechanisms for addressing bullying, abuse, violence, discrimination, and other threats. By establishing a unified and preventive approach to school safety, this measure seeks to ensure that schools are equipped not only to respond to incidents, but also to identify and prevent risks before they result in harm. Ultimately, a safe learning environment is essential to quality education. Protecting learners and school personnel from violence, hazards, and other threats will allow schools to better fulfill their fundamental role in developing healthy, capable, and resilient Filipino children and youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTOLIN “LENLEN” A. label: HB 11492
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FILIPINO FAMILY AS THE FOUNDATION OF THE NATION, INSTITUTIONALIZING FAMILY-CENTERED GOVERNANCE, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION, DEVELOPMENT, AND WELL-BEING OF FILIPINO FAMILIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation and commands the State to strengthen its solidarity and actively promote its total development. It further recognizes marriage as an inviolable social institution and the foundation of the family, protects the right of spouses to found a family according to their religious convictions and the demands of responsible parenthood, affirms the natural and primary right and duty of parents in the rearing of the youth, protects the rights of children, and equally protects the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception. These guarantees reflect a fundamental principle of a free and humane society: the dignity of the person is ordinarily first encountered, recognized, protected and developed within the family. The family is more than an aggregation of individuals receiving separate government services. It is a community of persons joined by enduring relationships of marriage, parenthood, filiation, kinship, responsibility, care and mutual support. It is where children first experience belonging and formation, where parents assume primary responsibility for their upbringing, where generations care for one another, and where citizens first learn responsibility, solidarity and participation in society. The rights of persons and the integrity of the family therefore reinforce one another. The State must protect every individual from violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect while, at the same time, respecting the legitimate autonomy of family life and supporting families in the discharge of responsibilities that properly belong to them. This balance requires the principle of subsidiarity. Public authorities should assist families when assistance is needed, coordinate with communities and civil society when these can effectively respond, and intervene directly when protection or the public welfare requires it. Government should strengthen legitimate family functions rather than unnecessarily displace them. This principle is especially important today. Filipino families face increasingly complex economic, social and cultural pressures. Household size continues to decline. Marriage is occurring later and less frequently. Fertility has fallen below replacement level. Millions of families experience prolonged separation because of overseas or internal migration. Parents confront growing demands involving work, caregiving, education, technology, mental health and child protection. Grandparents increasingly 2 perform caregiving responsibilities. Poor and vulnerable families frequently navigate several government agencies merely to address problems experienced simultaneously within one household. Government possesses numerous family-related statutes and programs, yet these interventions remain dispersed across institutions organized according to administrative mandates rather than around the family that experiences these conditions as one reality. This bill therefore establishes a permanent national system of family- centered governance. It creates the National Commission on the Filipino Family, supported by a National Advisory Council and a professional Secretariat, as the principal policy, coordinating, monitoring and standards-setting institution for family-centered governance. It establishes a National Filipino Family Development Framework, measurable family well-being indicators, proportionate Family Impact Assessments for major government measures, local family-service convergence, and mechanisms for accountability and periodic evaluation. The bill recognizes the family as a subject of legitimate interests and participation while fully respecting the constitutional and statutory rights of each family member. It preserves the Family Code and expressly avoids altering marriage, filiation, parental authority, support, succession, property relations and other matters of substantive family law by implication. The measure strengthens marriage preparation and voluntary accompaniment during the early years of married life; expands parenting and family-formation services; promotes responsible fatherhood and motherhood; strengthens family-school cooperation and parental participation in education; 3 integrates family support with maternal and child health and early childhood services; and reinforces protection of children and other vulnerable family members. It also recognizes that work and family life are inseparable dimensions of human development. Families require adequate income and conditions of employment that allow parents and carers to perform their responsibilities. The bill therefore integrates family economic security, work-family balance, caregiving, housing, nutrition and social protection into the national family- policy framework. Consistent with the Constitution, the measure affirms the inherent dignity of every human being and the equal protection of the life of the mother and the unborn from conception. It strengthens prenatal, maternal and early-childhood support, particularly during the first one thousand days of life, while preserving existing laws governing legal personality, health services and family relations. It further recognizes solidarity with the weakest as an essential responsibility of society. Poor families, children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, solo parents, families affected by migration, disaster or displacement, and persons threatened by violence, abuse or exploitation require particular attention. At the same time, solidarity must strengthen rather than create unnecessary dependence. Public assistance should, whenever reasonably possible, increase the capacity of families and communities to care for their members and participate fully in economic and civic life. label: HB 11493
title: AN ACT REGISTERING AND REGULATING SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The proliferation of social media platforms has revolutionized the way Filipinos communicate, access information, and participate in public discourse. These platforms have become essential tools for education, business, governance, and social interaction. However, the rapid expansion and influence of social media have also brought challenges, including the spread of misinformation, hate speech, cyberbullying, privacy violations, and other harmful online behaviors that threaten public order and individual rights. The Social Media Platform Regulation Act of 2026 seeks to establish a comprehensive legal framework to regulate social media platforms operating in the Philippines. This legislation aims to balance the protection of freedom of expression and innovation with the need to ensure accountability, transparency, and the safety of users in the digital space. The key provisions of the bill include: ● The establishment of clear guidelines for the operation of social media platforms to prevent the dissemination of harmful content such as fake news, hate speech, and illegal activities; ● Requirements for transparency in content moderation policies and algorithms used by social media companies; ● Safeguards to protect user privacy and data security; ● Mechanisms for prompt and effective response to complaints and grievances from users; ● Promotion of digital literacy and responsible online behavior among Filipinos; ● Strengthening the cooperation between the government, social media platforms, and civil society to foster a safer and more accountable online environment. This bill seeks to address that gap by mandating the registration and regulation of social media platforms operating in the Philippines, especially those with a significant user base or content reach in the country. It aims to ensure that these platforms observe standards of transparency, cooperate with government agencies in identifying sources of fake news, and implement robust mechanisms to detect and take down harmful content without infringing on constitutionally protected freedoms. It also seeks to promote accountability and discourage the spread of false information by imposing heavy fines and criminal prosecution, ensuring that addressing national and global issues is not hindered by disinformation. By enacting this law, the State reaffirms its commitment to uphold the constitutional rights of every Filipino while adapting to the evolving challenges posed by digital technologies. It ensures that social media platforms contribute positively to nation-building, democracy, and social cohesion. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. label: HB 11494
title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE CORPORATE LIFE OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION (PITC) FOR ANOTHER TWENTY FIVE YEARS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 2 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1071, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED CHARTER OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine International Trading Corporation (PITC) was created through Presidential Decree No. 252, and its charter was subsequently revised by Presidential Decree No. 1071, otherwise known as the “Revised Charter of the Philippine International Trading Corporation.” Under Section 2 of Presidential Decree No. 1071, the Corporation is authorized to exist for a period of fifty (50) years, with its present corporate term set to expire on 25 January 2027. For several decades, PITC has served as a government corporate vehicle in pursuing the State’s objectives in international trade. Consistent with its charter, the Corporation has undertaken trade-related activities and provided services intended to facilitate international trade, promote Philippine products and enterprises, and support the Government in its foreign procurement and marketing activities. As the expiration of PITC’s corporate term approaches, there is a need to ensure the continuity of its juridical personality, operations, and existing commitments. The expiration of its corporate term without an appropriate legislative measure may create uncertainty regarding the Corporation’s authority to continue performing its lawful functions, administering its assets and liabilities, honoring its contractual commitments, and undertaking transactions necessary for the fulfillment of its mandate. The proposed measure seeks to address this concern by providing for the continued corporate existence of PITC, while ensuring that such continued existence remains subject to appropriate government oversight and accountability. The proposed framework recognizes that the continued existence of a government- owned or -controlled corporation must be accompanied by mechanisms for periodic assessment of its relevance, efficiency, financial viability, performance, and consistency with national development policies and priorities. Accordingly, the GCG may conduct periodic performance evaluation and oversight of PITC, taking into account, among others, its financial performance, operational efficiency, governance and risk management systems, delivery of services, and contribution to the promotion and development of Philippine international trade. The measure further recognizes that perpetual corporate existence does not exempt PITC from continuing government evaluation, oversight, and accountability. The Corporation shall remain subject to the evaluation, monitoring, and other appropriate actions authorized under Republic Act No. 10149, otherwise known as the “GOCC Governance Act of 2011,” and other applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Where warranted by such evaluation and consistent with applicable law, the appropriate government authorities may undertake or recommend such lawful measures as may be necessary to ensure that the Corporation remains relevant, efficient, financially viable, and responsive to the national interest. The grant of perpetual existence is not intended to constitute a determination that the Corporation shall operate indefinitely regardless of its continued relevance, performance, or economic viability. Rather, PITC shall remain subject to the performance evaluation, monitoring, and oversight mechanisms applicable to government-owned or -controlled corporations under Republic Act No. 10149 and other applicable laws. At the same time, the proposed measure does not seek to expand the substantive powers and functions of PITC under Presidential Decree No. 1071. Rather, it seeks to ensure the continuity of the Corporation’s juridical personality and operations while strengthening accountability and providing for continuing evaluation by the appropriate government authorities. The proposed perpetual corporate term will also eliminate the need for periodic legislative action solely for the purpose of extending the Corporation’s corporate existence, while preserving the authority of Congress to amend, repeal, or otherwise modify the Corporation’s charter or corporate existence through subsequent legislation. This approach provides greater institutional stability and continuity while maintaining the necessary safeguards to ensure that PITC remains relevant, efficient, financially viable, and responsive to the national interest. Perpetual corporate existence does not preclude the State from undertaking performance evaluation, monitoring, and oversight of the Corporation's relevance, performance, efficiency, and financial viability, nor does it prevent the appropriate government authorities from recommending or undertaking such lawful measures as may be warranted by the results of such evaluation. The continued corporate existence of PITC is therefore intended to prevent disruption in its legal existence and operations and to ensure the orderly continuity of its contracts, obligations, assets, liabilities, and other lawful commitments. It will likewise enable the Corporation to continue performing its existing mandate and contributing, within the scope of its charter, to the promotion and development of Philippine international trade. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMO B. RODRIGUEZ, JR. label: HB 11495
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION AND WELFARE OF ANIMALS, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL COMMISSION ON ANIMAL WELFARE, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8485, AS AMENDED, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Animal Welfare Act of 1998 (Republic Act No. 8485), as amended in 2013, was a landmark in Philippine law — the first to impose criminal liability for acts of cruelty against animals. However, more than a decade of enforcement has proven that the law is no longer equal to the scale of the problem. Institutional authority over animal welfare remains fragmented, penalties are weak and undifferentiated, population management tools are absent, and accountability for government-run facilities is virtually nonexistent.1 Science has also advanced. International standards now recognize animals as sentient beings capable of suffering, fear, and positive emotional states. Animal welfare policy is now based on the Five Domains framework: nutrition, physical environment, health, behavioral expression, and mental state.2 Philippine law has not kept pace. The gap between law and reality is stark. According to a report issued by Mars 1 World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code, Chapters 7.1–7.8 (Animal Welfare); Universal Declaration on Animal Welfare (UDAW), adopted by the World Society for the Protection of Animals. 2 D.J. Mellor, “Updating Animal Welfare Thinking: Moving beyond the ‘Five Freedoms’ towards ‘A Life Worth Living’,” Animals, Vol. 6, No. 3 (2016), p. 21. Petcare in 2024, there are 13 million stray cats and dogs in the Philippines.3 Despite the fact that a majority of Philippine households have at least one pet in their domestic residence,4 animal welfare has received little priority in State policy and government programs. Worse, in 2020, the Care and Responsibility for Animals (CARA) Welfare Philippines, Inc. reported 3,000 cases of animal abuse, including beating, kicking, and mutilating.5 Hence, this Bill, which is an overhaul of the Animal Welfare Act of 1998. It anchors Philippine policy on the Five Domains of Animal Welfare and the Philippines’ international commitments, including the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species.6 It replaces a weak and scattered enforcement architecture with a single empowered agency, and it closes the legal loopholes that have allowed cruelty to go unpunished. Specifically, this Bill seeks to: (1) Replace the Committee on Animal Welfare with a National Commission on Animal Welfare, an independent and autonomous quasi-judicial agency with full fiscal autonomy, rule-making authority, licensing and enforcement powers, and the mandate to facilitate all efforts in prosecuting animal cruelty cases;7 (2) Mandate local government units to establish dedicated personnel with their local government veterinarians, deploy fully capacitated and trained personnel, and implement Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return programs as the primary, humane method of controlling stray animal populations;8 (3) Impose strict public accountability on pounds, including mandatory spay- neuter prior to release, publicly accessible impoundment records, and minimum operating hours open to the public; (4) Prohibit animal experimentation in elementary schools and require all secondary and tertiary institutions to adhere to global standards in the preservation and care of animals, such as the internationally recognized 3Rs Principle (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement);9 3 Zaldarriaga, Joe. “The Private Sector and Animal Welfare.” Philippine News Agency, February 17, 2025. <https://www.pna.gov.ph/opinion/pieces/1014-the-private-sector-and-animal-welfare> 4 Id. 5 Wang, Mel. “Inside The Never-Ending Fight Against Animal Abuse In The Philippines” – Rolling Stone Philippines, October 6, 2025. https://rollingstonephilippines.com/state-of-affairs/animal-rights-abuse-philippines/ 6 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), 1992; Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), 1973, to which the Philippines is a State Party. 7 RA 8485, Sec. 1, as amended by RA 10631, constitutes the Committee on Animal Welfare (CAW) under the Department of Agriculture. 8 Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNVR) is endorsed by the World Health Organization and WOAH as an evidence-based, humane method of managing free-roaming dog and cat populations. See WHO/WSPA, Guidelines for Dog Population Management (1990). 9 The 3Rs Principle was articulated by W.M.S. Russell and R.L. Burch, The Principles of Humane Experimental Technique (1959), and has since been adopted by the International Council for Laboratory (5) Overhaul the penalty structure with a graduated scale of up to three years’ imprisonment and a fine of Php 500,000.00 for causing the death of an animal, up to eighteen months and Php 80,000.00 for grave injury, and up to one year and Php 30,000.00 for lesser harm, with maximum penalties automatically applied in aggravated cases; (6) Comprehensively prohibit all forms of dog-meat trading, animal cruelty content, animal fighting, and animal poisoning as inherently cruel and exploitative practices, and provide penalties for violation thereof. (7) Provides for the integration of Animal Welfare Education in basic and higher education institutions. (8) Establish a presumption of neglect against the owner or occupant of premises where an animal is found neglected, and codify the right of good- faith rescuers to enter such premises under the doctrine of negotiorum gestio10 without criminal liability; In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11496
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ASSIGNMENT OF AN AGRICULTURAL TECHNICIAN IN EACH LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT AND ENHANCING THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES OF THE TECHNICIANS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture used to be one of the Philippines’ strongest sectors in the economy. We prided ourselves with the ability of our farmers to compete in the global market. However, present times show a completely different picture. What used to be a robust agricultural sector now has given way to other sectors such as the services and manufacturing sector. From exporters of products such as rice, we now import rice to be able to feed our growing population. But the agricultural sector should not be left to decline, in fact it may present the solution to many of our economic woes. A boosted agricultural sector would help us with food security issues. If agriculture becomes economically viable, rural economies would undergo a drastic transformation. Farmers would no longer have to venture into cities to find work, thereby reducing rural-urban migration. This in turn would lead to decongested cities and reduce the pressure to create more and more jobs in urban environments. This is why we need to inculcate advancements made in agricultural technology with our farmers. While there exist programs that already seek to impart such knowledge directly to our farmers, its effects may be attained faster and in greater magnitude if there is an assigned an expert in agricultural technology that routinely aids and assesses each farmer’s yield and capabilities. It is for these foregoing premises that approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11497
title: AN ACT PROTECTING SENIOR CITIZENS FROM VIOLENCE, DEFINING ELDER ABUSE, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State, under Article II, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution, proclaims the “value[ of] the dignity of every human person,” thereby “guarantee[ing] full respect for human rights.” In connection, under Article XIII, Section 11, the sector of the elderly is one that is entitled to prioritization when it comes to receiving government aid and protection, for their access and enjoyment of “essential goods, health and other social services.” Hence, under Article XV, Section 4, though the family, as a social unit, is entrusted with “the duty to care for its elderly members,” the State is likewise given this responsibility, to be acted upon “through just programs of social security.” As early as March 2020, it was confirmed that we have gotten “closer to having an aging population,” where “at least 7[%] are over 65 years old”:1 More than 8 million, or 8.2 percent, of the Philippines’ population of 108.9 million are aged 60 and above, per a report of the Commission on Population and Development (PopCom). Of this group, 5 million (or 4.7 percent) are aged 65 and older. With the rise in the aged population came an increase in the cases of senior citizens who have been subjected to abuse and/or been abandoned outrightly by their families:2 The Coalition of Services of the Elderly Inc., which advocates better care for senior citizens, warned recently that a crisis looms in elderly care. 1Ador Vincent Mayol, “Number of abandoned elderly rising,” Inquirer, March 9, 2020, available at https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1238586/number-of-abandoned-elderly-rising#ixzz6VxqjnkLU. 2“Crisis in elderly case,” Philippine Star, July 13, 2003, available at https://www.philstar.com/opinion/2003/07/13/213451/crisis-elderly-care. COSE said the elderly has become the fastest growing sector of the Philippine population. COSE, citing figures from the National Statistics Office, reported that the country has 155,200 people aged 65 to 80 who are listed as living alone. Some are widowed; others live alone by choice while others have been listed as abandoned. About 31,500 who are at least 80 years old have been abandoned or are living alone, COSE reported. Elderly abuse has unfortunately become a full-blown social cancer in the Philippines:3 Physical abuse are acts that are committed with intention of causing physical pain and injury. It can be in the form of being hit, sexually assaulted or burned. Any act leading to physical or bodily pain (i.e. bruises, sprains, welts, abrasions and fractures) and injury is classified under this. Psychological or emotional abuse involves verbal assaults, threats, humiliation, and ridicule. Such abuse is usually accompanied by physical abuse but may happen separately. Material or financial abuse includes misuse of property or money, theft, or forced signing of legal documents. Neglect may be referred to as passive or unintentional and active or intentional. Passive or unintentional neglect would mean isolation of the elderly or the elderly are left alone. The family, because of other duties, may not be able to meet the needs of the elderly or the caregiver is incompetent to provide care for the elderly. Active or intentional neglect involves the deliberate withholding of items needed for daily living (food, medicine, companionship and care) especially from those who are physically dependent. xxx A. Domestic Abuse There has been no major local study of this incident. DSWD admitted receiving reports of such circumstances but no record or action has been made. Unlike child abuse, to be able to protect abused elderly, the elderly themselves should report such incident before any action could be taken. Many abuses occur in different forms in their own homes but only few would admit such circumstances. The victims are often silent or in denial. They are afraid to seek help and guidance from people who can help them. Thus, elderly abuse is still unrecognized in our country. 3Clarita R. Carlos, “Concerns of the Elderly in the Philippines,” Philippine Social Sciences Review 56(1-4): 18-22, available at https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/8a6b/2d097fc02065e561553ba2231b04f3a9450d.pdf. Being physically vulnerable, the elderly is one of the most usual preys and victims of abuse. Because of the frailty, such condition is taken advantage of. Moreover being single and widowed is another factor adding to their susceptible condition. Being dependent on the family, unfortunately, in a way has become a disadvantage as well. For some families, they see the state of the elderly as an opportunity to take over whatever wealth the elderly has and deliberately neglecting or ignoring the elderly. A radio program called the Senior Citizen hour receives several calls and letters asking for advice regarding elderly abuse. Most of the abusers are the children themselves. Financial abuse is one of the frequent complaints accompanied by physical abuse. The children who still live with their parents, either employed or unemployed are oftentimes the perpetrators or abusers. The abusers extort money from them to support their needs or expenses, failure of the elderly to give money usually leads to physical abuse. There are also cases wherein the working parents would force their elderly parents to take care of their grandchildren even though the elderly have expressed their refusal. There are several cases being reported but do not really fall into any category of elderly abuse but still can be considered to be abusive. For instance, an elderly couple live together with their four children. label: HB 11498
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY SALARY AND OTHER BENEFITS OF HEALTH WORKERS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The experiences of the COVID-19 Pandemic in the Philippines left a lasting mark and a vital lesson. The country, as well as the globe entire, were caught lacking and unready to deal with a health emergency of such size. Although not unprecedented in recent human history, the pandemic was unique in its scale and disruption in living memory. It is a grim reality, warned by medical experts, scientists, and historians alike, that such a global pandemic will not be the last. It most assuredly will happen again. As such, the COVID-19 pandemic serves as a wake-up call. For our government, its instruments, and our precarious health care system, capacities must be expanded, processes must be streamlined, and bureaucracy must be made more efficient. A strong healthcare system likewise relies on its greatest resource: human resources, or the health workers that are on the frontline of such health emergencies. Without competent members of the healthcare profession comprising our public health system, we cannot expect that our public healthcare will be able to sustain and provide quality healthcare for all Filipinos. As such, it is of utmost importance that they be given the appreciation and benefits they deserve, in light of their significance in Philippine society. It is then incumbent for us to increase their salary and benefits considering the risks that their employment poses. It is for these reasons that the passage of this bill is earnestly sought In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is urgently sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11499
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF CEBU AND THE PROVINCE OF NEGROS ORIENTAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Cebu and Negros Island are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve connectivity within Central Visayas, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, investment, and regional development. It would also provide an additional transport option when sea crossings are unavailable or disrupted. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel connecting the Municipality of Santander, Cebu, and the Municipality of Sibulan, Negros Oriental. The proposed project would establish a direct and continuous land transport connection between Cebu Island and Negros Island, subject to the results of comprehensive feasibility, engineering, environmental, and other necessary technical studies. The project must consider not only the bridge or tunnel crossing itself, but also the necessary approach roads, interchanges, and connections to the existing road networks of Cebu and Negros Oriental. These components must be planned and developed as an integrated transport corridor to ensure that the completed link provides safe, efficient, and convenient movement between the two islands. The proposed link would make travel between Cebu and Negros Oriental easier and more efficient, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services, employment centers, and economic opportunities. It could also strengthen disaster response and emergency mobility by providing another route for personnel, equipment, relief supplies, and other essential resources between the two islands. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARCELINO C. label: HB 11501
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE AND THE PROVINCE OF BOHOL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Southern Leyte and Bohol are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve access between Eastern and Central Visayas and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, and investment. It would also provide another transport option when sea crossings are unavailable. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel following a proposed alignment from Maasin City, Southern Leyte, through Lapinig Island, Bohol to Ubay, Bohol. It would establish a continuous land route across the two water crossings, subject to the results of feasibility and engineering studies. Lapinig Island serves as an intermediate point in the proposed route. Accordingly, the project must consider the connections between Maasin City and Lapinig Island, between Lapinig Island and Ubay, and across the island itself. Examining these sections together is necessary to ensure that the completed link functions as one practical transport corridor. The proposed link would make travel between Southern Leyte and Bohol easier, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services. It could also strengthen disaster response by giving emergency personnel, equipment, and relief supplies another route between the two provinces when conditions permit. label: HB 11505
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (DOH) TO ENSURE THE AVAILABILITY OF MEDICINES AND PROCUREMENT OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT IN ALL PUBLIC HOSPITALS THROUGH THE UTILIZATION OF THE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO INDIGENT AND FINANCIALLY INCAPACITATED PATIENTS (MAIFIP) FUND.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to protect aud promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. Despite this constitutional guarantee, many public hospitals across the country continue to grapple with chronic shortages of essential medicines and a lack of basic diagnostic equipment. This reality places a heavy burden on indigent and financially incapacitated Filipinos who rely entirely on government healthcare facilities for their survival and well-being. This proposed measure seeks to address this critical gap by institutionalizing a proactive and sustainable procurement mechanism. It mandates the Department of Health (DOH) to ensure a continuous, adequate supply of essential medicines and guarantees that all public hospitals are equipped with baseline diagnostic tools like functional X-ray, ultrasound, and ECG machines. To ensure the viability of this mandate, the bill introduces a strategic funding approach. It maximizes the existing Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) Fund by explicitly earmarking at least twenty-five percent (25%) of its annual allocation exclusively for the procurement of essential medicines and medical equipment. By converting a portion of direct financial assistance into tangible, readily available healthcare resources at the point of care, the government can prevent stockouts, lower overall healthcare costs through bulk procurement, and provide immediate diagnostic and medical relief to marginalized patients. Furthermore, the bill institutes safeguards for transparency, efficient inventory management, and regular congressional reporting to ensure that the funds are utilized effectively and reach the Filipinos who need them most. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHILIY CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11506
title: AN ACT MANDATING TO PROFESSIONALIZE AND ELEVATE STERILE PROCESSING AS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND PATIENT SAFETY, AND DEVELOP THE INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS, RESOURCES AND BEST PRACTICES IN STERILIZATION SCIENCES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution declares that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” Central to this mandate is the guarantee of patient safety and the delivery of high-quality healthcare services in all medical facilities across the country. Despite advancements in medical technology, Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) remain a persistent and life-threatening risk to patients. A critical vulnerability in infection control is the improper cleaning, decontamination, and sterilization of reusable medical devices and hospital workspaces. The emergence of highly resilient pathogens, such as prions, and the increasing complexity of surgical instruments necessitate a rigorous, scientifically backed approach to infection control that leaves no room for error. Currently, there is a need to professionalize and standardize stcrile processing as a distinct, highly regulated discipline within the Philippine healthcare system. The Central Sterile Services Department (CSSD) is the beating heart of hospital infection control, yet standardizing its operations to meet rigorous international benchmarks requires dedicated legislative backing. This bill seeks to elevate sterilization sciences by requiring all health care facilities, whether government or private, hospital or office-based clinic, to secure a specialized “Sterile Permit” prior to operation. To achieve this, the proposed measure: 1. Establishes Strict Regulatory Standards: Mandates health care facilities to submit detailed operational plans for decontamination, disinfection, and sterilization based on international best practices, including the Spaulding Classification System. 2. Empowers the Department of Health: Designates the Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau (HFSRB) as the licensing agency tasked with inspecting facilities, issuing permits, monitoring HAI rates, and enforcing compliance. 3. Professionalizes the Workspace and Workforce: Requires dedicated architectural spaces for decontamination and _ sterile storage, specialized equipment like medical washers, strict use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and concrete protocols for process failures and occupational exposure. 4. Protects Healthcare Workers: Integrates occupational satety measures and transmission-based precautions to shield the personnel handling bioburden and hazardous materials daily. By treating sterile processing not merely as a hospital support service, but as a critical, highly specialized component of patient survival, we can drastically reduce preventable infections, protect our frontline healthcare workers, and align Philippine medical facilities with global health standards. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11507
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AND RELIABILITY SYSTEM, THEREBY CREATING THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AUTHORITY (NHSA), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” While significant strides have been made to expand healthcare access across the country, access alone is insufficient if the care provided is unsafe. Preventable medical harm, adverse events, and systemic errors remain a significant but often underreported threat to public health and national development. Currently, the approach to medical errors in the healthcare sector is heavily punitive. This environment discourages healthcare workers from reporting near-misses and adverse events out of fear of administrative, civil, or criminal retaliation. Without transparent reporting, the healthcare system loses critical opportunities to analyze root causes, correct systemic flaws, and prevent future harm. The proposed bill mandates the creation of the National Healthcare Safety Authority (NHSA), an independent body attached to the Department of Health (DOH). The NHSA will be tasked with developing mandatory national patient safety standards, conducting safety audits, and establishing a confidential, non-punitive national incident reporting system. By legally protecting good-faith reporters, the State empowers healthcare professionals to become active partners in identifying systemic risks without the fear of unjust reprisal. Furthermore, this bill introduces a public Healthcare Safety Rating System to empower patients with transparent data regarding facility compliance and safety outcomes. It also mandates the integration of these safety metrics into PhilHealth’s accreditation and reimbursement systems, ensuring that public funds are directed toward institutions that prioritize high-quality, reliable care. Healthcare must be designed to heal, not harm. By establishing a dedicated authority and a proactive, evidence-based framework for patient safety, this legislation will strengthen public trust in our medical institutions and ensure that every Filipino receives the safe, high-quality healthcare they deserve. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11508
title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF BASIC ROAD SAFETY AND COMPREHENSIVE DRIVERS' EDUCATION AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF THE K-12 PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Road safety is a pressing public health and education concern. The World Health Organization’s Global Status Report on Road Safety (2023) highlights that road traffic injuries remain the leading cause of death among people aged 5 to 29 worldwide. In the Philippines, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported over 11,000 road crash fatalities in 2022, while Metro Manila alone recorded more than 65,000 road accidents in the same year. These alarming figures underscore the need for a preventive approach through early education. By integrating Basic Road Safety and Comprehensive Drivers’ Education into the K-12 curriculum, students will gain practical knowledge on traffic rules, pedestrian rights, commuter etiquette, and defensive driving principles. The inclusion of a Monitoring and Evaluation mechanism ensures accountability and continuous improvement, allowing policymakers to track outcomes such as reduced youth-related road incidents and improved safety awareness. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11509
title: AN ACT INCREASING CAMPUS SECURITY AND CRIME AWARENESS BY INSTALLING CLOSED-CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) CAMERAS AND WALK- THROUGH METAL DETECTORS IN ALL SCHOOLS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Schools are meant to be sanctuaries of learning where students, teachers, and school personnel can thrive without fear of violence or disruption. However, educational institutions remain vulnerable to various threats that may compromise safety, disrupt learning, and undermine the right of every learner to a secure educational environment. This bill seeks to strengthen and institutionalize school security nationwide by mandating the installation of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras and walk-through metal detectors in all schools. CCTV cameras will enhance monitoring, incident documentation, and crime prevention, while metal detectors will serve as a preventive measure against the entry of firearms, bladed weapons, and other dangerous objects into school premises. The measure also requires coordination among the Department of Education (DepEd), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), Philippine National Police (PNP), and Local Government Units (LGUs) to ensure the proper deployment, maintenance, and operation of these security measures. Schools may likewise be prioritized based on risk assessment and other relevant security considerations. By institutionalizing these measures, the State affirms its responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of students, teachers, and school personnel. Ensuring a safe and secure school environment is essential to sustaining quality education and allowing learners to study, grow, and develop without fear. This legislation is a proactive and long-term measure to strengthen school safety and prevent violence and other security threats within educational institutions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11510
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SAFETY INTERNET EDUCATION PROGRAM IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In today’s hyperconnected world, the internet has become both a gateway to opportunity and a source of risk. The Philippines, with 90.8 million social media users as of January 2025—representing 78% of the population and averaging 3 hours and 32 minutes daily online use (DataReportal, We Are Social, Meltwater – Digital 2025 Report), ranks among the most active nations globally. This level of engagement underscores the urgent need for structured education on internet safety and media literacy. While young Filipinos are often described as “digital natives,” technical proficiency alone does not equate to digital literacy. Exposure to cyberbullying, misinformation, predatory grooming, and privacy breaches continues to rise, threatening both individual well-being and national resilience. This measure seeks to institutionalize an Internet Safety Education Program (ISEP) in all elementary and secondary schools. The program will equip teachers with professional training, empower students through peer-driven initiatives, and engage parents and communities in building a “360-degree” safety net. By embedding internet safety and media literacy into the curriculum, the bill ensures that the next generation is not only connected, but protected, informed, and responsible. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11511
title: AN ACT PROTECTING SENIOR CITIZENS FROM VARIOUS FORMS OF FRAUD THROUGH INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND PROVIDING MECHANISMS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Senior citizens are increasingly vulnerable to fraud schemes that exploit mail, telecommunication, and online platforms. Common tactics such as phishing, text scams, and investment fraud not only cause financial losses but also bring emotional distress to the elderly. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (2021 Financial Inclusion Survey), only 2% of respondents correctly answered all six basic financial literacy questions, showing limited awareness that makes seniors more prone to scams. The Anti-Money Laundering Council (2015 Strategic Analysis Report) further reported that cross-border investment fraud involving the Philippines amounted to ₱4.66 billion over five years, underscoring the scale of financial crimes that can affect vulnerable populations. This measure mandates the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), through local government units, to regularly disseminate information on mail, telemarketing, and internet fraud targeting senior citizens. It also requires coordination with agencies such as the BSP, SEC, NTC, DICT, and NBI to provide updated fraud prevention materials and reporting mechanisms. By institutionalizing education, awareness, and reporting systems, this bill ensures that senior citizens, their families, and caregivers are better equipped to recognize and avoid fraudulent schemes. It strengthens government accountability and affirms Congress’ commitment to safeguarding the welfare of the elderly in the digital age. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR CHILD DEVELOPMENT WORKERS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The early years of a child's life are critical to their physical, emotional, social, and cognitive development. During this period, Child Development Workers (CDWs) play a vital role in providing care, early education, protection, and developmental support to young children, particularly those in vulnerable and underserved communities. Despite the importance of their work, many CDWs continue to face challenges related to employment security, compensation, benefits, professional development, and access to adequate support and resources. These conditions may affect not only their welfare but also the quality and continuity of early childhood development services provided to children. CDWs perform responsibilities that require patience, dedication, specialized knowledge, and a deep commitment to the welfare of children. It is therefore necessary for the State to recognize their indispensable contribution to nation-building and ensure that they are provided with appropriate employment protection, fair compensation, benefits, training opportunities, and other forms of support. This measure seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for the protection and promotion of the rights and welfare of CDWs. It aims to strengthen their employment security, provide appropriate plantilla positions and compensation, promote continuing education and skills development, and ensure access to benefits and other privileges commensurate with the importance of their duties. By investing in the welfare and professional development of CDWs, the State likewise invests in the future of Filipino children. A well-supported and adequately protected workforce is essential to ensuring that every child receives quality care, early learning, and developmental support during the most formative years of life. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11513
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF MOBILE DEVICES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC GADGETS DURING CLASS HOURS FROM KINDERGARTEN TO SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The widespread use of mobile devices and electronic gadgets among students has created both opportunities and challenges in the classroom. While these tools can support learning, their unregulated use during class hours has led to distractions, reduced academic performance, and even health concerns such as poor posture, sleep disorders, and vision problems. According to the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), 41% of Filipino students are distracted by their own device use and 37% by other students using devices during math classes. Globally, countries such as France, Spain, China, and Australia have already adopted restrictions on smartphone use in schools, balancing technology with structured learning environments. Locally, the Department of Education (DepEd) has issued guidelines discouraging cellphone use in classrooms, but enforcement has been inconsistent. This bill institutionalizes a clear and enforceable policy across all public and private schools from Kindergarten to Senior High School, ensuring that classrooms remain focused and conducive to holistic development. The measure also provides for monitoring and compliance to ensure that schools adhere to the prohibition and that enforcement is consistent nationwide. By passing this Act, Congress affirms its duty to protect the physical, intellectual, and social well-being of Filipino learners. Limiting gadget use during class hours will foster discipline, improve focus, and promote healthier learning environments for the youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The quality of education largely depends on the dedication and competence of our public school teachers. As the primary movers of learning and nation-building, they deserve fair compensation and adequate support that recognize the value of their profession and enable them to perform their duties effectively. Despite their indispensable role, many public school teachers continue to face financial and professional challenges brought about by increasing responsibilities and the rising cost of living. These realities underscore the need to strengthen the government's commitment to improving their welfare and ensuring that the teaching profession remains attractive to qualified and dedicated educators. This measure seeks to enhance the compensation and benefits of public school teachers as an investment in the country's education system and the future of every Filipino learner. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” FORTES, JR. label: HB 11515
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING SPECIAL EDUCATION (SPED) CENTERS IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR SPED TEACHER TRAINING, SPECIALIZATION, AND SUPPORT, AND EXPANDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11223 (UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE ACT) AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11959 (REGIONAL SPECIALTY CENTERS ACT) TO INCLUDE COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENTAL AND SPECIALIZED EDUCATIONAL SERVICES FOR CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11223, or the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, and Republic Act No. 11959, or the Regional Specialty Centers Act, laid the foundation for an integrated and people-centered health system. However, gaps remain in addressing the developmental and educational needs of children with disabilities, particularly during early childhood and school age when timely intervention is most critical. Public schools are the most accessible institutions for Filipino families, yet the establishment of Special Education (SPED) Centers remains uneven and discretionary. The absence of a nationwide mandate and sustainable funding mechanism continues to limit access to properly resourced SPED services. Challenges such as the shortage of trained SPED teachers, limited specialization programs, inadequate compensation, and weak coordination between health and education systems persist. This measure seeks to institutionalize the establishment of SPED Centers in public elementary and secondary schools nationwide, prioritizing underserved and marginalized areas. It provides sustained funding for SPED teacher training, specialization, scholarships, and professional development, alongside additional compensation and incentives for SPED personnel and allied professionals. Further, the bill strengthens collaboration among the Department of Education, Department of Health, local government units, and barangays to integrate developmental and therapeutic services into the mandates of the UHC Act and the Regional Specialty Centers Act. Importantly, it also emphasizes parental involvement through consultations and school-based activities, ensuring that families are active partners in the education and holistic development of children with disabilities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11516
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING GOVERNMENT SUPPORT FOR GIFTED AND TALENTED STUDENTS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every Filipino learner possesses unique talents and abilities that, when properly nurtured, can contribute to the country's progress and development. Gifted and talented students require learning opportunities that go beyond the regular curriculum to fully develop their potential and prepare them to become future leaders, innovators, researchers, artists, and professionals. While existing programs provide support to some gifted learners, access to specialized education and development opportunities remains limited. There is a need to institutionalize a comprehensive support system that promotes academic excellence, creativity, innovation, and talent development while ensuring that deserving learners receive the guidance and opportunities they need to succeed. This measure seeks to establish a sustainable framework for identifying, developing, and supporting gifted and talented Filipino students through specialized educational programs, scholarships, mentorship, and research and innovation opportunities. By investing in their potential, the State strengthens the country's human capital and promotes long-term national development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11517
title: AN ACT DECLARING JANUARY 9 OF EVERY YEAR A SPECIAL NONWORKING HOLIDAY IN THE ENTIRE COUNTRY TO COMMEMORATE THE FEAST OF THE BLACK NAZARENE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is the third-largest Catholic country in the world, with about 90 million Catholics, or more than 86 percent of the whole population1. Thus, the prominence of Catholic traditions and occasions in our nation. For more than 400 years, the historical statue of a dark-skinned Jesus Christ kneeling and carrying his cross has been a symbol of devotion, struggle, faith, and resilience for Filipino Catholics. The iconic statue, which is currently enshrined in the Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene, more famously known as the Quiapo Church, has survived raging fires, earthquakes, floods due to numerous typhoons, and even bombings during the Second World War. On January 9 of every year, an estimated 18 million Filipinos from all around the country take part in the celebration of the Feast of the Black Nazarene. Devotees take part in an extraordinary procession popularly known as Traslación where they carry a replica of the iconic statue in a display of extreme religious devotion. This iconic religious procession does not happen in Manila alone but is also conducted in different locations nationwide, such as in Cagayan de Oro, Samar, and other provinces which feature their own version of the kneeling mulatto Nazarene. 1 Asia Society. “Religion in the Philippines.” https://asiasociety.org/education/religion-philippines (Accessed Online 9 September 2022) As a widely practiced religious event by many of our countrymen, it is imperative that January 9 of every year be declared as a special nonworking holiday to commemorate the Feast of the Black Nazarene. Furthermore, given the immense number of people involved in the celebration of this feast, and in order to ensure peace and order and the security and safety of participants and the general public, it is necessary to institutionalize the coordination of different government agencies and instrumentalities for smooth coordination between the public and private sectors, and the extension of necessary assistance in connection with the celebration of the Feast of the Black Nazarene. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D.
