label: HB 11585
title: AN ACT GRANTING CHILD CARE LEAVE TO PARENTS, LEGAL GUARDIANS, AND PERSONS LAWFULLY ENTRUSTED WITH THE CARE OF A CHILD, PROVIDING FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution recognizes the family's role in nation-building. Article XV, Section 1 expressly provides that “The State recognizes the family as the foundation of the nation.” It further declares that the State shall strengthen the family as a basic autonomous social institution and shall equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception. The Constitution likewise recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and guarantees their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being. Article II, Section 12 further mandates the State to protect the sanctity of family life and to protect and strengthen the family as a basic autonomous social institution. Article XV, Sections 2 and 3 likewise recognize parents' rights and responsibilities in rearing children and direct the State to defend children's right to assistance, including proper care and protection from neglect. abuse, cruelty, exploitation, and other conditions prejudicial to their development. The Constitution also recognizes, under Article XIII, Section 3, the right of workers to humane working conditions and directs the State to afford full protection to labor. These constitutional guarantees reveal that safeguarding the family, nurturing children, and upholding the dignity of workers are not isolated duties. They are crafted together as shared responsibilities of the State. The latest available Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Labor Force Survey as of September 2026 is for June 2026. It reports 53.25 million Filipinos aged 15 and over in the labor force, of whom 50.66 million were employed. The labor force participation rate was 65.1%, while unemployment stood at 4.9%. Current laws offer vital protections and leave benefits for workers and families, such as maternity, paternity, solo-parent, and service incentive leaves. This measure does not seek to replace or lessen these safeguards. Instead, it aims to complement them by addressing sitations that existing leave options may not fully cover. For many first-time parents, caring for a child can feel daunting, especially without experience, guidance, or enough external support. Parents, guardians, and caregivers may algo face tough situations but cannot easily seek help due to work demands. In these moments, even a short period of protected leave can open the door to meeting a child's essential needs, reaching out for help, talking with teachers or professionals, or simply being there when a child needs utmost care, comfort, and guidance. Even more urgently, some children suffer quietly, facing fear, neglect, confusion, or distress without understanding what is happening or how to seek help. Their struggles often go unnoticed when the adults meant to care for them cannot be present due to work commitments. The State must therefore recognize that child care is more than attending to illness or emergencies. It includes listening, guiding, observing, teaching, accompanying, protecting, and understanding a child's behavioral, emotional, developmental, educational, and psychesocial needs. This measure is likewise consistent with the broader principle of responsible parenthood recognized in existing Philippine legislation. Republic Act No. 10354, or the Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act of 2012, recognizes responsible parenthood and provides for access to information and services concerning responsible parenthood and reproductive health. This proposed measure complements that framework by addressing the continuing responsibility of parents and caregivers to provide care, guidance, protection, and support after a child is born. The State must nurture the family from the home up. If the family forms the bedrock of society, then safeguarding its protection and strength is ensuring the nation's very foundation. We must guard that the basic unit of our society receives the care, dignity, protection, and support it deserves. This measure therefore seeks not merely to provide another workplace benefit, but to bring the Constitution's recognition of the family and its promise to children and workers to life. It acknowledges that presence is a powerful form of care, and that timely support from a pagent or caregiver can keep a child's struggles from growing into greater challenges. Statutory and contractual leave benefits. It therefore strengthens, rather than displaces, the protections already established by law. With this measure, the State affirms that whenever a child needs care, guidance, protection, or simply a listening ear, the person responsible for that child's well-being should have a real chance to be present. Passing this measure will help fortify families, support first-time parents and caregivers, aid those facing hardships, shield children who might otherwise suffer quietly, and fulfill the Constitution's call to protect families, champion children's welfare, and promote humane working conditions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11586
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PRE-MARRIAGE RESPONSIBLE PARENTHOOD PROGRAM, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 15 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10354, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “RESPONSIBLE PARENTHOOD AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH ACT OF 2012,” AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the family as the foundation of the nation and directs the State to protect and strengthen it. Consistent with this policy, Republic Act No. 10354, otherwise known as the “Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act of 2012,” already requires applicants for a marriage license to receive instruction on responsible parenthood, family planning, breastfeeding, and infant nutrition as a condition for the issuance of a Certificate of Compliance. However, while Section 15 of Republic Act No. 10354 provides an important foundation for pre-marriage education, it does not prescribe a comprehensive and standardized curriculum on child development, child behavior, positive parenting, positive discipline, responsive caregiving, and child protection. Since the enactment of Republic Act No. 10354, Republic Act No. 11148, or the “Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act,” has further recognized the importance of positive parenting, responsive caregiving, parent- or caregiver-child interaction, and early childhood development. Philippine policy has therefore evolved, but the pre-marriage education requirements under Section 15 have not been correspondingly expanded. This measure aims to enrich, not replace, Section 15 of Republic Aet No. 10354 by weaving these vital competencies into the current pre-marriage orientation and counseling program. It introduces a unified, evidence-based Pre-Marriage Responsible Parenthood and Family Preparation Course that explores child development, behavior, emotional regulation, positive discipline, parent-child communication, child protection, and responsible parenthood. The measure is educational and preventive. It does not create a parental-fitness test or authorize the government to determine an individual's moral, psychological, religious, economic, or parental suitability for marriage. Completion of the Course, rather than a determination of fitness, shall constitute compliance. By reinforcing an established legal framework and harmonizing it with evolving Philippine policies on positive parenting and child development, this measure aspires to equip future spouses for the challenges of family life and champion the protection, well-being, and flourishing of Filipino children. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT CREATING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY INNOVATION HUB, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Innovation fuels economic growth, sparks technological breakthroughs, creates jobs, and paves the way for sustainable progress. When ideas, research, technology, and entrepreneurship come together, innovation empowers communities and industries to tackle new challenges, boost productivity, and unlock fresh opportunities for prosperity. The Zamboanga Peninsula boasts a vibrant and expanding economy, a wealth of talented people, and immense promise for research, entrepreneurship, and technological progress. Blessed with abundant raw materials, rich agricultural and marine resources, and unique local products, the region stands poised to add value, drive innovation, and compete on both national and global stages. By harnessing these assets through innovation, local ideas and products can become high- value goods, cutting-edge technologies, and thriving enterprises. Zamboanga City, especially its First Legislative District, stands ready to become the home of a vibrant innovation hub—a dynamic meeting ground for innovators, researchers, entrepreneurs, industries, government agencies, academic institutions, and all who share a vision for progress. Consistent with and in furtherance of Republic Act No. 11293, otherwise known as the “Philippine Innovation Act,” this measure seeks to establish the Zamboanga City Innovation Hub (ZCIH) as the main innovation hub serving Zamboanga City and the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. The Hub shall serve as a center for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technology development, incubation, prototyping, and commercialization, while providing technical, institutional, and business support to innovators, startups, researchers, students, and micro, small, and medium enterprises. Creating the ZCIH will help bring the national innovation agenda to life by energizing the region’s innovation ecosystem, championing research and technology, elevating the value and competitiveness of local resources, nurturing technology-driven enterprises, and opening doors to inclusive and sustainable growth across the Zamboanga Peninsula. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly soughit. label: HB 11588
title: AN ACT CREATING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY HIGH SCHOOL FOR THE ARTS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipinos shine for their creativity, ingenuity, and resourcefulness, qualities that pulse through our music, dance, literature, theater, visual arts, crafts, and architecture. Art is the heartbeat of our history and cultural identity. Through art, generations have kept traditions alive, shared stories, voiced dreams, and handed down our vibrant heritage to those who come after. The 1987 Constitution recognizes the importance of both education and the arts. Article II, Section 17 provides that the State shall give priority to education, science and technology, arts, culture, and sports. Article XIV, Section 1 further mandates the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education and to make such education accessible to all. The Constitution likewise calls for the preservation and enrichment of Filipino culture and equal access to cultural opportunities through the educational system. Yet, despite these mandates, countless young Filipinos with remarkable artistic gifts remain without access to the specialized instruction, facilities, and opportunities they need to flourish. Just as scholars and athletes thrive with guidance and training, artists deserve a nurturing environment where their talents can vibrantly blossom. This proposal seeks to establish the Zamboanga City School for the Arts, a specialized public secondary school for students with exceptional aptitude and potential in Arts and Design. The School shall provide quality general education alongside specialized training in various artistic disciplines, in accordance with the standards and programs of the Department of Education. Zamboanga City stands ready and eager to become the first in Region IX to host a high school devoted to the arts. With its vibrant tapestry of traditions, languages, music, dance, literature, crafts, and countless cultural expressions, the City is poised to become a beacon for arts education in the Zamboanga Peninsula. The School will not only safeguard Mindanao’s multitude of traditions but also empower young artists to explore, adopt. and invent new forms of cfeative expression. The School aims to welcome not only the youth of Zamboanga City but also gifted students from every corner of the Zamboanga Peninsula. With fair and inclusive admission standards, those with artistic promise can pursue specialized arts education, no matter their background or means. The School will offer inspiring studios, rehearsal and performance spaces, state-of-the-art facilities, technology, and resources essential for vibrant arts education. It may also forge partnerships with government agencies, local communities, cultural institutions, artists, universities, and other organizations to enrich its programs. This institution is a bold investment in the Region [X's cultural future. [ts graduates will emerge as artists, educators, cultural advocates, designers, and creative professionals who will safeguard and enrich their communities’ heritage while shaping the evolving tapestry of Philippine culture. The young artists who will walk the halls of the Zamboanga City School for the Arts are destined to become guardians of our cultural legacy. By providing them with education, resources, and opportunities, the State can help Filipino creativity, talent, and traditions thrive for generations yet to come. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11589
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING SUPPORT FOR SEAWEED AND CARRAGEENAN SCIENCE AND INNOVATION, PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND COMPETITIVENESS, PROVIDING FOR CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE, CREATING THE SEAWEED AND CARRAGEENAN FUNDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines ranks among the world's major seaweed producers, and the industry provides livelihoods and incomes for thousands of coastal families, farmers, fisherfolk, processors, traders, and other stakeholders. Beyond its economic significance, seaweed is a primafy raw material for carrageenan and is used in diverse food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, agricultural, cosmetic, and industrial applications. Despite considerable potential, the Philippine seaweed and carrageenan sectors continue to encounter challenges related to productivity, climate change, disease management, post-harvest losses, technology adoption, product quality, value addition, research and development, and access to both domestic and international markets. A coordinated, science-based approach is required to strengthen the seaweed and carrageenan value chain in the Philippines. The proposed measure aims to establish a National Seaweed and Carrageenan Scienee and Innovation Program under the leadership of the Department of Science and Technology. This Program will provide a comprehensive framework for research, technology development, innovation, technology transfer, extension services, commercialization, and market development. A key provision of the bill is the establishment or designation of Centers of Excellence, which will serve as regional hubs for research and development, technology demonsffation, product development, training, testing, technology transfer, and collaboration among government, academia, industry, farmers, fisherfolk, and communities. The bill also establishes Seaweed and Carrageenan Funds to provide sustained fimancial support for research and innovation, technology development, training, technology transfer, commercialization, product development, and market promotion. Recognizing that scientific discoveries and technologies have limited impact unless effectively disseminated, the measure provides for strengthened technology transfer and extension services. These services will enable farmers, fisherfolk, processors, cooperatives, and enterprises to access and adopt appropriate technologies that can increase productivity, improve quality, reduce losses, enhance sustainability, and increase income. The bill further advances market development initiatives to strengthen the position of Philippine seaweed and carrageenan products in both domestic and international markets. Support in product development, certification, branding, standards compliance, trade promotion, and export development will enable Philippine producers and enterprises to compete more effeetively in the global marketplace. An Inter-Agency Committee on Seaweed and Carrageenan Science and Innovation will be established to ensure coordination among government agencies and stakeholders, and to prevent duplication of programs and resources. This measure will strengthen the scientific and technological foundations of the seaweed and carrageenan industries, while promoting environmental sustainability, inclusive development, innovation, and global competitiveness. The passage of this measure is expected to result in higher productivity and inéomes, stronger rural and coastal economies, increased value addition, expanded markets, amd the development of a more sustainable and globally competitive Philippine seaweed and carrageenan industry. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The mango is one of the Philippines' most important fruit crops and is recognized by law as a high-value crop under Republic Act No. 7900, otherwise known as the "High-Value Crops Development Act of 1995." The law recognizes mango as one of the country's high-value fruit crops and provides a framework to strengthen production, processing, marketing, distribution, research, training, and financing for high-value crops. Despite the mango industry’s vital role, a wealth of untapped potential remains to boost productivity, strengthen climate resilience, improve postharvest practices, innovate processifg and product development, and expand market reach and global competitiveness. The Department of Science and Technology’s latest profile highlights mango as the national fruit and underscofes the urgent need for strategic research, technology advancement, knowledge sharing, capacity building, and robust policy support to propel the industry forward. Zamboanga City stands out among the country’s mango-producing regions for its rich yet often overlooked mango resources and remarkable genetic diversity. The city’s mangoes, among the most underrated in the Philippines, offer a delightful local variety with a unique blend of sweetness and tang, a small seed, delicate skin, and an irresistible aroma. Grown across several barangays, this mango is a hidden agricultural gem, brimming with promise for scientific exploration, varietal discovery, propagation, innovative product development, branding, and commercial success. Beyond its prized mango varieties, Zamboanga City and the greater Zamboanga Pemiinsula are also home to the indigenous baluno (Mangifera caesia Jack), a unique mango-family fruit native to Mindanao and its neighboring regions. Recognized in scientific and forestry literature, the baluno tree thrives in these areas, bearing edible fruit that ripens into a sweet and delightful treat. The true value of these local and indigenous mango treasures goes far beyond their eurrent commercial output. Their rich genetics, distinctive flavors and aromas, adaptability to local environments, deep cultural roots, and exciting possibilities for food innovation and value-added products make them deserving of dedicated research, conservation, propagation, and thoughtful commercialization. The Philippine mango industry boasts a robust production base. According to the Philippine Mango Industry Roadmap, the Zamboanga Peninsula ranks among the nation’s key mango-producing regions, and local agricultural data show that Zamboanga City dedicates considerable land and resources to thriving mango cultivation. This proposed measure aims to launch the Philippine Mango Science, Innovation, and Sustainable Development Program, creating a unified platform for research, innoyation, conservation, production, processing, value enhancement, technology transfer, capacity building, market expansion, and export promotion. The proposed Act shall complement and strengthen existing national policies and programs, particularly: 1. Republic Act No. 7900, or the "High-Value Crops Development Act of 1995," which recognizes mango as a high-value crop and provides for financing, prodiiction, processing, marketing, research, experimental stations, seed farms, and farmer training. 2. Republic Act No. 7844, or the "Export Development Act of 1994," declares export development a national strategy and establishes mechanisms for export promotion, research and development, technical assistance, quality standards, market development, and strengthening the Export Development Council. 3. Republic Act No. 10848, which further provided for the implementation of the Agricultural Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (ACEF) and authorized support for agricultural productivity, production and postharvest machinery and equipment, processing facilities, agricultural research and development, and programs a to enhance the competitiveness of farmers and agricultural sectors in domestic and international markets. This measure complements, not replicates, existing laws. It will establish a targeted policy framework that unites government agencies, research and academic institutions, farmers’ groups, cooperatives, local governments, and private-sector partners in building a science-driven, globally competitive Philippine mango industry. Specifically, the bill champions research into mango genetics, varietal discovery and profiling, propagation, climate resilience, integrated pest and disease control, sustainable cultivation, advanced postharvest technologies, food safety, innovative processing and packaging, product development, and market intelligence, and responsible development of locally important mango varieties and indigenous mango-family resources, including the Zamboanga City local mango varieties and baluno, while ensuring that commercialization does not compromise biodiversity, ecological sustainability, or the rights and interests of local farming and indigenous communities. The measure likewise recognizes that true competitiveness goes beyond production. Philippine mangoes need state-of-the-art postharvest facilities, efficient cold-chain systems, cutting-edge processing technologies, rigorous quality standards, strong branding, traceability, dynamic market development, and export-ready infrastructure. national program, the Philippines can transform its mango resources from primarily raw agricultural commodities into high»value, science-driven products capable of competing in domestic and international markets. Passing this measure will empower farmers, spark agricultural innovation, boost rural enterprises, safeguard precious plant genetics, create jobs, open new doors for food processing and agribusiness, and drive the nation’s sustainable agricultural and export growth. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SUPPORT FOR SARDINE SCIENCE AND INNOVATION PROGRAM, PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, HIGHER VALUE- ADDITION, PROFITABILITY, COMPETITIVENESS, JOB CREATION, EXPORT DEVELOPMENT, AND CONTRIBUTION TO NATIONAL ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine sardine industry stands at the crossroads of fisheries, agriculture, food manufacturing, and coastal economic growth. It nourishes millions of Filipinos and supports the livelihoods of fisherfolk, workers, manufacturers, processors, transporters, distributors, tfaders, and a vibrant spectrum of enterprises, from micro to large-scale. At the heart of the industry lies the City of Zamboanga, celebrated as the “Sardines Capital of the Philippines.” Here, a thriving hub of sardine-related activities pulses with energy, from fishing and fish landing to warehousing, processing, canning, packaging, transportation, and distribution. Across Zamboanga’s coastal barangays, communities are woven into the fabric of the sardine industry. These neighborhoods host and support a network of facilities for storage, warehousing, canning, processing, packaging, logistics, and more. The sardine industry is aot just a fisheries pursuit, but a dynamic coastal industrial ecosystem that generates jobs and economic vitality throughout the city and neighboring areas. depend solely on increasing the quantity of sardines harvested or processed. The Philippines must move toward a science-driven, innoyation- led, higher-value sardine economy. The fundamental principle of this measure is straightforward: we must harness precise science and bold innovation to unlock greater economic value from every sustainably sourced sardine. By embracing scientific research, accurate stock assessments, cutting-edge fisheries technology, smarter post-harvest handling, modern processing, automation, artificial intelligence, energy-saving manufacturing, innovative packaging, creative product development, by-product utilization, digital traceability, and sharper market intelligence, the industry can boost productivity while trimming waste and unnecessary costs. These advancements translate directly into economic gains. When science and innovation empower enterprises to create more value from the same or fewer resources, profit margins rise. These stronger, more sustainable margins unlock new opportunities to reinvest in machinery, research, workforce training, business growth, new products, and untapped markets. Innovation increases productivity and value addition. Higher productivity and value addition improve profitability. Higher profitability encourages reinvestment and expansion. Expansion creates more jobs. Greater production of higher-value goods expands domestic economic activity and exports. Increased domestic economic activity and exports contribute to Philippine GDP growth. This measure sees science and innovation not just as research costs, but as powerful tools for job creation, investment growth, enterprise profitability, export expansion, and a stronger national economy. The proposed Support for Sardine Science and Innovation Program will offer a unified framework to realize these goals. It will champion research and development, fisheries s¢ience, technology transfer, modernized processing, sustainable packaging, energy efficiency, high-value product creation, digitalization, workforce training, export growth, and the commercialization of new ideas. Particular emphasis shall be placed on value addition. Instead of relying primarily on increasing fishing volume, the industry shall be encouraged to generate greater economié value from sustainably harvested resources through improved processing, premium products, innovative packaging, better quality, new food products, sardine-based ingredients, utilization of by-products, and access to higher-value markets. This strategy empowers Philippine enterprises to compete not just on price and volume, but on quality, technology, innovation, sustainability, reliability, and true value. The measure also honors the vital role of Zamboanga City. Its thriving sardine industry, coastal communities, processing plants, canneries, warehouses, packaging operations, skilled workforce, and allied enterprises form a solid foundation for building a national Sardine Science and Innovation Center. By boosting Zamboanga’s capacity for research, technology, processing innovation, skills training, export promotion, and investment, the city can shine as a model for science-driven fisheries industrialization, inspiring and supporting other sardine-producing regions acr@ss the Philippines. At its core, sustainability remains essential. Scientific innovation should never be a license for overexploiting marine resources. Instead, science must guide the nation in setting sustainable fishing levels, then harness technology, productivity, efficiency, and value addition to maximize economic returns within those boundaries. The long-term profitability of the sardine industry depends upon the continued availability of healthy sardine stocks and productive marine ecosystems. The proposed legislation aims to build an economic model where sustainability and profitability go hand in hand, each strengthening the other. With better science, the country gains a clearer understanding of its resources. With innovation, it processes them more efficiently. With value addition, it earns more from sustainable production. With higher profits, enterprises grow and create jobs. With rising exports and economic activity, the industry makes a stronger mark on Philippine GDP. It is to generate greater economic value, more jobs, stronger Filipino enterprises, inéreased investments, expanded exports, and a deeper contribution to the Philippine economy, all while safeguarding sardine resources for generations to come. Passing this measure will lay the groundwork to transform the Philippine sardine ; into a science-based, innovation-driven powerhouse that is globally competitive, creates jobs, and drives economic growth. label: HB 11592
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING SUPPORT FOR SPANNER, RED FROG, OR CURACHA CRAB SCIENCE AND INNOVATION, PROMOTING ITS SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, COMPETITIVENESS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Curacha, scientifically identified as Ranina ranina (Linnaeus, 1758), is internationally referred to as the spanner crab or red frog crab and locally as Curacha or Kuracha. This species, belonging to the family Raninidae, is recognized as an important edible and commercially valuable crab. Philippine scientific and fisheries literature identify the species as particularly abundant and economically significant in the coastal waters of southwestern Mindanao, including Zamboanga and the Sulu area. Curacha represents more than a seafood delicacy; it is a vital marine resource that supports the livelihoods of fisherfolk and coastal communities and contributes to the food cultufe and culinary identity of Zamboanga and neighboring areas. Scientific studies have documented its economic significance and the presence of both domestic and international markets for the species. Ranina ranina has a broad Indo-Pacific distribution and is commercially harvested in several countries. The species is particularly recognized in international seafood markets, including those in Australia and East Asia. Large specimens command significant value in live seafood markets, demonstrating the commercial potential of the species when supported by effective fisheries management, production systems, quality standards, and market infrastructure. The primary challenge for the Philippines is not solely to increase the volume of Curacha harvested from the sea. Rather, it is to develop the science and technology necessary to sustainably provide a stable, adequate, high-quality, and traceable supply of Curacha while safeguarding the resource that supports coastal communities. Science and innovation form the foundation for achieving this objective. Research on reproductive biology, population dynamics, genetics, nutrition, disease management, habitat, hatchery production, nursery systems, aquaculture, stock enhancement, responsible harvésting, post-harvest handling, processing, and value addition can enable the country to transition from reliance on unpredictable wild harvests to a more sustainable and knowledge-based Curacha industry. Studies on the reproductive biology of Ranina ranina in southwestern Mindana@ have already generated important scientific information regarding reproductive activity, egg-bearing females, maturity, and fecundity. These findings demonstrate that a robust and sustained scientific program can provide the information required for responsible management and the future development of production technologies. This proposed measure establishes the National Curacha Science and Innovation Program, designating the Department of Science and Technology as the lead agency. It also provides for Centers for Excellence, a Curacha Innovation Fund, technology transfer and extension sefvices, market development, and an inter-agency mechanism. The proposed Curacha Innovation Fund will support research institutions, universities, fisherfolk organizations, cooperatives, entrepreneurs, startups, processors, and other qualified stakeholders in developing technologies to enhanee the sustainability and competitiveness of the Curacha industry. The proposed Centers for Excellence, particularly in Zamboanga City, Sulu, and other strategic locations, will serve as research and innovation hubs where scientists, fisherfolk, industry, and government collaborate to develop practical solutions. These centers will build upon existing scientific capacity in Western Mindanao and the Sulu area, where research on Ranina ranina has already been conducted. The measure also recognizes that production alone is insufficient. The country must consistently deliver safe, high-quality, properly handled, traceable, and competitively priced products to both domestic and international consumers. Therefore, market development, branding, product development, food safety, export readiness, cold-chain infrastructure, and international market compliance are integral components of the proposed program. The ultimate objective is to establish a sustainable Curacha value chain, encompassing scientific research, resource management, production, harvesting, post-harvest handling, processing, technology transfer, market development, and exportation. This comprehensive approach aims to benefit fisherfolk, coastal communities, researchers, entrepreneurs, consumers, and the Philippine economy. Investing in science and innovation today will help ensure that Curacha remains an abundant and sustainable resource in the future. More importantly, the country can develop the capacity to adequately and sustainably produce Curacha for a growing domestic and international market, transforming a treasured seafood resource of Zamboanga and Sulu into a competitive Philippine marine product while safeguarding the ecosystems and communities that support it. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Technical education and skills development are essential to building a productive, adaptable, and competitive workforce. Through relevant and accessible technical-vogational education and training, Filipino workers and jobseekers can acquire competencies that improve their employability, productivity, livelihood opportunities, and capacity for entrepreneurship. Republic Act No. 7796, otherwise known as the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994,” established the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) and mandated it to develop and implement technical education and skills development programs responsive to the requirements of the Philippine economy and the labor market. The Zamboanga City Special Economic Zone and Freeport, or ZAMBOECOZONE, was established pursuant to Republic Act No. 7903, otherwise known as the “Zamboanga City Special Economic Zone Act of 1995.” The law established the Zamboanga City Special Economic Zone Authority to manage and operate the economic zone and envisioned the ZAMBOECOZONE as an agro-industrial, commercial, financial, investment, and tourist center and free port capable of attracting investments, generating employment, and promoting the economic and social development of Zamboanga City and surrounding areas. As the ZAMBOECOZONE continues to grow, demand for a workforce equipped with the right skills to support its thriving enterprises also grows. To meet the needs of industries, investors, and employers within the Freeport, technical-vocational education and skills training must align closely with real-world manpower requirements. Establishing a TESDA training facility within the heart of the ZAMBOECOZONE brings skills development directly to the doorsteps of workers, jobseekers, businesses, and local communities. This proposed measure paves the way for the Zamboanga City TESDA Training Center to take root within the ZAMBOECOZONE, forging a strong and lasting connection Between TESDA’s mission and the Freeport’s economic ambitions. The Center will become a hub for technical-vocational education, offering training, competency assessment, reskilling, upskilling, retraining, entrepreneurship support, and services designed to empower the local workforée. Placing the Center within the ZAMBOECOZONE is a strategic move that allows TESDA to collaborate closely with enterprises and industry leaders to pinpoint the exact skills and qualifications employers seek. The Center can open doors to apprenticeships, enterprise-based training, work-based learning, industry immersion, trainer development, employment referrals, and other partnerships that help bridge the gap between training and real employment. The proposed legislation also considers the existing cooperation between TESDA and the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority. In September 2026, the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority reported establishing a TESDA Provincial Training Center within its First Industrial Park in Sitio San Ramon, Barangay Talisayan. The facility is located in the Left Wing, Lower Ground Floor of the ZAMBOECOZONE Administration Building, while the Authority continues to complete its establishment. The Authority also reported that a 25-year Deed of Usufruct signed with TESDA on May 9, 2024 covers an 8,805.326-square-meter lot within the First Industrial Park for the development of a Provincial Training Center. Instead of creating a separate facility, the measure aims to institutionalize, expand, and sustain the TESDA training center within the ZAMBOECOZONE. By integrating existing agreements, facilities, personnel, programs, and resources, the Center can maximize the impact and efficiency of government efforts. Seetors of manufacturing, industrial operations, construction, welding and metal fabrication, electri¢al and electronics technology, automotive servicing, logistics, information and communications technology, food processing, agriculture and agribusiness, fisheries-related activities, tourism and hospitality, culinary services, renewable energy, machine operation and maintenance, and other occupations identified by TESDA and industry stakeholders as in demand. The Center will open doors for workers and jobseekers eager to learn new skills or enhance their current abilities. Beneficiaries may include the unemployed, underemployed, out-o “school youth, persons with disabilities, returning overseas Filipino workers, displaced workers, those employed within the ZAMBOECOZONE, and other eligible individuals. With TESDA’s scholarship and financial assistance programs, qualified trainees can access the support they need, depending on program guidelines and available funding. The measure preserves the respective mandates of TESDA and the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority. TESDA shall retain administrative and technical supervision over the Center, ineluding its training programs, competency standards, personnel, assessment and certification eons and operational policies. Consistent with Republic Act No. 7903, the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority shall coordinate appropriately and may make available land, facilities, utilities, infrastructure support, security, and other assistance necessary for the Center's operation. The arrangement is intended to create institutional cooperation without transferring TESDA's statutory functions to the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority. The legislation also calls on TESDA and the ZAMBOECOZONE Authority to establish systems to monitor and evaluate the Center’s progress. These efforts will help guarantee that public resources are invested in training programs that truly build relevant skills and open doors to meaningful jobs, livelihoods, and business opportunities. label: HB 11594
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE ZAMBOANGA CULTURAL CENTER FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, PROVIDING FOR ITS FUNCTIONS, GOVERNANCE, PROGRAMS AND SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines thrives with a vibrant tapestry of Indigenous Cultural Communities and Peoples, whose unique traditions, languages, wisdom, arts, histories, and institutions form the very heart of the nation's cultural heritage. The Constitution recognizes the rights of Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples within the framework of national unity and development. Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997, further recognizes and protects the rights of Indigenous Peoples to preserve and develop their cultures, traditions, and institutions and created the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples as the primary government agency responsible for protecting and promoting their rights and well-being. EeLibrary+1 Zamboanga City stands out as a beacon of cultural significance, home to a rich mgsaic of Indigenous Peoples and communities whose heritage shapes the vibrant identity of both the city and Western Mindanao. Recognizing this need, the City Government of Zamboanga acted in 2020 by emacting Ordinance No. 547, which established the Zamboanga Cultural Complex for Indigenous Peoples and other major cultures, with dedicated funding. This commitment was further strengthened with the passage of Ordinance No. 661 in 2024. This proposed measure aims to secure national government support and establish a lasting institutional foundation for a dedicated cultural center in Zamboanga City. The proposed Zamboanga Cultural Center for Indigenous Peoples shall serve as a venue for cultural education, exhibitions, research, documentation, preservation, performances, traditional arts, conimunity activities, and intergenerational transmission of indigenous knowledge systems and practi¢es. The Center shall not replace existing cultural institutions. Instead, it shall complement the programs of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts, the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, the National Museum of the Philippines, the National Library of the Philippines, the National Archives of the Philippines, and the City Government of Zamboanga. More importantly, the proposed Center shall ensure that Indigenous Peoples themselves have a meaningful role in determining how their cultures are documented, presented, taught, preserved, and transmitted. This is consistent with the principles of cultural integrity, self- determination, and participation embodied in Republic Act No. 8371. The creation of the Center will offer Zamboanga City and Western Mindanao a |asting public institution devoted to Indigenous cultural heritage, opening doors to education, research, cultural expression, community engagement, and mindful cultural tourism. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11595
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to upgrade the Batangas Provincial Medical Center into a Tertiary Level III General Hospital under the control, supervision, and management of the Department of Health. The proposed upgrade will enable the hospital to better respond to the medical needs of Batangueños and lessen the need for patients to seek higher-level care in hospitals located farther from their communities. A strong public healthcare system depends on hospitals that are capable of meeting the actual needs of the communities they serve. As demand for medical services increases, local health institutions must also be strengthened so that patients can receive appropriate and timely care without having to travel far from their homes. Improving hospital capacity is therefore an important step toward making quality healthcare more accessible, especially for families who rely heavily on public medical facilities. For years the Batangas Provincial Medical Center in the Municipality of Tuy has served as an important healthcare facility for residents of the municipality and nearby communities in Batangas. The continuing growth in demand for medical care further emphasizes the need for the institution to expand its comprehensive and specialized services. Strengthening the functions of this hospital will contribute to a more accessible and responsive healthcare system in the Province of Batangas and help ensure that patients receive appropriate care when they need it most. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Ryan S. label: HB 11596
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6552, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “REALTY INSTALLMENT BUYER ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act (R.A) No. 6552, otherwise known as the “Realty Installment Buyer Act”, was enacted to protect buyers of real property on installment from onerous and oppressive conditions. Through the years, as real estate transactions and modes of payment have evolved, there is a need to further strengthen these safeguards and ensure that buyers are adequately protected from inequitable contractual practices. This bill seeks to strengthen the rights of buyers availing installment schemes by providing clearer rules on grace periods and cancellation of contracts, allowing restructuring or renegotiation in cases of financial difficulty, regulating penalties and additional interest on delayed payments, and ensuring the timely transfer and registration of ownership upon full payment. It likewise recognizes modern means of communication to ensure that buyers are properly informed before cancellation may take effect. These amendments seek to provide greater fairness, transparency, and certainty in real estate installment transactions, while maintaining reasonable protections for both buyers and sellers. In view of the foregoing, which is a counterpart measure of Senate Bill 2504, is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 11598
title: AN ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill proposes the creation of an additional Regional Trial Court (RTC) branch to be stationed in the City of Carmona, with jurisdiction over the City of Carmona and the Municipality of General Mariano Alvarez (GMA). The historic progress of Carmona, following its cityhood, together with the continued development of GMA, has led to an anticipated rise in civil, criminal, and commercial litigation. To meet these growing demands and to ensure that justice remains accessible and efficient for the people of these rapidly advancing communities, the establishment of a new Regional Trial Court in Carmona is both timely and relevant. The creation of a new RTC branch is a necessary measure to strengthen the administration of justice in the area. By establishing a court dedicated to these communities, this measure will ease the load of existing dockets and help maintain the prompt disposition of cases. This is not merely an administrative adjustment but a substantive fulfillment of the constitutional mandate for the speedy disposition of cases under Article III, Section 16 of the Constitution. It gives life to the judiciary's core duty to resolve legal controversies promptly and ensures that the right to speedy justice becomes an accessible reality for every Carmonense and resident of GMA. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. ROY M. label: HB 11599
title: AN ACT PROMOTING EMPLOYMENT IN THE PROVINCES BY GRANTING A TAX CREDIT TO DOMESTIC AND FOREIGN ENTERPRISES THAT HIRE RESIDENTS OUTSIDE THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution affirms that the state shall promote full employment, afford full protection to labor and to promote equality of employment opportunities for all, and ordains that all regions of the country shall be given optimum opportunity to develop. Notwithstanding these constitutional mandates, economic activity remains heavily concentrated in the capital. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority, the NCR accounted for 31.2 percent of the national economy in 2024. This is despite of the fact that based on the 2020 Census of Population and Housing conducted by the same agency, the NCR is home to only 12.37 percent of the Philippine population. As a consequence, workers from the provinces are constrained to leave their homes and families in order to secure gainful employment. Existing fiscal incentives do not sufficiently address this disparity. According to the Fiscal Incentives Review Board, the incentives under the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 11534 or the CREATE Act and Republic Act No. 12066 or the CREATE MORE Act, including the additional deduction of fifty percent (50%) on labor expense, are available only to registered business enterprises. No corresponding incentive is extended to the ordinary employer that establishes operations in the provinces and employs the residents thereof. The present measure seeks to fill this gap by attaching the incentive to the employment itself. The proposed measure is patterned after two (2) foreign models. The first is the Work Opportunity Tax Credit or WOTC under Section 51 of the United States Internal Revenue Code. According to the United States Internal Revenue Service, the WOTC, enacted in 1996, allows an employer to claim, as a credit against federal income tax, forty percent (40%) of up to US$6,000 of the first- year wages paid to a newly hired individual belonging to a targeted group, among them the residents of designated empowerment zones and rural renewal counties. From the WOTC, this bill adopts the form of the incentive, namely, a tax credit computed on the wages of a newly hired employee and granted by reason of the place of residence of such employee. The second is the Jobs Growth Incentive or JGI of Singapore. According to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, which administered the program, the government co-funded up to twenty- 1 five percent (25%) of the first S$5,000 of the gross monthly wages of every new local hire for twelve (12) months, and up to fifty percent (50%) in the case of mature workers, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders, on the condition that the local workforce of the employer had increased over its baseline. From the JGI, this bill adopts its safeguards, to wit: that the incentive be granted only for employment that is genuinely new, and that a higher rate be accorded to workers who face greater difficulty in securing employment. Accordingly, the proposed measure grants the employer a credit against income tax equivalent to twenty-five percent (25%) of the first-year wages of every resident of the provinces hired for work in the provinces, and forty percent (40%) in the case of priority hires, such as workers aged forty (40) years and above, persons with disabilities, and members of households covered by the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program. In order to protect government revenues, the credit shall be allowed only for employment in excess of the existing workforce of the employer, and only after the employee has rendered at least six (6) months of service. It bears stressing that both models were instituted as temporary measures. As stated by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, the JGI covered new hires from September 2020 to March 2023 only. According to the United States Department of Labor, the WOTC is authorized until 31 December 2025, and as reported by CPA Practice Advisor in January 2026, a measure for its further extension has been filed in both chambers of the United States Congress. Consistent therewith, the credit herein proposed shall apply only to hiring made within five (5) years from the effectivity of the Act, after which Congress shall review its results. The creation of employment in the provinces will keep Filipino families together and retain wages within the local economy. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 11600
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE HUMAN SETTLEMENTS ADJUDICATION COMMISSION, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTIONS 13, 14, 16, 17, 18 AND 19 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11201, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SETTLEMENTS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Human Settlements Adjudication Commission (HSAC) plays a vital role in protecting the rights and interests of homebuyers, homeowners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders in the housing and real estate sector. As the principal adjudicatory body for disputes involving subdivision and condominium developments, homeowners associations, and related housing matters, the effective and timely exercise of its jurisdiction is essential to ensuring accessible and meaningful remedies for the public. Republic Act No. 11201, otherwise known as the "Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development Act," established the HSAC and defined its powers, jurisdiction, and organizational structure. However, the increasing complexity and volume of housing and real estate disputes necessitate further strengthening of the Commission's institutional and adjudicatory framework. This measure seeks to enhance the HSAC's organizational structure, personnel complement, jurisdiction, adjudicatory mechanisms, and enforcement powers to enable it to discharge its mandate more efficiently and effectively. It likewise strengthens the Commission's legal, administrative, technical, and operational support through additional personnel and appropriate organizational units. label: HB 11603
title: AN ACT PROVIDING A HEALTH CARE PROGRAM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE A public school cannot deliver quality education without teachers who are physically and mentally capable of performing their duties. Teachers do more than teach in the classroom. They also monitor student progress, provide feedback, prepare reports, participate in school activities, and respond to the different needs of their learners. Public school teachers therefore require a dependable health-care arrangement that complements existing government benefits. Access to a Healthcare Maintenance Organization can help teachers obtain preventive, rehabilitative, and other necessary medical services while reducing delays and personal expenses. Moreover, an HMO incentive has higher benefit limits, consultations, hospital coverage for pre-existing conditions, and more access to accredited hospitals nationwide. This bill seeks to establish a health-care program for all public school teachers under the Department of Education. It directs the Department to procure, through competitive bidding, a contract with a duly recognized Healthcare Maintenance Organization accepted by hospitals throughout the country. The bill further provides that the amount necessary for its implementation shall be included in the General Appropriations Act for the year following its approval. By protecting the health of teachers, the State also protects the continuity and quality of public education. ATTY. MIRO S. title: AN ACT PENALIZING ACTS OF ROAD RAGE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE There has been an alarming surge in road rage incidents across the country in recent years. Reports of motorists engaging in hostile behavior, including shouting, cursing, using foul or degrading language, issuing threats or engaging in intimidation, have become all too common. In many instances, road rage has escalated into physical assaults or attempts to inflict harm. Some cases have even resulted in serious injuries or fatalities due to the use of firearms and other weapons. The increasing frequency and severity of road rage incidents demand decisive government intervention. At present, there is a glaring lack of specific legislation that categorically defines and penalizes road rage as a distinct and punishable offense. This legislative gap leaves road users vulnerable to the hostile and often violent actions of aggressive drivers. This proposed bill seeks to define and penalize acts of road rage to safeguard all road users from harassment, intimidation, physical harm, or loss of life. Beyond punitive measures, this bill also emphasizes the importance of prevention and education. It mandates the implementation of programs that promote responsible road behavior and foster a culture of respect and accountability among motorists. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11605
title: AN ACT DEFINING DEFENSIVE DRIVING AND PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF MOTOR VEHICLE DRIVERS INVOLVED IN A ROAD CRASH
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In the Philippines, there is a recurring and problematic practice where drivers involved in vehicular incidents—even those who are clearly not at fault—are subjected to automatic arrest and detention. This often happens because law enforcement perceives any involvement in an accident, particularly one resulting in injury or death, as presumptive proof of criminal negligence. This "automatic detention" culture places an unfair burden on individuals who were merely reacting to sudden and unavoidable hazards. This bill seeks to address this by: 1. Institutionalizing "Defensive Driving": Recognizing that a driver’s attempt to avoid harm through reasonable maneuvers (such as braking, swerving, or stopping) is a crucial factual consideration. 2. Protecting Due Process: Mandating that law enforcement and prosecutors evaluate the full circumstances of an incident—including dashcam footage, witness accounts, and environmental factors—before deciding to detain a driver or proceed with criminal charges. 3. Ending Automatic Detention: Ensuring that if the evidence suggests the driver acted defensively and reasonably, the driver is not subject to unnecessary detention while the case is being investigated. It encourages the use of regular preliminary investigations for complex cases rather than immediate inquests that keep drivers in custody. This measure does not provide immunity. If further investigation proves that the driver was, in fact, negligent, they will remain liable under the law. However, it ensures that the Philippine justice system distinguishes between those who cause accidents through true recklessness and those who are victims of unfortunate circumstances. By requiring an objective, evidence-based approach to vehicular incidents, this bill upholds the constitutional right to due process and prevents the waste of public resources on the detention of innocent citizens. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11606
title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE PERIOD OF VALIDITY OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES OF MOTOR VEHICLES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 14 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “LAND TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC CODE”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motor vehicle drivers and riders are essential to Philippine society. They transport people, goods, and services, helping support the country’s economy and everyday life. This includes jeepney and bus drivers, delivery riders, and private vehicle owners. However, they face many challenges, such as rising fuel prices, expensive vehicle maintenance, and the costs and inconvenience of complying with government requirements. One major burden is the yearly renewal of motor vehicle registration. For those who depend on their vehicles for their livelihood, this process takes time, money, and effort. This bill proposes extending the validity of motor vehicle registrations. The measure would provide financial and practical relief to millions of Filipino drivers and riders by reducing the need for annual renewal. It recognizes their important contribution and seeks to lessen the difficulties they face. Furthermore, recognizing that technological advances have made newer vehicles more reliable, consequently, extended registration periods may be warranted beyond the three-year exemption. The extension would also benefit the government. It would reduce the workload of the Land Transportation Office (LTO) and allow its personnel to focus on other important services and improvements. It could also help reduce long lines and overcrowding in LTO offices and make the registration process more efficient. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11607
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ASSISTANCE TO INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS SITUATION (AICS) PROGRAM UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT (DSWD), PROVIDING FUNDING, ESTABLISHING OVERSIGHT AND IMPLEMENTING RULES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many individuals and families affected by sudden, severe, or unforeseen events—medical emergencies, accidents, displacement, death in the family, trafficking, and other crisis situations—often require immediate financial, material, medical, psychological, and transport support to stabilize their circumstances. While AICS interventions have been provided on an ad hoc basis, the absence of a statutory mandate limits predictable funding, standardization of eligibility and benefits, and coordinated delivery across national and local levels. Institutionalizing AICS will ensure timely, standardized, and accountable assistance to those in urgent need, with priority given to the poor, vulnerable, marginalized, and disadvantaged The AICS program is hereby institutionalized to provide immediate and timely assistance to individuals and families assessed to be experiencing crises or extreme difficult situations needing financial or material support. The AICS programs serves as a stop-gap measure to support the recovery of individuals and families suffering from unexpected life events or crises. In addition to the usual assistance under the program, there is a need to expand the scope of assistance to include Fuel Subsidy allowance. A targeted fuel subsidy for motorists facing crisis situations is warranted to ensure immediate mobility and access to essential services during emergencies. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11608
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF MOTORCYCLE TAXI RIDERS AND DELIVERY RIDERS, PROMOTING THEIR RIGHTS AND WELFARE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motorcycle delivery riders and drivers play a vital role in the Philippines’ transportation, delivery, and digital-economy sectors. Through their daily work, they transport passengers and deliver food, medicine, documents, and other essential goods to individuals, households, and businesses throughout the country. Their services help sustain commerce, support local businesses, improve access to essential products, and provide convenience to the public. Despite their important contribution, many riders and drivers continue to face difficult and uncertain working conditions. They may also be exposed to road accidents, harassment, discrimination, and other forms of abuse. Many also lack sufficient access to social protection, health and accident insurance, emergency assistance, and other employment-related benefits. These conditions demonstrate the need for a clear legal framework that recognizes the essential role of motorcycle delivery riders and drivers and protects them from exploitation and unfair treatment. This bill seeks to establish their rights in fulfillment of the State’s constitutional duty to protect labor, promote social justice, and ensure decent and humane working conditions. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11609
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY ALLOCATION OF PARKING SPACES FOR MOTORCYCLES AND A GRACE PERIOD FOR DELIVERY SERVICE VEHICLES IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ESTABLISHMENTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motorcycle use in the Philippines has increased because it provides affordable and convenient transportation. At the same time, delivery riders have become essential in bringing goods, food, and services to the public. However, many motorcycle riders and delivery personnel have difficulty finding proper parking. Some establishments do not have designated motorcycle parking, while others charge fees even when delivery riders stay only briefly to pick up or deliver orders. This proposed law requires commercial, office, and public establishments to provide designated parking spaces for motorcycles. It also grants delivery riders a reasonable grace period during which they may wait or complete their transactions without being charged parking fees or penalties. This measure promotes fair access to parking facilities and recognizes the important role of delivery riders in the Philippine economy. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11610
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11235, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MOTORCYCLE CRIME PREVENTION ACT”, AS AMENDED, TO INCLUDE ALL MOTOR VEHICLES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11235, or the Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act, has been an important tool in addressing crimes involving motorcycles. The original law, enacted in 2019, sought to reduce the occurrence of crimes like robbery, drive-by shootings, and other violent acts committed by individuals using motorcycles as a means of escape or a weapon. On May 2025, Republic Act No. 12209 was enacted which seeks to rationalize the safety features and penalties relative to the operation of motorcycles. However, while the law successfully targets crimes committed by motorcycle riders, there has been a noticeable gap in the law's application to other types of motor vehicles which have also been increasingly used for criminal activities, such as cars, vans, and other forms of transport. In light of this, it is imperative that the law be expanded to cover not only motorcycles but also other types of motor vehicles, thereby ensuring a more comprehensive approach to crime prevention and improving public safety across all forms of transportation. The Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Act aims to amend Republic Act No. 11235 by expanding its coverage to include all motor vehicles, not just motorcycles. This bill seeks to strengthen the existing legal framework to ensure that law enforcement agencies have the tools necessary to track and prevent the use of motor vehicles in the commission of crimes. The inclusion of motor vehicles within the law’s coverage will provide a more comprehensive solution to crimes that pose significant threats to the safety and security of all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11611
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PUBLIC TRANSPORT SAFETY MONITORING SYSTEM AND PROVIDING FOR THE USE OF SAFETY MONITORING AND EMERGENCY RESPONSNE TECHNOLOGY IN PUBLIC TRANSPORT VEHICLES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Millions of Filipinos depend on public transportation each day. Accordingly, passengers should be assured of safe travel and have timely access to assistance in the event of accidents, crimes, harassment, or other emergencies. Technology such as GPS, CCTV, dashcams and emergency alert systems can help government agencies and transport operators respond quickly to incidents and investigate complaints. However, these technologies must be part of a coordinated system rather than being installed merely as standalone devices. This bill therefore seeks to establish a Public Transport Safety Monitoring System that will allow government to monitor public transport vehicles, receive emergency alerts, preserve relevant recordings, and coordinate with law enforcement and emergency responders. The measure also protects the privacy of passengers, drivers and operators by requiring compliance with existing data privacy laws. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11612
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INSTALLATION OF TIMERS IN TRAFFIC LIGHTS AND PEDESTRIAN LIGHTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Traffic congestion and road accidents remain significant concerns in both urban and rural areas. Motorists and pedestrians often experience uncertainty when approaching intersections because they cannot determine how much time remains before a traffic or pedestrian signal changes. This may result in sudden stops, rushed crossings, traffic violations, and avoidable accidents. The installation of countdown timers on traffic lights and pedestrian lights will provide motorists and pedestrians with clear and timely information regarding the remaining duration of each signal. By displaying the time left before a signal changes, timers can promote safer decision-making, improve compliance with traffic rules, reduce sudden movements at intersections, and contribute to the smoother flow of traffic. Through this measure, the State can promote safer roads, improve traffic management, protect pedestrians and motorists, and reduce congestion through the use of simple and effective technology. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11613
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AT LEAST ONE (1) LEVEL II HOSPITAL IN EVERY PROVINCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 15, Article II of the Constitution states that "The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them." Furthermore, it provides that the State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health and other social services available to all the people at affordable cost. The Philippines is composed of 82 provinces, each serving as an important geographic and administrative unit in the delivery of basic services. Among these essential services is healthcare, making it vital to ensure that adequate and appropriate health services are available within these geographic areas and accessible to communities across the country. However, access to hospital care remains uneven to date. While several provinces already have hospitals capable of providing Level II services, such facilities are not uniformly available throughout the country. The Department of Health has recognized this disparity, with former Health Secretary Teodoro J. Herbosa reporting that 40 of the country’s 82 provinces did not have a DOH hospital, with residents in some areas having to travel three to four hours to another city or province to access a DOH facility and government-supported medical services'. Such barrier can make it more difficult for patients to benefit from government programs such as the Zero Balance Billing policy, particularly when access to govermment hospitals require considerable travel. ! Villanueva, G. (2025, September 10). DOH says lack of hospitals, beds hinder access to zero balance billing. Philippine Daily Inquirer. This challenge is particularly significant and visible for communities outside highly urbanized cities. Patients requiring healthcare services beyond those available at primary or Level I facilities may have to travel to another province or highly urbanized city, or seek treatment from private hospitals, resulting in additional costs that can be particularly burdensome for those with limited financial means. Strengthening hospital capacity at the provincial level is therefore necessary to bring more comprehensive medical care closer to communities and reduce the geographic and financial barriers to accessing appropriate hospital services. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize the establishment of at least one (1) Level II government hospital in every province of the Philippines. Its objective is to establish a uniform national framework that ensures every province has access to enhanced and comprehensive hospital care. It likewise seeks to advance the policy of the Department of Health pursuant to the Republic Act No. 11223, or the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, whereby all provinces should have at least one Level II hospital, with the vision of establishing an equitable health system where every Filipino can access appropriate and quality healthcare where they reside. The measure further aims to upgrade, expand, modernize, or, where feasible, convert existing provincial DOH primary care facilities and Level I hospitals into Level II hospitals. By ensuring that every province has access to at least one (1) Level II government hospital, the State can strengthen the country’s healthcare system, facilitate patients’ access to government health programs such as the Zero Balance Billing policy, and advanee its constitutional mandate to make essential health services accessible and affordable to all. title: AN ACT PENALIZING SELECTIVE, DISCRETIONARY, AND DISCRIMINATORY ACTS IN THE DELIVERY OF SOCIAL PROTECTION PROGRAMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 1, Article XI of the 1987 Constitution states that “[p]ublic office is a public trust. Every government worker is expected to serve the Filipino people with utmost integrity, efficiency, and fairness. However, the persistent gap between this ideal situation and the reality on the ground is apparent. Across the country, access to social assistance, from emergency relief and medical subsidies to educational aid and cash transfers, is too often derailed by favoritism, politics, and local bias. During times of crisis, the local distribution of aid frequently devolves into a system of "palakasan." Some barangays are selective in their distribution of relief goods, requiring the presentation of voter’s IDs or prioritizing their friends and relatives.’ Deserving, low-income families get left off the master lists simply because they lack the right connections or fall on the wrong side of local political lines. Meanwhile, those with close ties to officials skip the line, turning basic public services into political favors. This bill seeks to tackle the issue of discrepancy head-on by creating clear, enforceable penalties for any government worker who uses discretion to favor, exclude, or discriminate against beneficiaries. By removing personal bias from the distribution process and enforcing strict accountability, this measure ensures that government aid finally reaches every qualified Filipino fairly, impartially, and without condition. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Keith Micah “Atty. Mike” D.L. Tan Ath District, Quezon } Department of the Interier and Local Government. (2920. label: HB 11615
title: AN ACT PROMOTING INCLUSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTIVITY GROWTH, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6971, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PRODUCTIVITY INCENTIVES ACT OF 1990
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to promote gainful employment, improve working conditions, maintain industrial peace and harmony, and promote the principle of partnership and shared responsibility between labor and management, Mandatory wage increase without corresponding increases in the productivity of the workers will only result in higher inflation rate as firms and businesses would pass on the cost of the wage increments to the cost of the product or the service being produced or provided, thus wiping out the value of wage increases almost as soon as they are mandated. The continuing oil crisis triggers a domino effect that excessively impacts the poor and low-income households that spend most of their income on immediate survival needs and live without savings to absorb sudden price hikes. By recognizing the right of labor to its just share in the fruits of production, and the right of business enterprises to reasonable returns on investments and for growth and expansion, this proposed measure aims to provide incentives to both labor and management for undertaking productivity improvement programs, as it also grants tax incentives to business enterprises that adopt the program with a special deduction from gross income equivalent to 50% of the total productivity incentives given to employees, and to business enterprises that provide training and special studies to employees. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ~~ Keith Micah “Atty. Mike” D.L.
